17.10.11.b.s: yukṣvā hi devahūtamāniti dvābhyāṃ saṃcitamagnimabhimṛśya vasvastvā rudraiḥ purastātpāntvityetairyathāliṅgaṃ saṃcitamagnimājyena prokṣati /
17.10.11.b.d: युक्ष्वा हि देवहूतमानिति द्वाभ्यां संचितमग्निमभिमृश्य वस्वस्त्वा रुद्रैः पुरस्तात्पान्त्वित्येतैर्यथालिङ्गं संचितमग्निमाज्येन प्रोक्षति ।
17.10.11.b.m: with the two verses “Harness those who best invoke the gods...”, having touched the piled Agni, he sprinkles the piled Agni with clarified butter according to the characteristic marks with [the mantras beginning with] “May the Vasus with the Rudras protect you in the east...”.

17.10.11.c.m: Facing east, in the middle with the last [mantra].

17.11.1.a.s: sahasrasya pramā asīti sahasreṇa hiraṇyaśalkairūrdhvastiṣṭhanpratidiśamagniṃ prokṣati dvābhyāṃdvābhyāṃ śatābhyām /
17.11.1.a.d: सहस्रस्य प्रमा असीति सहस्रेण हिरण्यशल्कैरूर्ध्वस्तिष्ठन्प्रतिदिशमग्निं प्रोक्षति द्वाभ्यांद्वाभ्यां शताभ्याम् ।
17.11.1.a.m: Standing upright, with “You are the measure of a thousand...”, he sprinkles the fire in each quarter with a thousand gold chips, two hundred [for each quarter].

17.11.1.b.m: Facing east, in the middle with the last two hundred.

17.11.2.a.s: imā me agna iṣṭakā dhenavaḥ santvitīṣṭakā debūryajamānaḥ kurute
17.11.2.a.d: इमा मे अग्न इष्टका धेनवः सन्त्वितीष्टका देबूर्यजमानः कुरुते
17.11.2.a.m: With “May these bricks, O Agni, be milch-cows to me...”, the sacrificer renders the bricks yielding.

17.11.3.a.s: aiḍikyā cityādhvaryuragnimabhimṛśya śatarudrīyaṃ juhoti jartilayavāgvā gavīdhukayavāgvā vā jartilairgavīdhukasaktubhiḥ kusayasarpiṣājākṣīreṇa mṛgīkṣīreṇa vārkaparṇenodaṅtiṣṭan /
17.11.3.a.d: ऐडिक्या चित्याध्वर्युरग्निमभिमृश्य शतरुद्रीयं जुहोति जर्तिलयवाग्वा गवीधुकयवाग्वा वा जर्तिलैर्गवीधुकसक्तुभिः कुसयसर्पिषाजाक्षीरेण मृगीक्षीरेण वार्कपर्णेनोदङ्तिष्टन् ।
17.11.3.a.m: The adhvaryu, having touched the fire with the Aiḍikī layer, standing facing north, offers the Śatarudrīya with gruel of wild sesame or with gruel of gavīdhukā grains, or with wild sesame, gavīdhukā groats, butter from a kusaya vessel, goat's milk, or the milk of a wild doe, using an arka leaf,

17.11.3.b.s: uttarasya pakṣasyottarāparasyāṃ sraktyāṃ vikarṇyāṃ svayamātṛṇāyāmanuparicāraṃ vā
17.11.3.b.d: उत्तरस्य पक्षस्योत्तरापरस्यां स्रक्त्यां विकर्ण्यां स्वयमातृणायामनुपरिचारं वा
17.11.3.b.m: on the north-western corner of the northern wing, on the Vikarṇī, on the Svayamātṛṇā, or moving all around.

17.11.4.a.s: namaste rudra manyava ityetānanuvākāṃstraidhaṃ vibhajyāpi vā prathamādupakramya namastakṣabhya iti jānudaghne dhārayamāṇo rathakārebhyaśca va ityupakramya namaḥ svāyudhāyeti nābhidaghne śeṣeṇa prāgavatānebhya āsyadaghne hutvā sahasrāṇi sahasraśa iti daśāvatānānhutvānvārohāñjuhoti
17.11.4.a.d: नमस्ते रुद्र मन्यव इत्येताननुवाकांस्त्रैधं विभज्यापि वा प्रथमादुपक्रम्य नमस्तक्षभ्य इति जानुदघ्ने धारयमाणो रथकारेभ्यश्च व इत्युपक्रम्य नमः स्वायुधायेति नाभिदघ्ने शेषेण प्रागवतानेभ्य आस्यदघ्ने हुत्वा सहस्राणि सहस्रश इति दशावतानान्हुत्वान्वारोहाञ्जुहोति
17.11.4.a.m: Having divided these anuvākas beginning with “Homage, Rudra, to your anger...” into three parts, or alternatively beginning from the first, holding [the ladle] at knee height up to “Homage to the carpenters...”, and beginning with “And to your chariot-makers...” at navel height up to “Homage to him of good weapons...”, and having offered the remainder up to the descending formulas at mouth height, and having offered the ten descending formulas beginning with “Thousands in thousands...”, he offers the ascending formulas.

17.11.5.a.s: namo rudrebhyo ye pṛthivyāmiti jānudaghne dhārayamāṇo namo rudrebhyo ye 'ntarikṣa iti nābhidaghne namo rudrebhyo ye divītyāsyadaghne hutvaitāneva yajamānaṃ vācayitvaitāneva viparītānpratyavarohānhutvā saṃcare paśūnāmarkaparṇamudasyati
17.11.5.a.d: नमो रुद्रेभ्यो ये पृथिव्यामिति जानुदघ्ने धारयमाणो नमो रुद्रेभ्यो ये ऽन्तरिक्ष इति नाभिदघ्ने नमो रुद्रेभ्यो ये दिवीत्यास्यदघ्ने हुत्वैतानेव यजमानं वाचयित्वैतानेव विपरीतान्प्रत्यवरोहान्हुत्वा संचरे पशूनामर्कपर्णमुदस्यति
17.11.5.a.m: Holding [the leaf] at knee height with “Homage to the Rudras who are on earth...”, at navel height with “Homage to the Rudras who are in the atmosphere...”, having offered at mouth height with “Homage to the Rudras who are in heaven...”, having made the sacrificer recite these very [formulas], and having offered these same formulas in reverse order as descending offerings, he throws up the arka leaf in the cattle path.

17.11.6.a.s: yaṃ dviṣyāttasya saṃcare yasya rudraḥ prajāṃ paśūnvābhimanyetodaṅ paretya rudrāñjapaṃścaredityayajñasaṃyuktaḥ kalpaḥ
17.11.6.a.d: यं द्विष्यात्तस्य संचरे यस्य रुद्रः प्रजां पशून्वाभिमन्येतोदङ् परेत्य रुद्राञ्जपंश्चरेदित्ययज्ञसंयुक्तः कल्पः
17.11.6.a.m: “In the path of him whom he hates; or, if Rudra should afflict someone's offspring or cattle, he should go away toward the north and wander reciting the Rudra hymns”—this is a procedure not connected with the sacrifice.

17.12.1.a.s: yo rudro agnāviti raudraṃ gāvīdhukaṃ carum
17.12.1.a.d: यो रुद्रो अग्नाविति रौद्रं गावीधुकं चरुम्
17.12.1.a.m: With “The Rudra who is in the fire...”, [he takes] a caru of gavīdhukā grains dedicated to Rudra.

17.12.2.a.s: etena yajuṣā yasyāmiṣṭakāyāṃ śatarudrīyaṃ juhoti tasyāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati
17.12.2.a.d: एतेन यजुषा यस्यामिष्टकायां शतरुद्रीयं जुहोति तस्यां प्रतिष्ठापयति
17.12.2.a.m: With this yajus formula he establishes it on the brick upon which he offers the Śatarudrīya.

17.12.3.a.s: tisṛdhanvamayācitaṃ yajamāno brāhmaṇāya dattvā yatte rudra puro dhanurityetairyathāliṅgamupatiṣṭhate
17.12.3.a.d: तिसृधन्वमयाचितं यजमानो ब्राह्मणाय दत्त्वा यत्ते रुद्र पुरो धनुरित्येतैर्यथालिङ्गमुपतिष्ठते
17.12.3.a.m: Having given an unasked-for bow with three arrows to a brahmin, the sacrificer reverences [the fire] according to their characteristic marks with [the mantras beginning with] “The bow that is yours in the east, Rudra...”.

17.12.4.a.m: Taking a water jar, the adhvaryu circumambulates the fire three times from left to right, pouring water around with “Firmness, vigor...”.

17.12.5.a.s: nidhāya kumbhamaśmāste kṣudamuṃ te śugṛcchatu yaṃ dviṣma iti trirapariṣiñcanpratiparyeti
17.12.5.a.d: निधाय कुम्भमश्मास्ते क्षुदमुं ते शुगृच्छतु यं द्विष्म इति त्रिरपरिषिञ्चन्प्रतिपर्येति
17.12.5.a.m: Having set down the pot, he walks around counter-clockwise three times without pouring, with the mantra: 'The stone is your hunger; let that sorrow reach him whom we hate.'

17.12.6.a.s: yadyabhicaredidamahamamuṣyāmuṣyāyaṇasyāyuḥ prakṣiṇomīti dakṣiṇasyāmuttarasyāṃ vā sraktyāṃ kumbhaṃ prakṣiṇuyāt
17.12.6.a.d: यद्यभिचरेदिदमहममुष्यामुष्यायणस्यायुः प्रक्षिणोमीति दक्षिणस्यामुत्तरस्यां वा स्रक्त्यां कुम्भं प्रक्षिणुयात्
17.12.6.a.m: If he would perform sorcery, he should shatter the pot on the southern or the northern corner, saying: 'Here I cut off the life of so-and-so, son of so-and-so.'

17.12.7.a.s: avakā vetasaśākhāṃ maṇḍūkaṃ ca dīrghavaṃśe prabadhya samudrasya tvāvākayeti saptabhiraṣṭābhirvāgniṃ vikarṣati
17.12.7.a.d: अवका वेतसशाखां मण्डूकं च दीर्घवंशे प्रबध्य समुद्रस्य त्वावाकयेति सप्तभिरष्टाभिर्वाग्निं विकर्षति
17.12.7.a.m: Having tied an avakā plant, a reed-branch, and a frog to a long bamboo, he drags [them] over the fire with seven or eight [mantras], beginning with: 'Thee, of the ocean, with the avakā...'

17.12.8.a.m: Having indeed extinguished [the burning parts] while dragging, having stopped all the vital breaths of the frog, he tosses [them] onto the rubbish heap.

17.12.9.a.m: Whomever he might hate, he should touch him with these.

17.12.10.c.m: The two wings, with the Bṛhat and the Rathaṃtara;

17.12.10.e.m: On the right hip, with the Vāravantīya;

17.12.10.f.m: On the left hip, with the Vāmadevya.

17.12.11.a.m: Near the wing, he sings the verse-less Sāman of Prajāpati.

17.12.12.a.m: The hotṛ recites after [him] with the saṃcita-ukthya [hymn], beginning with: 'Father Mātariśvan...'

17.12.13.a.m: If the hotṛ is unwilling, the adhvaryu causes the sacrificer to recite the milkings of the chant and the recitation.

17.12.14.a.m: At the mantra: 'Thou art the praised of the praised,' he dismantles the Pravargya.

17.13.1.a.s: juhvāṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā svayaṃ kṛṇvāna iti dve
17.13.1.a.d: जुह्वां पञ्चगृहीतं गृहीत्वा स्वयं कृण्वान इति द्वे
17.13.1.a.m: Having taken five portions [of clarified butter] in the juhū spoon, [he offers] two [oblations] with the verse: 'Making oneself...'

17.13.2.a.m: 'Granting dispensation to the descendant of Manu, beholding the straight path,

17.13.2.b.s: ajuṣanta maruto yajñametaṃ vṛṣṭiṃ devānāmamṛtaṃ svarvidam //
17.13.2.b.d: अजुषन्त मरुतो यज्ञमेतं वृष्टिं देवानाममृतं स्वर्विदम् ॥
17.13.2.b.m: The Maruts enjoyed this sacrifice, the rain of the gods, the immortal, sun-finding.'

17.13.2.c.m: 'Turning round in the midst of the world, transforming the creatures, begetting various forms,

17.13.2.d.s: saṃvatsaraḥ parameṣṭhī dhṛtavrato yajñaṃ naḥ pātu rajasaḥ purastāt //
17.13.2.d.d: संवत्सरः परमेष्ठी धृतव्रतो यज्ञं नः पातु रजसः पुरस्तात् ॥
17.13.2.d.m: May the Year, the supreme lord of steadfast observance, protect our sacrifice before the aerial space.'

17.13.2.e.s: prajāṃ dadātu parivatasaro no dhātā dadātu sumanasyamānaḥ /
17.13.2.e.d: प्रजां ददातु परिवतसरो नो धाता ददातु सुमनस्यमानः ।
17.13.2.e.m: 'May the Parivatsara give us offspring; may the Creator, well-disposed, give [offspring]!

17.13.2.f.s: bahvīḥ sākaṃ bahudhā viśvarūpā ekavratā māmabhisaṃviśantviti pañcānvārohānhutvāparaṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā kārṣṇī upānahāvupamuñcate /
17.13.2.f.d: बह्वीः साकं बहुधा विश्वरूपा एकव्रता मामभिसंविशन्त्विति पञ्चान्वारोहान्हुत्वापरं पञ्चगृहीतं गृहीत्वा कार्ष्णी उपानहावुपमुञ्चते ।
17.13.2.f.m: May many, manifold, all-formed [creatures] of one vow enter together into me'—having offered these five Anvāroha oblations and taken another five portions [of clarified butter], he puts on two shoes made of black-antelope skin,

17.13.5.b.m: With the two [verses]: 'Homage to thy heat, to thy flame...,' he mounts the fire-altar;

17.13.5.c.m: The sacrificer [mounts] with: 'I have stepped onto the earth...'

17.13.6.a.s: nṛṣade vaḍiti pañcabhiruttaravedivadagniṃ svayamātṛṇāṃ vā vyāghārya ye devā devānāmiti dvābhyāmanuparicāraṃ dadhnā madhumiśreṇa darbhagrumuṣṭināgniṃ vyavokṣya kūrmapṛṣantaṃ kṛtvā prāṇadā apānadā iti pratyavaruhyāgnistigmeneti dvābhyāmagnaye 'nīkavata ekāmāhutiṃ hutvā
17.13.6.a.d: नृषदे वडिति पञ्चभिरुत्तरवेदिवदग्निं स्वयमातृणां वा व्याघार्य ये देवा देवानामिति द्वाभ्यामनुपरिचारं दध्ना मधुमिश्रेण दर्भग्रुमुष्टिनाग्निं व्यवोक्ष्य कूर्मपृषन्तं कृत्वा प्राणदा अपानदा इति प्रत्यवरुह्याग्निस्तिग्मेनेति द्वाभ्यामग्नये ऽनीकवत एकामाहुतिं हुत्वा
17.13.6.a.m: Having sprinkled the fire-altar or the naturally perforated stone as in the case of the high altar with five [formulas] beginning with: 'To the dweller among men, vaṭ!,' having sprinkled the fire-altar with curds mixed with honey by means of a handful of darbha roots following the verses: 'Which gods of the gods...,' making it like a tortoise-back, having stepped down with: 'Givers of breath, givers of downward breath...,' and having offered one oblation to Agni Anīkavat with the two [verses] beginning with: 'Agni with sharp...'

17.14.1.a.m: Having filled the sruc ladle with sixteen portions [of clarified butter], he offers the Vaiśvakarmaṇa oblations:

17.14.2.b.s: cakṣuṣaḥ pitā manasā hi dhīra iti nānāsūktābhyāṃ dve āhutī
17.14.2.b.d: चक्षुषः पिता मनसा हि धीर इति नानासूक्ताभ्यां द्वे आहुती
17.14.2.b.m: 'Father of the eye, for wise in mind...'—thus two oblations from the two different hymns.

17.14.3.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta ciraṃ pāpmano nirmucyetetyekaikaṃ tasyetyuktam
17.14.3.a.d: यं कामयेत चिरं पाप्मनो निर्मुच्येतेत्येकैकं तस्येत्युक्तम्
17.14.3.a.m: For whomever he desires that he should be freed from evil for a long time, [he should offer] each one singly for him—thus it is declared.

17.14.4.a.s: yadyenamudake bhīrvidnedudakāñjalimādāya samudrāya vayunāyetyapsu juhuyādityayajñasaṃyuktaḥ kalpaḥ
17.14.4.a.d: यद्येनमुदके भीर्विद्नेदुदकाञ्जलिमादाय समुद्राय वयुनायेत्यप्सु जुहुयादित्ययज्ञसंयुक्तः कल्पः
17.14.4.a.m: If fear of water should seize him, he should take a hollowed handful of water and offer it into water with: 'To the ocean, to the path...'—this is a procedure not connected with the sacrifice.

17.14.5.a.s: udenamuttarāṃ nayetyaudumbarīḥ samidho ghṛtoṣitāstisṛbhistisra ādhāya paśubandhavadagniṃ praṇayati
17.14.5.a.d: उदेनमुत्तरां नयेत्यौदुम्बरीः समिधो घृतोषितास्तिसृभिस्तिस्र आधाय पशुबन्धवदग्निं प्रणयति
17.14.5.a.m: With the three verses beginning with: 'Lead him higher...,' having placed three udumbara kindling-sticks soaked in ghee, he leads the fire forward as in the animal sacrifice.

17.14.6.a.s: udu tvā viśve devā ityagnimudyamya pañca diśo daivīriti pañcabhirharatyāgnīdhrāt
17.14.6.a.d: उदु त्वा विश्वे देवा इत्यग्निमुद्यम्य पञ्च दिशो दैवीरिति पञ्चभिर्हरत्याग्नीध्रात्
17.14.6.a.m: Having lifted up the fire with: 'Up, indeed, thee, all the gods...,' he carries it from the Āgnīdhra with five [verses], beginning with: 'Five divine quarters...'

17.14.7.a.s: āśuḥ śiśāna iti dakṣiṇato brahmā daśarcenānveti /
17.14.7.a.d: आशुः शिशान इति दक्षिणतो ब्रह्मा दशर्चेनान्वेति ।
17.14.7.a.m: The brahman follows along on the south with the ten-verse hymn: 'Swift, sharpening...';

17.14.7.b.m: Or the maitrāvaruṇa, or the pratiprasthātṛ.

17.14.8.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta rāṣṭraṃ syāditi tametena saṃnahyānviyāt /
17.14.8.a.d: यं कामयेत राष्ट्रं स्यादिति तमेतेन संनह्यान्वियात् ।
17.14.8.a.m: Whomever he would desire that he should possess a kingdom, he should follow along having equipped him with this [hymn];

17.14.8.b.m: An oblation should be made when a battle is joined;

17.14.8.c.m: The firewood consists of reed or Madhuka wood—this is a procedure not connected with the sacrifice.

17.14.9.a.s: vimāna eṣa divo madhya āsta iti dvābhyāmāgnīdhre 'śmānaṃ nidhāyendraṃ viśvā avīvṛdhanniti catasṛbhirāpucchādgatvā
17.14.9.a.d: विमान एष दिवो मध्य आस्त इति द्वाभ्यामाग्नीध्रे ऽश्मानं निधायेन्द्रं विश्वा अवीवृधन्निति चतसृभिरापुच्छाद्गत्वा
17.14.9.a.m: Having placed a stone in the Āgnīdhra with the two [verses]: 'This measure sits in the middle of heaven...,' and having walked as far as the tail with the four [verses]: 'All have magnified Indra...'

17.15.1.a.s: prācīmanu pradiśamiti pañcabhiragnimadhiruhya naktoṣāsāgne sahasarākṣeti dvābhyāṃ saṃhitābhyāṃ dadhnaḥ pūrṇāmaudumbarīṃ svayamātṛṇāyāṃ juhoti
17.15.1.a.d: प्राचीमनु प्रदिशमिति पञ्चभिरग्निमधिरुह्य नक्तोषासाग्ने सहसराक्षेति द्वाभ्यां संहिताभ्यां दध्नः पूर्णामौदुम्बरीं स्वयमातृणायां जुहोति
17.15.1.a.m: Having mounted the fire-altar with the five [formulas]: 'Along the eastern direction...,' he offers an udumbara [ladle] full of curd onto the naturally perforated stone with the two connected [verses]: 'Night and Dawn...,' 'O Agni of a thousand eyes...'

17.15.2.a.m: With 'Night and Dawn...,' he offers with milk from a black cow with a white calf.

17.15.3.a.m: Some say he sprinkles it with milk.

17.15.4.a.s: ūrṇāvantaṃ prathamaḥ sīda yonimiti hoturabhijñāya paśukānsaṃbhārānnyupya suparṇo 'si garutmāniti tisṛbhiḥ svayamātṛṇāyāmagniṃ pratiṣṭhāpya preddho agne dīdihi puro na ityaudumbarīṃ samidhamādadhāti
17.15.4.a.d: ऊर्णावन्तं प्रथमः सीद योनिमिति होतुरभिज्ञाय पशुकान्संभारान्न्युप्य सुपर्णो ऽसि गरुत्मानिति तिसृभिः स्वयमातृणायामग्निं प्रतिष्ठाप्य प्रेद्धो अग्ने दीदिहि पुरो न इत्यौदुम्बरीं समिधमादधाति
17.15.4.a.m: Recognizing the hotṛ's [verse]: 'Sit thou first in the wool-bearing womb...,' having scattered the materials for [obtaining] cattle, and having established the fire upon the naturally perforated stone with the three [verses]: 'Thou art the winged eagle...,' he places an udumbara kindling-stick with: 'Kindled, O Agni, shine before us...'

17.15.5.a.s: vidhema te parame janmannagna iti vaikaṅkatīm
17.15.5.a.d: विधेम ते परमे जन्मन्नग्न इति वैकङ्कतीम्
17.15.5.a.m: A vaikaṅkata [kindling-stick] with: 'Let us honor thee in the highest birth, O Agni...'

17.15.6.a.m: A śamī [kindling-stick] with: 'That wondrous [glory] of Savitṛ the desirable...'

17.15.7.b.s: agne tamadyāśvamiti dve āhutī hutvā dvādaśagṛhītena srucaṃ pūrayitvā sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvā iti saptavatyā pūrṇāhutiṃ juhoti
17.15.7.b.d: अग्ने तमद्याश्वमिति द्वे आहुती हुत्वा द्वादशगृहीतेन स्रुचं पूरयित्वा सप्त ते अग्ने समिधः सप्त जिह्वा इति सप्तवत्या पूर्णाहुतिं जुहोति
17.15.7.b.m: Having offered two oblations with: 'O Agni, this horse today...,' and having filled the sruc ladle with twelve portions [of clarified butter], he offers the full oblation with the verse containing 'seven': 'Seven are thy kindling-sticks, O Agni, seven thy tongues...'

17.15.8.a.s: tāṃ juhvadiha so 'stviti digbhyo 'gniṃ manasā dhyāyati
17.15.8.a.d: तां जुह्वदिह सो ऽस्त्विति दिग्भ्यो ऽग्निं मनसा ध्यायति
17.15.8.a.m: Offering it, he meditates mentally on the fire from the quarters with: 'May he be here!'

17.16.1.a.m: Having performed [the rites] up to the sprinkling of the altar ground, he commences the ritual procedure of the Vaiśvānara [sacrifice].

17.16.2.a.s: vedaṃ kṛtvāgniṃ paristīrya pāṇiprakṣālanādi karma pratipadyate
17.16.2.a.d: वेदं कृत्वाग्निं परिस्तीर्य पाणिप्रक्षालनादि कर्म प्रतिपद्यते
17.16.2.a.m: Having made the sacred broom and strewn around the fire, he proceeds to the action beginning with the washing of the hands.

17.16.3.a.m: The preparation of the utensils is according to requirement.

17.16.4.a.s: nirvapaṇakāle vaiśvānaraṃ dvādaśakapālaṃ nirupya sapta mārutānsaptakapālānnirvapati
17.16.4.a.d: निर्वपणकाले वैश्वानरं द्वादशकपालं निरुप्य सप्त मारुतान्सप्तकपालान्निर्वपति
17.16.4.a.m: At the time of apportioning [the oblations], having apportioned [the oblation] on twelve potsherds for Vaiśvānara, he apportions seven [cakes] on seven potsherds for the Maruts.

17.16.6.a.m: At the time of issuing calls, he issues the call omitting the wife.

17.16.7.a.m: At the time of taking the clarified butter, he takes [it] into the dhruvā spoon only.

17.16.8.a.m: He proceeds to the rite beginning with the consecration of the sprinkling-waters.

17.16.9.a.s: staraṇakāle 'pareṇāgniṃ barhiḥ stīrtvā dhruvāṃ sruvaṃ ca sādayati
17.16.9.a.d: स्तरणकाले ऽपरेणाग्निं बर्हिः स्तीर्त्वा ध्रुवां स्रुवं च सादयति
17.16.9.a.m: At the time of strewing [the sacrificial grass], having strewn the sacrificial grass to the west of the fire, he sets down the dhruvā-ladle and the sruva-spoon.

17.16.10.a.m: He adapts the formula: "May these two sit down..."

17.16.11.a.m: Having put down the grass broom, he proceeds to the sāmidhenī verses.

17.16.12.a.s: na saṃpreṣyati na saṃmārṣṭi na prayājānyajati
17.16.12.a.d: न संप्रेष्यति न संमार्ष्टि न प्रयाजान्यजति
17.16.12.a.m: He does not issue a ritual call, he does not wipe [the spoons], and he does not offer the fore-offerings.

17.16.13.a.s: ājyabhāgābhyāṃ pracarya juhvāmupastīrya kṛtsnaṃ vaiśvānaramavadāya dvirabhighāryoccairvaiśvānarasyāśrāvayati
17.16.13.a.d: आज्यभागाभ्यां प्रचर्य जुह्वामुपस्तीर्य कृत्स्नं वैश्वानरमवदाय द्विरभिघार्योच्चैर्वैश्वानरस्याश्रावयति
17.16.13.a.m: Having performed the two butter-portion offerings, having spread [ghee] as an underlayer in the juhū-spoon, having cut off the whole Vaiśvānara [cake], and having basted it twice, he calls loudly for the Vaiśvānara [offering].

17.16.14.a.m: He offers silently the offerings to the Maruts as entirely offered.

17.16.15.a.s: īdṛṅ cānyādṛṅ ceti saptabhirgaṇairāsīno hastena gaṇena gaṇamanudrutya mārutāñjuhoti
17.16.15.a.d: ईदृङ् चान्यादृङ् चेति सप्तभिर्गणैरासीनो हस्तेन गणेन गणमनुद्रुत्य मारुताञ्जुहोति
17.16.15.a.m: Seated, reciting group by group [the formula beginning] "Such and otherwise-such..." with the seven groups, he offers the Marut offerings by hand.

17.16.16.a.m: Some say: he offers group by group with the forest-recitation in the middle.

17.16.17.a.m: Some say: he encloses the Vaiśvānara all around with the Marut offerings.

17.16.18.a.s: svatavāṃśca praghāsī ca sāṃtapanaśca gṛhamedhī ca krīḍī ca sākī corjiṣī cetyeṣa ṣaṣṭha āmnātaḥ
17.16.18.a.d: स्वतवांश्च प्रघासी च सांतपनश्च गृहमेधी च क्रीडी च साकी चोर्जिषी चेत्येष षष्ठ आम्नातः
17.16.18.a.m: "And the powerful one, and the consumer, and the scorcher, and the householder, and the playful one, and the mighty one, and the vigorous one"—this is taught as the sixth [group].

17.16.19.a.m: He attaches "and the measured, and the commensurate" everywhere.

17.17.1.a.s: yadi kāmayeta kṣatraṃ viśa ojīyaḥ syāditi grāme 'nuvākyasya trīṇi catvāri vā padānyanudrutyāraṇye'nuvākyamanudrutya grāme'nuvākyasya śeṣeṇa juhuyāt
17.17.1.a.d: यदि कामयेत क्षत्रं विश ओजीयः स्यादिति ग्रामे ऽनुवाक्यस्य त्रीणि चत्वारि वा पदान्यनुद्रुत्यारण्येऽनुवाक्यमनुद्रुत्य ग्रामेऽनुवाक्यस्य शेषेण जुहुयात्
17.17.1.a.m: If he should desire: "May the nobility be stronger than the commonalty," he should, after reciting three or four words of the village-recitation, recite the forest-recitation, and offer with the remainder of the village-recitation.

17.17.2.a.m: Thus, having offered with three groups from the beginning, he should offer with the forest-recitation.

17.17.3.a.m: As with the former [groups], so with the three subsequent groups.

17.17.4.a.s: yadi kāmayeta viṭ kṣatrādojīyasī syāditi yathāsamāmnātamāditastribhirgaṇairhutvāraṇye'nuvākyasya ṣaṭsu padāntarāleṣu ṣaḍgaṇānopyāraṇye'nuvākyena juhuyāt
17.17.4.a.d: यदि कामयेत विट् क्षत्रादोजीयसी स्यादिति यथासमाम्नातमादितस्त्रिभिर्गणैर्हुत्वारण्येऽनुवाक्यस्य षट्सु पदान्तरालेषु षड्गणानोप्यारण्येऽनुवाक्येन जुहुयात्
17.17.4.a.m: If he should desire: "May the commonalty be stronger than the nobility," having offered as handed down with three groups from the beginning, having inserted six groups into the intervals of the six words of the forest-recitation, he should offer with the forest-recitation.

17.17.5.a.m: As with the former [groups], so with the three subsequent groups.

17.17.6.a.m: He does not issue a ritual call, he does not wipe [the spoons], and he does not offer the after-offerings.

17.17.7.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta kṣatreṇāsya kṣatraṃ hanyātprasvādāyatanāccyaveteti tasyāraṇye'nuvākyenāgniṣṭhaṃ rathavāhanaṃ vā vyaṅgayedityayajñasaṃyuktaḥ kalpaḥ
17.17.7.a.d: यं कामयेत क्षत्रेणास्य क्षत्रं हन्यात्प्रस्वादायतनाच्च्यवेतेति तस्यारण्येऽनुवाक्येनाग्निष्ठं रथवाहनं वा व्यङ्गयेदित्ययज्ञसंयुक्तः कल्पः
17.17.7.a.m: "If he should desire of someone: 'May he smite his nobility with nobility, may he fall from his own domain,' he should cripple his chariot-chassis standing at the fire with the forest-recitation"—this is a procedure unconnected with the sacrifice.

17.17.8.a.s: agnāviṣṇū sajoṣaseti caturgṛhītaṃ hutvaudubarīṃ srucaṃ vyāyāmamātrīṃ mṛdā pradigdhāṃ paścādāsecanavatīṃ ghṛtasya pūrayitvā vājaśca me prasavaśca ma iti saṃtatāṃ vasordhārāṃ juhotyā mantrasamāpanāt
17.17.8.a.d: अग्नाविष्णू सजोषसेति चतुर्गृहीतं हुत्वौदुबरीं स्रुचं व्यायाममात्रीं मृदा प्रदिग्धां पश्चादासेचनवतीं घृतस्य पूरयित्वा वाजश्च मे प्रसवश्च म इति संततां वसोर्धारां जुहोत्या मन्त्रसमापनात्
17.17.8.a.m: Having offered a fourfold portion of ghee with "O Agni and Viṣṇu, being in harmony...", having filled an udumbara ladle of a vyāyāma's length, smeared with clay, and having a pouring-lip at the back, with clarified butter, he offers the continuous Shower of Wealth with "And my food, and my production..." up to the conclusion of the formula.

17.17.9.a.s: yaṃ kāmayeta prāṇānasyānnādyaṃ vi chindyāmiti vigrāhaṃ tasyetyuktam
17.17.9.a.d: यं कामयेत प्राणानस्यान्नाद्यं वि छिन्द्यामिति विग्राहं तस्येत्युक्तम्
17.17.9.a.m: It has been said: "If he should desire concerning someone: 'May I cut off his vital breaths and food,' [he should offer it] discontinuously for him."

17.17.10.a.m: In whatever ghee remains, having cooked the brahmaudana porridge, he should feed four brahmins.

17.17.10.b.m: Or, having cooked porridge measuring four śarāvas, he should feed [them] with that [ghee] as condiment.

17.17.11.a.m: To those who have eaten, he should give four milch cows.

17.17.12.a.m: [There are] three [verses beginning] "From the ocean the wave..."

17.18.1.a.s: tridhā hitaṃ paṇibhirguhyamānaṃ gavi devāso ghṛtamanvavindan /
17.18.1.a.d: त्रिधा हितं पणिभिर्गुह्यमानं गवि देवासो घृतमन्वविन्दन् ।
17.18.1.a.m:
"Deposited threefold, hidden by the Paṇis, the gods discovered the clarified butter in the cow;
Indra generated one [part], Sūrya one, [and] from Vena they fashioned one by their own inherent power.

17.18.1.b.s: indra ekaṃ sūrya ekaṃ jajāna venādekaṃ svadhayā niṣṭatakṣuḥ //
17.18.1.b.d: इन्द्र एकं सूर्य एकं जजान वेनादेकं स्वधया निष्टतक्षुः ॥
17.18.1.b.m:
These flow from the ocean of the heart, having a hundred enclosures, unseen by the deceiver;
I gaze upon the streams of clarified butter; in their midst is the golden reed.

17.18.1.c.m:
Like rivers the streams flow well together, being purified within the heart by the mind;
These waves of clarified butter flow forth like fleeing deer escaping the hunter.

17.18.1.d.s: ghṛtasya dhārā abhi cākaśīmi hiraṇyayo vetaso madhya āsām //
17.18.1.d.d: घृतस्य धारा अभि चाकशीमि हिरण्ययो वेतसो मध्य आसाम् ॥
17.18.1.d.m:
Swift as the wind, they fly along like rapid [currents] on the course of a river, the streaming [drops];
Like a red racehorse bursting through the course, the stream of clarified butter swells with waves.

17.18.1.e.s: samyak sravanti sarito na dhenā antarhṛdā manasā pūyamānāḥ /
17.18.1.e.d: सम्यक् स्रवन्ति सरितो न धेना अन्तर्हृदा मनसा पूयमानाः ।
17.18.1.e.m:
Like beautiful young women smiling as they go to an assembly, they flow towards the fire;
Streams of clarified butter reach the kindling-sticks; enjoying them, Jātavedas rejoices.

17.18.1.f.s: ete arṣantyūrmayo ghṛtasya mṛgā iva kṣipaṇorīṣamāṇāḥ //
17.18.1.f.d: एते अर्षन्त्यूर्मयो घृतस्य मृगा इव क्षिपणोरीषमाणाः ॥
17.18.1.f.m:
Like maidens adorning themselves to go to the wedding, I gaze upon [them];
Where soma is pressed, where the sacrifice is, thither flow the streams of clarified butter.

17.18.1.g.s: sindhoriva prādhvane śūghanāso vātapramiyaḥ patayanti yajvāḥ /
17.18.1.g.d: सिन्धोरिव प्राध्वने शूघनासो वातप्रमियः पतयन्ति यज्वाः ।
17.18.1.g.m:
Flow toward the sweet praise, toward the race for cattle; place blessed treasures in us;
Lead this sacrifice of ours to the gods; the streams of clarified butter flow sweetly."

17.18.1.h.s: ghṛtasya dhārā aruṣo na vājī kāṣṭhā bhindannūrmibhiḥ pinvamānaḥ //
17.18.1.h.d: घृतस्य धारा अरुषो न वाजी काष्ठा भिन्दन्नूर्मिभिः पिन्वमानः ॥
17.18.1.h.m:
With "Thy whole realm rests upon the world, within the ocean, in the heart, within life;
Brought into being in the gathering of the host of waters, may we attain that sweet wave of thine," the sacrificer recites over [the offering] when it has been offered, or while it is being offered.

17.18.1.i.s: abhi pravanta samaneva yoṣāḥ kalpāṇyaḥ smayamānāso agnim /
17.18.1.i.d: अभि प्रवन्त समनेव योषाः कल्पाण्यः स्मयमानासो अग्निम् ।

17.18.1.j.s: ghṛtasya dhārāḥ samidho nasanta tā juṣāṇo haryati jātavedāḥ //
17.18.1.j.d: घृतस्य धाराः समिधो नसन्त ता जुषाणो हर्यति जातवेदाः ॥
17.18.1.j.m: [There are] seven cultivated plants and seven wild plants.

17.18.1.k.s: kanyā iva vahatumetavā u añjyañjānā abhi cākaśīmi /
17.18.1.k.d: कन्या इव वहतुमेतवा उ अञ्ज्यञ्जाना अभि चाकशीमि ।
17.18.1.k.m: Having liquefied the food substances separately, having offered the cultivated [grains] with the udumbara spoon with "The production of strength has produced this...", he offers the wild ones.

17.18.1.l.s: yatra somaḥ sūyate yatra yajño ghṛtasya dhārā abhi tatpavante //
17.18.1.l.d: यत्र सोमः सूयते यत्र यज्ञो घृतस्य धारा अभि तत्पवन्ते ॥
17.18.1.l.m: Having offered each time, he pours the residue into a vessel.

17.18.1.m.s: abhyarṣata suṣṭutiṃ gavyamājimasmāsu bhadrā draviṇāni dhatta /
17.18.1.m.d: अभ्यर्षत सुष्टुतिं गव्यमाजिमस्मासु भद्रा द्रविणानि धत्त ।
17.18.1.m.m: Having set up an udumbara chair near the south side [of the fire], having spread on it a black antelope skin with its neck to the east and the hairy side turned up, he consecrates with the residues the sacrificer seated upon it and holding onto the fire from behind.

17.18.1.n.s: imaṃ yajñaṃ nayata devatā no ghṛtasya dhārā madhumatpavante //
17.18.1.n.d: इमं यज्ञं नयत देवता नो घृतस्य धारा मधुमत्पवन्ते ॥
17.18.1.n.m: A kṣatriya [is consecrated] on a tiger skin.

17.18.1.o.s: dhāmante viśvaṃ bhuvanamadhi śritamantaḥ samudre hṛdyantarāyuṣi /
17.18.1.o.d: धामन्ते विश्वं भुवनमधि श्रितमन्तः समुद्रे हृद्यन्तरायुषि ।
17.18.1.o.m: A vaiśya on a goat skin.

17.18.1.p.s: apāmanīke samithe ya ābhṛtastamaśyāma madhumantaṃ ta ūrmimiti hutāṃ hūyamānāṃ vā yajamāno 'numantrayate
17.18.1.p.d: अपामनीके समिथे य आभृतस्तमश्याम मधुमन्तं त ऊर्मिमिति हुतां हूयमानां वा यजमानो ऽनुमन्त्रयते
17.18.1.p.m: One who desires spiritual luster [is consecrated] on a black antelope skin.

17.19.1.a.m: Some say: on a goat skin for one desiring prosperity.

17.19.2.a.m: Having recited "At the impulse of the god...", [he consecrates] a brahmin with "I sprinkle thee for sovereignty with Agni;"

17.19.3.a.s: pṛthagannāni dravīkṛtyaudumbareṇa sruveṇa vājasyemaṃ prasavaḥ suṣuva iti grāmyā hutvāraṇyā juhoti
17.19.3.a.d: पृथगन्नानि द्रवीकृत्यौदुम्बरेण स्रुवेण वाजस्येमं प्रसवः सुषुव इति ग्राम्या हुत्वारण्या जुहोति

17.19.5.a.s: dakṣiṇaṃ praty apipakṣam audumbarīm āsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpya tasyāṃ kṛṣṇājinaṃ prācīnagrīvam uttaralomāstīrya tasminn āsīnaṃ yajamānam agnimanvārabdhaṃ saṃpātair abhiṣiñcati
17.19.5.a.d: दक्षिणं प्रत्य् अपिपक्षम् औदुम्बरीम् आसन्दीं प्रतिष्ठाप्य तस्यां कृष्णाजिनं प्राचीनग्रीवम् उत्तरलोमास्तीर्य तस्मिन्न् आसीनं यजमानम् अग्निमन्वारब्धं संपातैर् अभिषिञ्चति
17.19.5.a.m: Some teach the reversal of the formulas for the kṣatriya and the vaiśya.

17.19.6.a.m: Standing facing west, having consecrated [the sacrificer] who is seated facing east from his head, he causes [the liquid] to trickle down towards his face.

17.19.6.c.m: Having offered with the milk of a black cow having a white calf with "Night and dawn...", he offers the twelve realm-sustaining oblations with six rounds.

17.19.7.a.m: Having recited the round formula "Conquering by truth, abiding in truth...", he offers the first offering with "Svāhā to him!";

17.19.8.a.s: devasya tvety anudrutyāgnes tvā sāmrājyenābhiṣiñcāmīti brāhmaṇam /
17.19.8.a.d: देवस्य त्वेत्य् अनुद्रुत्याग्नेस् त्वा साम्राज्येनाभिषिञ्चामीति ब्राह्मणम् ।

17.19.8.c.m: The [formula] "O lord of the world..." is the seventh of the rounds, and the thirteenth of the oblations.

17.19.9.a.m: Some teach the reversal of the mantras for a Rājanya and a Vaiśya.

17.19.10.a.s: prāṅmukham āsīnaṃ pratyaṅmukhas tiṣṭhañ śīrṣato 'bhiṣicyā mukhād anvavasrāvayati
17.19.10.a.d: प्राङ्मुखम् आसीनं प्रत्यङ्मुखस् तिष्ठञ् शीर्षतो ऽभिषिच्या मुखाद् अन्ववस्रावयति
17.19.10.a.m: Standing facing west, having sprinkled [him] from the head as he sits facing east, he makes it flow down along the face.

17.19.11.a.m: On this point they say: It must surely be offered; for one who has pressed [soma] does not descend before anyone.

17.19.12.a.s: naktoṣāseti kṛṣṇāyai śvetavatsāyai payasā hutvā ṣaḍbhiḥ paryāyairdvādaśa rāṣṭrabhṛto juhoti
17.19.12.a.d: नक्तोषासेति कृष्णायै श्वेतवत्सायै पयसा हुत्वा षड्भिः पर्यायैर्द्वादश राष्ट्रभृतो जुहोति
17.19.12.a.m: Having offered with the milk of a black [cow] having a white calf with the verse "Night and Dawn", he offers the twelve Rāṣṭrabhṛt [oblations] in six rounds.

17.20.1.a.s: ṛtāṣāḍṛtadhāmeti paryāyam anudrutya tasmai svāheti prathamām āhutiṃ juhoti /
17.20.1.a.d: ऋताषाडृतधामेति पर्यायम् अनुद्रुत्य तस्मै स्वाहेति प्रथमाम् आहुतिं जुहोति ।
17.20.1.a.m: Having recited the round, "Conquering by truth, whose abode is truth...", he offers the first oblation with: "To him svāhā!"

17.20.1.b.m: With "To them svāhā!" [he offers] the second.

17.20.2.a.m: In this manner he divides the other rounds.

17.20.3.a.s: bhuvanasya pata iti paryāyāṇāṃ saptamyāhutīnāṃ trayodaśī
17.20.3.a.d: भुवनस्य पत इति पर्यायाणां सप्तम्याहुतीनां त्रयोदशी
17.20.3.a.m: [The formula] "O lord of the world..." is the seventh of the rounds, the thirteenth of the oblations.

17.20.5.a.m: With 'Lord of the world...', he offers five oblations on the front part of the chariot,

17.20.6.a.m: Some say he offers upon the head of the chariot while it is being held over the āhavanīya.

17.20.7.a.m: Having offered over it, lifting it up, they carry it to the dwelling of the adhvaryu.

17.20.9.a.m: He gives them, together with the chariot, to the adhvaryu.

17.20.11.a.d: समुद्रो ऽसि नभस्वानित्यञ्जलिना त्रीणि वातनामानि जुहोति
17.20.11.a.m: With 'You are the ocean, rich in mist...', he offers with hollowed hands the three names of the wind;

17.20.12.a.m: for 'there is no cutting [of a portion] of this,' it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

17.20.13.a.m: Some say: he offers to the wind with a fold of black-antelope skin.

17.20.14.a.s: agna udadhe yā ta iṣauryuvā nāmeti pañcājyāhutīrhutvā samīcī namāsi prācī digiti dadhnā madhumiśreṇa ṣaṭ sarpāhutīranuparicāram
17.20.14.a.d: अग्न उदधे या त इषौर्युवा नामेति पञ्चाज्याहुतीर्हुत्वा समीची नमासि प्राची दिगिति दध्ना मधुमिश्रेण षट् सर्पाहुतीरनुपरिचारम्
17.20.14.a.m: Having offered five butter oblations with 'O Agni, the receptacle of water, what arrow of yours...', 'The youth by name...', [he offers] walking around six serpent oblations with curds mixed with honey with 'You are the concordant ones, the eastern direction...';

17.20.15.a.m: six great oblations with 'Weapons by name are you...', just as the serpent oblations;

17.20.16.a.m: five Arka oblations with 'Light, O Gharma, svāhā!';

17.20.17.a.s: yāste agne sūrye ruca iti tisro rucaḥ
17.20.17.a.d: यास्ते अग्ने सूर्ये रुच इति तिस्रो रुचः
17.20.17.a.m: three splendour [oblations] with 'What splendours of yours, O Agni, are in the sun...'.

17.20.18.a.m: He commences the soma ritual beginning with the strewing of the altar ground.

17.20.19.a.m: Having performed whatever comes before the heaping of the dhiṣṇya hearths,

17.21.1.a.m: he piles the dhiṣṇyas with bricks mantra by mantra with the anuvāka, 'May my splendour, O Agni, be present in invocations...'.

17.21.2.a.m: On the āgnīdhrīya hearth he lays down [bricks] having a stone as the ninth;

17.21.3.a.m: twelve, sixteen, twenty-one, or twenty-four on the hotṛ's hearth;

17.21.4.a.m: 'eight each on the other dhiṣṇyas,' it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

17.21.5.a.m: The dhiṣṇyas are square or circular.

17.21.6.a.m: As many bricks as belong to them, so many pebbles are enclosed around [them].

17.21.7.a.s: tava śriye vyajihīta parvato gavāṃ gotramudasṛjo yadaṅgiraḥ /
17.21.7.a.d: तव श्रिये व्यजिहीत पर्वतो गवां गोत्रमुदसृजो यदङ्गिरः ।
17.21.7.a.m: 'For your glory the mountain split open, when you, O Aṅgiras, released the pen of cattle;

17.21.7.b.s: indreṇa yujā tamasā parīvṛtaṃ bṛhaspate nirapāmaubjo arṇavam //
17.21.7.b.d: इन्द्रेण युजा तमसा परीवृतं बृहस्पते निरपामौब्जो अर्णवम् ॥
17.21.7.b.m: With Indra as your ally, O Bṛhaspati, you drove out the ocean of waters that was enclosed by darkness.'

17.21.7.d.s: brāhaspatiḥ samajayadvasūni maho vrajāngomato deva eṣaḥ /
17.21.7.d.d: ब्राहस्पतिः समजयद्वसूनि महो व्रजान्गोमतो देव एषः ।
17.21.7.d.m: 'Bṛhaspati won all wealth, the great pens rich in cattle, this god;

17.21.7.e.m: Desiring to win the waters, irresistible towards the sun, Bṛhaspati slays the enemy with songs'—with these three [he places bricks] at the seat of the brahman.

17.21.8.a.s: yamo dādhāra pṛthivīṃ yamo viśvamidaṃ jagat /
17.21.8.a.d: यमो दाधार पृथिवीं यमो विश्वमिदं जगत् ।
17.21.8.a.m: 'Yama upholds the earth, Yama all this world;

17.21.8.b.m: To Yama everything has bowed down, whatever has breathed, protected by the wind.

17.21.8.c.m: As the five, as the six, as the fifteen ṛṣis,

17.21.8.d.m: He who knows Yama would tell, just as the single ṛṣi discerns.

17.21.8.e.m: Through the Trikadruka [days] he flies across the six broad spaces, the one great [domain];

17.21.8.f.s: gāyatrī triṣṭup chandāṃsi sarvā tā yama āhiteti tisro mārjālīye
17.21.8.f.d: गायत्री त्रिष्टुप् छन्दांसि सर्वा ता यम आहितेति तिस्रो मार्जालीये
17.21.8.f.m: The gāyatrī, the triṣṭubh, the metres—all those are placed in Yama'—with these three [he places bricks] on the mārjālīya.

17.22.1.a.m: 'Have mercy on us, O Rudra, and grant us delight...'

17.22.1.b.s: aśyāma te sumatiṃ devayajyayā kṣayadvīrasya tava rudra mīḍhvaḥ /
17.22.1.b.d: अश्याम ते सुमतिं देवयज्यया क्षयद्वीरस्य तव रुद्र मीढ्वः ।
17.22.1.b.m: 'May we attain your goodwill through worship of the gods, of you who rule over heroes, O bounteous Rudra;

17.22.1.c.s: sumnāyannidvaśo asmākamā carāriṣṭavīrā juhavāma te haviḥ //
17.22.1.c.d: सुम्नायन्निद्वशो अस्माकमा चरारिष्टवीरा जुहवाम ते हविः ॥
17.22.1.c.m: Favouring us, come to our wish; with uninjured heroes may we offer oblation to you.'

17.22.1.d.s: tveṣaṃ vayaṃ rudraṃ yajñasādhanaṃ vaṅkuṃ kavimavase ni hvayāmahe /
17.22.1.d.d: त्वेषं वयं रुद्रं यज्ञसाधनं वङ्कुं कविमवसे नि ह्वयामहे ।
17.22.1.d.m: 'Fierce Rudra, the accomplisher of sacrifice, the winding, the poet, we invoke downwards for help;

17.22.1.e.s: āre asmadamatiṃ heḍso asyatu sumatimidvayamasyā vṛṇīmaha iti tisraścātvāle
17.22.1.e.d: आरे अस्मदमतिं हेड्सो अस्यतु सुमतिमिद्वयमस्या वृणीमह इति तिस्रश्चात्वाले
17.22.1.e.m: Far from us may he cast away thoughtlessness, his wrath; we choose only the goodwill of him'—with these three [he places bricks] in the cātvāla trench.

17.22.2.a.s: havyaṃ prīṇīhi havyaṃ śrīṇīhi havyaṃ paca havyaṃ śrapaya havyamasi havyāya tvā havyebhyastvā havye sīdetyaṣṭau śāmitre
17.22.2.a.d: हव्यं प्रीणीहि हव्यं श्रीणीहि हव्यं पच हव्यं श्रपय हव्यमसि हव्याय त्वा हव्येभ्यस्त्वा हव्ये सीदेत्यष्टौ शामित्रे
17.22.2.a.m: With 'Please the oblation, cook the oblation, bake the oblation, boil the oblation, you are the oblation, for the oblation to you, for the oblations to you, sit down on the oblation'—with these eight [he places bricks] in the śāmitra.

17.22.3.c.m: 'With that prayer I come to you...'—with these three at the avabhṛtha.

17.22.5.a.m: Pieces that are broken, black, and spotted he throws away upon the rubbish heap.

17.22.6.a.m: Having broken the remaining ones and having performed whatever comes before measuring the sacrificial post, he erects one sacrificial post or eleven sacrificial posts.

17.22.7.a.m: Of them, the one facing the fire on the previous day;

17.22.8.a.m: Or he assigns [the animals] of the set of eleven to a single post.

17.22.9.a.s: agnīṣomīyasya paśupuroḍāśam aṣṭau devasuvāṃ havīṃṣy anunirvapati
17.22.9.a.d: अग्नीषोमीयस्य पशुपुरोडाशम् अष्टौ देवसुवां हवींष्य् अनुनिर्वपति
17.22.9.a.m: Following the animal cake of the Agni-Soma victim, he dispenses the eight oblations to the divine prompters.

17.22.10.a.m: However, the sviṣṭakṛt and the iḍā are common.

17.23.1.a.m: Before the morning recitation, touching [the fire altar] with the three [verses], 'I harness Agni...', he harnesses the fire.

17.23.2.a.s: yadyenaṃ pūrvo bhrātṛvyo 'bhīva syādaṣṭau gāyatrīḥ purastādbahiṣpavamānādupadadhyāt /
17.23.2.a.d: यद्येनं पूर्वो भ्रातृव्यो ऽभीव स्यादष्टौ गायत्रीः पुरस्ताद्बहिष्पवमानादुपदध्यात् ।
17.23.2.a.m: If a rival who is prior should overpower him, he should lay down eight gāyatrī [bricks] before the Bahiṣpavamāna chant.

17.23.2.b.m: [He places] eleven Triṣṭubh [bricks] before the midday [pressing chant],

17.23.2.c.m: twelve Jagatī [bricks] before the Ārbhava [pavamāna chant].

17.23.3.a.m: Or, if the rival is subsequent, the reverse is done:

17.23.3.b.m: they are placed after the pavamāna chants.

17.23.4.a.m: At the time of the animal [sacrifice], he dedicates the victim dedicated to Agni for the soma day;

17.23.5.a.s: dakṣiṇākāle hiraṇyapātraṃ madhoḥ pūrṇaṃ śatamānasya kṛtaṃ citraṃ dvānāmityavekṣyāśvenāvaghrāpya brahmaṇe dadāti
17.23.5.a.d: दक्षिणाकाले हिरण्यपात्रं मधोः पूर्णं शतमानस्य कृतं चित्रं द्वानामित्यवेक्ष्याश्वेनावघ्राप्य ब्रह्मणे ददाति
17.23.5.a.m: At the time of the sacrificial gifts, having looked at a gold vessel filled with honey, made of a hundred manas [in weight], with [the verse,] "A wondrous [face of the gods]...", and having made the horse sniff it, he gives it to the brahman.

17.23.6.a.m: He gives suitable sacrificial gifts to the adhvaryu.

17.23.7.a.s: yadyasyāgniṃ cinoti yajñāyajñīyasya stotra ekayāprastutaṃ bhavati
17.23.7.a.d: यद्यस्याग्निं चिनोति यज्ञायज्ञीयस्य स्तोत्र एकयाप्रस्तुतं भवति
17.23.7.a.m: If he piles the fire altar for [a sacrificer], at the Yajñāyajñīya chant [the stotra] is uncompleted by one [verse],

17.23.8.a.s: atha namaste astu mā mā hiṃsīriti dvābhyāmagnimabhimṛśyaikādaś samiṣṭayajūṃṣi juhoti
17.23.8.a.d: अथ नमस्ते अस्तु मा मा हिंसीरिति द्वाभ्यामग्निमभिमृश्यैकादश् समिष्टयजूंषि जुहोति
17.23.8.a.m: then, having touched the fire altar with the two [formulas], "Homage be to you, do not injure me...", he offers the eleven Samiṣṭayajus offerings.

17.23.9.a.s: navādhvarikāṇi hutveṣṭo yajño bhṛgubhiriti daśamaikādaśe juhoti
17.23.9.a.d: नवाध्वरिकाणि हुत्वेष्टो यज्ञो भृगुभिरिति दशमैकादशे जुहोति
17.23.9.a.m: Having offered the nine [formulas] of the normal sacrifice, he offers the tenth and eleventh with [the two formulas beginning,] "The sacrifice has been offered by the Bhṛgus...".

17.23.10.a.s: anūbandhyāvapāyāṃ hutāyāmaudumbarīṃ srucaṃ ghṛtasya pūrayitvemaṃ stanamūrjasvantaṃ dhayāpāmityagnervimokaṃ juhoti
17.23.10.a.d: अनूबन्ध्यावपायां हुतायामौदुम्बरीं स्रुचं घृतस्य पूरयित्वेमं स्तनमूर्जस्वन्तं धयापामित्यग्नेर्विमोकं जुहोति
17.23.10.a.m: When the omentum of the anūbandhyā cow has been offered, having filled the sruc made of udumbara wood with ghee, he offers the unyoking of the fire with [the verse,] "Suck this swelling breast of the waters...".

17.23.11.a.s: hute saktuhome yadākūtāditi daśākūtīrhutvā pratyavaruhya punarmanaḥ punarāyurāgātpunaḥ prāṇaḥ punarākūtamāgāt /
17.23.11.a.d: हुते सक्तुहोमे यदाकूतादिति दशाकूतीर्हुत्वा प्रत्यवरुह्य पुनर्मनः पुनरायुरागात्पुनः प्राणः पुनराकूतमागात् ।
17.23.11.a.m: When the barley-meal offering has been made, having offered the ten ākūti offerings with [the formulas beginning,] "From the intention...", having stepped down, [he worships the fire altar with the verse,] "Mind has returned, life has returned, breath has returned, intention has returned;

17.23.11.b.m: May Vaiśvānara, growing with his rays, dwell within as the guardian of immortality."

17.23.12.a.s: ye 'gnayaḥ purīṣyā iti prayāsyannāptibhiragniṃ yajamāna upatiṣṭhate
17.23.12.a.d: ये ऽग्नयः पुरीष्या इति प्रयास्यन्नाप्तिभिरग्निं यजमान उपतिष्ठते
17.23.12.a.m: When about to set forth, the sacrificer worships the fire with the āpti formulas: "Whichever fires are rich in loose earth...".

17.24.1.a.s: upa tvāgne divediva iti tisṛbhiranyeṣāmagnīn dṛṣṭvāgniṃ citvā sautrāmaṇyā yajeta /
17.24.1.a.d: उप त्वाग्ने दिवेदिव इति तिसृभिरन्येषामग्नीन् दृष्ट्वाग्निं चित्वा सौत्रामण्या यजेत ।
17.24.1.a.m: Having seen the fires of others, [he worships] with the three [verses,] "Towards you, O Agni, day by day...". Having piled the fire altar, he should sacrifice with the Sautrāmaṇī,

17.24.1.b.m: and with the curdled milk offering for Mitra and Varuṇa.

17.24.2.a.s: saṃvatsaraṃ na kaṃcana pratyavarohenna ca rāmāmupeyāt /
17.24.2.a.d: संवत्सरं न कंचन प्रत्यवरोहेन्न च रामामुपेयात् ।
17.24.2.a.m: For a year he should not descend [to the level of] anyone, nor should he approach a Śūdra woman,

17.24.3.a.s: yāvajjīvaṃ ca mastiṣkasya nāśnīyānna ca varṣati dhāvet
17.24.3.a.d: यावज्जीवं च मस्तिष्कस्य नाश्नीयान्न च वर्षति धावेत्
17.24.3.a.m: and for the rest of his life he should not eat brain, nor should he run when it rains;

17.24.4.a.m: if he should run, he should turn back.

17.24.5.a.m: Having piled [the fire altar] a second time, he should not approach another's wife;

17.24.5.b.m: having piled it a third time, [he should not approach] any woman,

17.24.6.a.s: agniṃ citvaitasminsaṃvatsare yo nardhnuyātsa kratumāharamāṇa ekacitīkaṃ cinvīta
17.24.6.a.d: अग्निं चित्वैतस्मिन्संवत्सरे यो नर्ध्नुयात्स क्रतुमाहरमाण एकचितीकं चिन्वीत
17.24.6.a.m: Having piled the fire altar, he who does not prosper in that year, undertaking a sacrifice, should pile an altar of one layer.

17.24.7.a.m: He should place on the high altar eight bricks with distinct formulas, beginning with: "To the ocean you...";

17.24.7.b.m: as many space-filler bricks as required, then loose earth.

17.24.8.a.s: atha yo na pratitiṣṭhetsa kratumāharamāṇa ekacitīkameva cinvīta
17.24.8.a.d: अथ यो न प्रतितिष्ठेत्स क्रतुमाहरमाण एकचितीकमेव चिन्वीत
17.24.8.a.m: Then, he who does not obtain a firm support, undertaking a sacrifice, should pile an altar of only one layer.

17.24.9.a.m: He should place on the high altar five bricks with distinct formulas: "Uniting, and wise...";

17.24.9.b.m: as many space-filler bricks as required, then loose earth.

17.24.10.a.m: Some hand down the two desires in reverse order.

17.24.11.a.m: The re-piling is prescribed in the sacred texts for three purposes:

17.24.11.b.m: for the purpose of renown, for the purpose of prosperity, or for the purpose of continuity.

17.24.12.a.m: We shall explain the one for the purpose of renown.

17.24.13.a.s: yadīṣṭyā yadi paśunā yadi somena yajeta yo 'sya purāgnistamanvavasāya yajeta
17.24.13.a.d: यदीष्ट्या यदि पशुना यदि सोमेन यजेत यो ऽस्य पुराग्निस्तमन्ववसाय यजेत
17.24.13.a.m: Whether he sacrifices with an iṣṭi, with an animal sacrifice, or with a soma sacrifice, having shifted the fire that was previously his, he should sacrifice.

17.24.14.a.s: api vā yenarṣaya ityaṣṭau nānāmantrā uttaravedyāmupadadhyāt /
17.24.14.a.d: अपि वा येनर्षय इत्यष्टौ नानामन्त्रा उत्तरवेद्यामुपदध्यात् ।
17.24.14.a.m: Or he should place on the high altar eight bricks with distinct formulas, beginning with: "By which the seers...";

17.24.14.b.m: as many space-filler bricks as required, then loose earth.

17.25.1.a.s: api vottaravedyāmuparyagnau dhāryamāṇe prajāpatistvā sādayatu tayā devatayāṅgirasvaddhruvā sīdetyuttaravedimabhimṛśet
17.25.1.a.d: अपि वोत्तरवेद्यामुपर्यग्नौ धार्यमाणे प्रजापतिस्त्वा सादयतु तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद्ध्रुवा सीदेत्युत्तरवेदिमभिमृशेत्
17.25.1.a.m: Or, while the fire is held over the high altar, he should touch the high altar with: "May Prajāpati seat you; with that deity, sit firm like Aṅgiras."

17.25.2.a.m: Or [he places] three naturally perforated bricks.

17.25.4.a.m: A naturally perforated brick, a chant, loose earth;

17.25.5.a.m: Or [he places] three naturally perforated bricks and three Viśvajyotis bricks.

17.25.7.a.m: A naturally perforated brick, a chant, loose earth, then a Viśvajyotis brick;

17.25.7.c.s: tṛtīyasyāṃ tu viśvajyotiḥ prathamātha svayamātṛṇātha sāmapurīṣam
17.25.7.c.d: तृतीयस्यां तु विश्वज्योतिः प्रथमाथ स्वयमातृणाथ सामपुरीषम्
17.25.7.c.m: in the third, however, the Viśvajyotis brick comes first, then the naturally perforated brick, then the chant and loose earth.

17.25.8.a.m: Or [he places] eight space-filler bricks [and] loose earth;

17.25.9.a.s: agniṃ citvā yaḥ somena yajeta sa etā ekatriṃśataṃ lokaṃpṛṇā uttaravedyāmupadhāya yajeta
17.25.9.a.d: अग्निं चित्वा यः सोमेन यजेत स एता एकत्रिंशतं लोकंपृणा उत्तरवेद्यामुपधाय यजेत
17.25.9.a.m: Having piled the fire altar, he who sacrifices with soma should sacrifice after placing these thirty-one space-filler bricks on the high altar.

17.25.10.a.s: samṛddhyarthāyāṃ tu dvitīyaṃ cinvāno dvitīyasyāṃ citau yenarṣaya ityaṣṭau nānāmantrā uttaravedyāmupadadhyāt /
17.25.10.a.d: समृद्ध्यर्थायां तु द्वितीयं चिन्वानो द्वितीयस्यां चितौ येनर्षय इत्यष्टौ नानामन्त्रा उत्तरवेद्यामुपदध्यात् ।
17.25.10.a.m: In the one for the purpose of prosperity, however, piling for the second time, in the second layer he should place on the high altar eight bricks with distinct formulas, beginning with: "By which the seers...";

17.25.10.b.m: and eight space-filler bricks, then loose earth.

17.25.11.a.s: śvo bhūta etāścaiva nānāmantrā ekādaśa ca lokaṃpṛṇā atha purīṣam
17.25.11.a.d: श्वो भूत एताश्चैव नानामन्त्रा एकादश च लोकंपृणा अथ पुरीषम्
17.25.11.a.m: On the next day, these very bricks with distinct formulas and eleven space-filler bricks, then loose earth.

17.25.12.a.s: śvo bhūta etāścaiva nānāmantrā dvādaśa ca lokaṃpṛṇā atha purīṣam
17.25.12.a.d: श्वो भूत एताश्चैव नानामन्त्रा द्वादश च लोकंपृणा अथ पुरीषम्
17.25.12.a.m: On the next day, these very bricks with distinct formulas and twelve space-filler bricks, then loose earth.

17.25.13.a.s: saṃtānārthāyāṃ tu tṛtīyaṃ cinvānastṛtīyasyāṃ citau yenarṣaya ityaṣṭau nānāmantrā uttaravedyāmupadadhyāt /
17.25.13.a.d: संतानार्थायां तु तृतीयं चिन्वानस्तृतीयस्यां चितौ येनर्षय इत्यष्टौ नानामन्त्रा उत्तरवेद्यामुपदध्यात् ।
17.25.13.a.m: In the one for the purpose of continuity, however, piling for the third time, in the third layer he should place on the high altar eight bricks with distinct formulas, beginning with: "By which the seers...";

17.25.13.b.m: as many space-filler bricks as required, then loose earth.

17.26.1.a.m: Moreover, they indeed say: "It should not be piled,"

17.26.1.b.m: for it has been declared: "Rudra, indeed, is this Fire".

17.26.2.a.m: 'Piled with metres' are optional [forms of the fire altar];

17.26.3.a.m: In the case of the tāpaścita fire-altar, the consecration [lasts] a year.

17.26.4.a.m: Before the upasads, [with the five formulas beginning with] ‘The [cake] on eight potsherds for Agni...’, he offers every four months with each upasad formula.

17.26.5.a.m: Following the upasads, he piles the fire-altar.

17.26.7.a.m: [Drinking milk from] four teats, three teats, two teats, [and] one teat: [these are] the dietary vows for three months each.

17.26.8.a.m: During the laying down [of the bricks], he remains for a year with the [hymn] to Agni of the seers.

17.26.9.a.m: It is known [from scripture]: ‘This is indeed the [hymn] to Agni of the seers, which is the Yājñasenī layer.’

17.26.10.a.m: Or whatever hymns to Agni there may be in the Ṛgveda, he should lay [the bricks] with them.

17.26.11.a.m: The bricks have individual mantras of the extent of a hymn.

17.26.11.b.m: As needed, the space-filler [bricks], then the loose earth.

17.26.12.a.d: तृतीये संवत्सरे ऽभिजिता विश्वजिता वा यजेत
17.26.12.a.m: In the third year he should sacrifice with an Abhijit or a Viśvajit.

17.26.14.a.s: udavasāya rohiṇīṃ vatsacchavīṃ sakarṇapucchāvacchātāṃ sakhurāṃ sakhurikāṃ vā bahirlomaḥ paridhāyoṣṇīṣeṇa pradakṣiṇaṃ śiro veṣṭayitvaudumbaraṃ camasamādatte /
17.26.14.a.d: उदवसाय रोहिणीं वत्सच्छवीं सकर्णपुच्छावच्छातां सखुरां सखुरिकां वा बहिर्लोमः परिधायोष्णीषेण प्रदक्षिणं शिरो वेष्टयित्वौदुम्बरं चमसमादत्ते ।
17.26.14.a.m: Having concluded the sacrifice, wearing the skin of a red calf, having ears and tail, cut whole, with hooves or small hooves, with the hair outwards, having wound [a turban] clockwise around his head with a turban, he takes up an udumbara goblet,

17.26.14.b.s: audumbarīṃ cābhrīṃ vaiṇavīṃ vā kalmāṣīṃ pūrvavatpramāṇām
17.26.14.b.d: औदुम्बरीं चाभ्रीं वैणवीं वा कल्माषीं पूर्ववत्प्रमाणाम्
17.26.14.b.m: and a spade of udumbara wood, or of bamboo, variegated, of the same size as before.

17.26.15.a.m: They [two] stay three nights at an udumbara tree in the forest, feeding on roots and fruits,

17.26.15.c.m: Having dug up a root and placed it in this vessel, the wife and the sacrificer feed each other.

17.26.17.a.m: The sacrificer should seek food with a broom or a small spade;

17.26.17.b.m: the wife with a winnowing basket or a knife, according to some.

17.26.18.a.m: They stay three nights among the Niṣādas,

17.26.18.d.m: or three nights each among the Brahmins.

17.26.19.b.m: and he should not refuse what is given [to him].

17.26.20.a.m: If not for a year, [then] twelve days [in each place], twelve days [in each place].

18.1.1.a.s: śaradi vājapeyena yajeta brāhmaṇo rājanyo varddhikāmaḥ
18.1.1.a.d: शरदि वाजपेयेन यजेत ब्राह्मणो राजन्यो वर्द्धिकामः
18.1.1.a.m: In autumn a Brahmin or a Rājanya desiring prosperity should sacrifice with the Vājapeya.

18.1.2.a.m: Some teach [it] as an obligatory sacrifice.

18.1.4.a.m: Its procedure is like that of the Ṣoḍaśin.

18.1.8.a.s: saptadaśāratnir bailvo yūpaḥ khādiro vā tūparaś caturaśro godhūmapiṣṭacaṣālo godhūmakalāpī vā
18.1.8.a.d: सप्तदशारत्निर् बैल्वो यूपः खादिरो वा तूपरश् चतुरश्रो गोधूमपिष्टचषालो गोधूमकलापी वा
18.1.8.a.m: The sacrificial post is seventeen cubits [high], of bilva or khadira wood, hornless, four-cornered, with a top-ring of wheat flour or with a wheat band.

18.1.9.a.s: yat prāg upasadbhyas tasmin kṛte pratiprasthātā surāyāḥ kalpena surāṃ saṃdadhāti
18.1.9.a.d: यत् प्राग् उपसद्भ्यस् तस्मिन् कृते प्रतिप्रस्थाता सुरायाः कल्पेन सुरां संदधाति
18.1.9.a.m: When that which precedes the upasads is performed, the pratiprasthātṛ brews the surā according to the procedure for surā.

18.1.11.a.s: kharakāle pratiprasthātā dakṣiṇasya havirdhānasyādhastāt paścād akṣaṃ surāgrahārthaṃ dvitīyaṃ kharaṃ karoti
18.1.11.a.d: खरकाले प्रतिप्रस्थाता दक्षिणस्य हविर्धानस्याधस्तात् पश्चाद् अक्षं सुराग्रहार्थं द्वितीयं खरं करोति
18.1.11.a.m: At the time of [erecting] the mound, the pratiprasthātṛ makes a second mound beneath the southern havirdhāna [cart] behind the axle for the purpose of the surā draughts.

18.1.12.a.m: At the time of the cord, he wraps the sacrificial post with seventeen garments.

18.1.13.a.s: pātrasaṃsādanakāle aindram atigrāhyapātraṃ prayujya tatsamīpe pañcaindrāṇy atigrāhyapātrāṇi prayunakti
18.1.13.a.d: पात्रसंसादनकाले ऐन्द्रम् अतिग्राह्यपात्रं प्रयुज्य तत्समीपे पञ्चैन्द्राण्य् अतिग्राह्यपात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति
18.1.13.a.m: At the time of placing the vessels, having set out the atigrāhya vessel for Indra, he sets out near it five atigrāhya vessels for Indra.

18.1.14.a.m: Their procedure is explained by the earlier [one].

18.1.15.a.s: ṣoḍaśipātraṃ prayujya tatsamīpe saptadaśa prājāpatyāṇi somagrahapātrāṇi prayunakti
18.1.15.a.d: षोडशिपात्रं प्रयुज्य तत्समीपे सप्तदश प्राजापत्याणि सोमग्रहपात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति
18.1.15.a.m: Having set out the ṣoḍaśin vessel, he sets out near it seventeen soma draught vessels for Prajāpati.

18.1.16.a.m: Their procedure is like that of the ṣoḍaśin vessel.

18.1.17.a.s: aparasmin khare pratiprasthātā saptadaśopayāmān mṛnmayāni surāgrahapātrāṇi prayunakti
18.1.17.a.d: अपरस्मिन् खरे प्रतिप्रस्थाता सप्तदशोपयामान् मृन्मयानि सुराग्रहपात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति
18.1.17.a.m: On the other mound, the pratiprasthātṛ sets out seventeen earthenware vessels for the surā draughts along with the upayāma [cups].

18.2.1.a.s: grahakāla aindram atigrāhyaṃ gṛhītvopayāmagṛhīto 'si nṛṣadaṃ tveti pañcaindran atigrāhyān gṛhṇāti
18.2.1.a.d: ग्रहकाल ऐन्द्रम् अतिग्राह्यं गृहीत्वोपयामगृहीतो ऽसि नृषदं त्वेति पञ्चैन्द्रन् अतिग्राह्यान् गृह्णाति
18.2.1.a.m: At the time of the draughts, having drawn the atigrāhya [draught] for Indra, he draws the five atigrāhya [draughts] for Indra with: ‘You are taken with a support; you for the dweller among men...’

18.2.3.a.s: ṣoḍaśinaṃ gṛhītvāyā viṣṭhā janayan karvarāṇīti saptadaśa prājāpatyān somagrahān gṛhṇāti
18.2.3.a.d: षोडशिनं गृहीत्वाया विष्ठा जनयन् कर्वराणीति सप्तदश प्राजापत्यान् सोमग्रहान् गृह्णाति
18.2.3.a.m: Having drawn the ṣoḍaśin [draught], he draws the seventeen soma draughts for Prajāpati with: ‘Pervading the positions, generating the variegated...’

18.2.5.a.s: kuvid aṅgety aparasmin khare pratiprasthātā saptadaśabhir upayāmaiḥ surāgrahān gṛhṇāti
18.2.5.a.d: कुविद् अङ्गेत्य् अपरस्मिन् खरे प्रतिप्रस्थाता सप्तदशभिर् उपयामैः सुराग्रहान् गृह्णाति
18.2.5.a.m: With ‘Surely indeed...’, on the other mound, the pratiprasthātṛ draws the surā draughts with seventeen upayāma [cups].

18.2.6.a.m: Some teach the two ladles as reversed.

18.2.7.a.m: He draws the surā draughts alternately with the soma draughts.

18.2.9.a.m: He places the soma draughts in front of the axle;

18.2.9.b.m: [The pratiprasthātṛ sets down] the surā draughts behind the axle.

18.2.10.a.s: deva savitaḥ pra suveti savanādausavanādau juhoti /
18.2.10.a.d: देव सवितः प्र सुवेति सवनादौसवनादौ जुहोति ।
18.2.10.a.m: With "O divine Savitṛ, impel...", he offers at the beginning of each pressing,

18.2.11.a.m: Wearing gold necklaces, the officiating priests proceed on the soma-pressing day.

18.2.12.a.s: paśukāle trīn kratupaśūn upākṛtya mārutīṃ vaśām upākaroti /
18.2.12.a.d: पशुकाले त्रीन् क्रतुपशून् उपाकृत्य मारुतीं वशाम् उपाकरोति ।
18.2.12.a.m: At the time of the animal sacrifice, having assigned the three victim animals of the sacrifice, he assigns a barren cow to the Maruts,

18.2.12.b.m: and an ewe whose teeth have not fallen out to Sarasvatī.

18.2.13.a.s: sārasvataṃ meṣam upākṛtya saptadaśa prājāpatyān paśūn upākaroti śyāmāṃs tūparān ekarūpān
18.2.13.a.d: सारस्वतं मेषम् उपाकृत्य सप्तदश प्राजापत्यान् पशून् उपाकरोति श्यामांस् तूपरान् एकरूपान्
18.2.13.a.m: Having assigned a ram to Sarasvant, he assigns seventeen hornless, uniform dark animals to Prajāpati.

18.2.14.a.m: Of those around which fire has been carried, they immolate the earlier ones ending with the one for Sarasvatī.

18.2.15.a.m: They keep the later ones, beginning with the one for Sarasvant, [alive].

18.2.16.a.m: It has been stated: "There are two strew-grass bundles for each animal."

18.2.17.a.s: prāṅ māhendrāt kṛtvā mādhyaṃdinīyān vā puroḍāśān nirupya sārasvatasya paśupuroḍāśaṃ nirupya bārhaspatyaṃ naivāraṃ saptadaśaśarāvaṃ caruṃ nirvapati /
18.2.17.a.d: प्राङ् माहेन्द्रात् कृत्वा माध्यंदिनीयान् वा पुरोडाशान् निरुप्य सारस्वतस्य पशुपुरोडाशं निरुप्य बार्हस्पत्यं नैवारं सप्तदशशरावं चरुं निर्वपति ।
18.2.17.a.m: Having proceeded [with the ritual] prior to the draught for Mahendra, or having portioned out the cakes of the midday pressing and portioned out the animal cake for Sarasvant, he portions out a wild-rice mess of seventeen dishes for Bṛhaspati.

18.3.1.a.s: indrasya vajro 'sīti ratham upāvahṛtyāpsv antar ity aśvān apsu snāpayanti
18.3.1.a.d: इन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसीति रथम् उपावहृत्याप्स्व् अन्तर् इत्य् अश्वान् अप्सु स्नापयन्ति
18.3.1.a.m: having taken down the chariot with "You are Indra's vajra...", they bathe the horses in water with "Within the waters..."

18.3.2.a.m: With "O Child of the Waters...", he wipes down their foreheads.

18.3.3.a.s: vāyur vā tvā manur vā tveti praṣṭivāhinaṃ rathaṃ yunakti /
18.3.3.a.d: वायुर् वा त्वा मनुर् वा त्वेति प्रष्टिवाहिनं रथं युनक्ति ।
18.3.3.a.m: With "Either Vāyu or Manu [yoke] you...", he yokes the chariot drawn by three horses.

18.3.3.b.m: The other sixteen chariots [are yoked] silently.

18.3.4.a.m: At the time of the dakṣiṇā, he gives seventeen chariots,

18.3.4.b.s: saptadaśānāṃsi saptadaśāśvān saptadaśa hastinaḥ saptadaśa niṣkān saptadaśa dāsyaḥ saptadaśājāḥ saptadaśāvīḥ saptadaśa vāsāṃsi saptadaśa gavāṃ śatāni
18.3.4.b.d: सप्तदशानांसि सप्तदशाश्वान् सप्तदश हस्तिनः सप्तदश निष्कान् सप्तदश दास्यः सप्तदशाजाः सप्तदशावीः सप्तदश वासांसि सप्तदश गवां शतानि
18.3.4.b.m:
seventeen carts, seventeen horses, seventeen elephants, seventeen gold ornaments, seventeen female slaves, seventeen she-goats, seventeen ewes, seventeen garments, [and] seventeen hundred cows.

He gives seventeen hundred cows,

18.3.5.c.s: saptadaśānāṃsi yuktāni saptadaśāśvarathān saptadaśa hastinaḥ saptadaśa niṣkān saptadaśa dāsyaḥ saptadaśa dundubhīn
18.3.5.c.d: सप्तदशानांसि युक्तानि सप्तदशाश्वरथान् सप्तदश हस्तिनः सप्तदश निष्कान् सप्तदश दास्यः सप्तदश दुन्दुभीन्
18.3.5.c.m: seventeen yoked carts, seventeen horse-drawn chariots, seventeen elephants, seventeen gold ornaments, seventeen female slaves, [and] seventeen drums.

18.3.8.a.m: He gives seventeen of each age [group],

18.3.9.a.m: the age groups beginning from one-year-olds up to five-year-olds.

18.3.10.a.m: When the dakṣiṇās have been assigned, he gives the chariot yoked with the yajus to the adhvaryu.

18.3.12.a.s: agreṇāhavanīyam udīcaḥ prāco vā rathān avasthāpayanti
18.3.12.a.d: अग्रेणाहवनीयम् उदीचः प्राचो वा रथान् अवस्थापयन्ति
18.3.12.a.m: They station the chariots in front of the āhavanīya, facing north or facing east.

18.3.13.a.m: The southern one among them is the one yoked with the yajus.

18.3.14.a.s: agreṇāgnīdhraṃ rājaputro 'vasthāya saptadaśa pravyādhān iṣum asyati
18.3.14.a.d: अग्रेणाग्नीध्रं राजपुत्रो ऽवस्थाय सप्तदश प्रव्याधान् इषुम् अस्यति
18.3.14.a.m: Stationing himself in front of the āgnīdhra, a prince shoots seventeen arrow casts.

18.3.15.a.s: yatra jaghanyaṃ nipatati tatraudumbarīṃ kāṣṭhāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ minoti
18.3.15.a.d: यत्र जघन्यं निपतति तत्रौदुम्बरीं काष्ठां लक्षणं मिनोति
18.3.15.a.m: Where the last one falls, there he fixes an udumbara post as a turning mark.

18.4.1.a.s: prāṅ māhendrāt kṛtvā naivāre sarpir ānīya cātvāle 'vadadhāti
18.4.1.a.d: प्राङ् माहेन्द्रात् कृत्वा नैवारे सर्पिर् आनीय चात्वाले ऽवदधाति
18.4.1.a.m: Having proceeded [with the ritual] prior to the draught for Mahendra, having poured clarified butter into the wild-rice [mess], he places it in the cātvāla trench.

18.4.3.a.s: cātvāle rathākṣākṛti kāṣṭhaṃ nikhāya tasminn audumbaraṃ rathacakraṃ saptadaśāraṃ pratimuñcati
18.4.3.a.d: चात्वाले रथाक्षाकृति काष्ठं निखाय तस्मिन्न् औदुम्बरं रथचक्रं सप्तदशारं प्रतिमुञ्चति
18.4.3.a.m: Having planted in the cātvāla trench a piece of wood shaped like a chariot axle, he fastens upon it an udumbara chariot wheel having seventeen spokes.

18.4.4.a.m: On the northern hip of the altar ground, they fasten seventeen drums.

18.4.5.a.d: विष्णोः क्रमो ऽसीति रथं यजमानो ऽभ्यैति
18.4.5.a.m: With "You are Viṣṇu's stride...", the sacrificer approaches the chariot.

18.4.6.a.m: With "The two curves, the two bends...", he touches the two chariot wheels,

18.4.7.a.m: With "Utter your voice for Indra!", they beat the drums together.

18.4.8.a.s: devasyāhaṃ savituḥ prasave bṛhaspatinā vājajitā vājaṃ jeṣam ity audumbaraṃ rathacakraṃ brahmārohati
18.4.8.a.d: देवस्याहं सवितुः प्रसवे बृहस्पतिना वाजजिता वाजं जेषम् इत्य् औदुम्बरं रथचक्रं ब्रह्मारोहति
18.4.8.a.m: With "At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ, with Bṛhaspati who wins the prize, may I win the prize!", the brahman mounts the udumbara chariot wheel.

18.4.9.a.m: He says to him: "Sing the sāman of the swift racers."

18.4.10.a.m: He turns its wheel three times clockwise.

18.4.11.a.m: While it is turning, the brahman sings.

18.4.12.a.s: devasyāhaṃ savituḥ prasave bṛhaspatinā vājajitā varṣiṣṭhaṃ nākaṃ ruheyam iti yajuryuktaṃ yajamāna ārohati
18.4.12.a.d: देवस्याहं सवितुः प्रसवे बृहस्पतिना वाजजिता वर्षिष्ठं नाकं रुहेयम् इति यजुर्युक्तं यजमान आरोहति
18.4.12.a.m: With "At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ, with Bṛhaspati who wins the prize, may I ascend the highest firmament!", the sacrificer mounts the chariot yoked with the yajus.

18.4.14.a.s: vājino vājajito vājaṃ sariṣyanto vājaṃ jeṣyanto bṛhaspater bhāgam ava jighrateti naivāram aśvau dhuryāv avaghrāpayati /
18.4.14.a.d: वाजिनो वाजजितो वाजं सरिष्यन्तो वाजं जेष्यन्तो बृहस्पतेर् भागम् अव जिघ्रतेति नैवारम् अश्वौ धुर्याव् अवघ्रापयति ।
18.4.14.a.m: With "O swift coursers, winners of the prize, about to run for the prize, about to win the prize, sniff Bṛhaspati's portion!", he makes the two yoke-horses sniff the wild-rice mess,

18.4.15.a.s: bṛhaspater bhāge ni mṛḍḍhvam iti praprotheṣu ca lepān nimārṣṭi
18.4.15.a.d: बृहस्पतेर् भागे नि मृड्ढ्वम् इति प्रप्रोथेषु च लेपान् निमार्ष्टि
18.4.15.a.m: With "Wipe [yourselves] on Bṛhaspati's portion!", he also wipes the remnants upon their nostrils.

18.4.16.a.s: aśvājanīty aśvājanīm ādāyādhvaryur yajuryuktam adhiruhyārvāsi saptir asīti tayāśvān samavakṣiṇoti
18.4.16.a.d: अश्वाजनीत्य् अश्वाजनीम् आदायाध्वर्युर् यजुर्युक्तम् अधिरुह्यार्वासि सप्तिर् असीति तयाश्वान् समवक्षिणोति
18.4.16.a.m: Taking the horse whip with "A horse whip [you are]...", having mounted the chariot yoked with the yajus, the adhvaryu touches the horses with it, reciting: "You are a courser; you are a steed..."

18.4.17.a.m: Without overtaking, the other chariots follow behind.

18.4.18.a.d: वाजिनो वाजं धावतेति चतसृभिर् धावतो ऽनुमन्त्रयते
18.4.18.a.m: With the four [verses] beginning with "O swift coursers, run for the prize...", he follows them as they run with his recitation.

18.4.19.a.m: While they are running, he causes the sacrificer to recite the Ujjitis beginning with "Agni by a single syllable..."

18.4.20.a.m: Having reached the turning mark, they turn northward and circle around clockwise.

18.4.21.a.m: With the four [verses] beginning with "Running with measured pace...", he follows them with his recitation as they run back.

18.5.1.a.s: ā mā vājasya prasavo jagamyād iti pratyāsṛteṣu hutvā punar naivāram avaghrāpayati /
18.5.1.a.d: आ मा वाजस्य प्रसवो जगम्याद् इति प्रत्यासृतेषु हुत्वा पुनर् नैवारम् अवघ्रापयति ।
18.5.1.a.m: Having offered with "May the impulsion of the prize come to me..." as they run back, he again makes [the horses] sniff the wild-rice mess.

18.5.1.b.m: With "You who have run...", he wipes off the remnants.

18.5.2.a.s: iyaṃ vaḥ sā satyā saṃdhābhūd iti dundubhivimocanīyaṃ homaṃ juhoti
18.5.2.a.d: इयं वः सा सत्या संधाभूद् इति दुन्दुभिविमोचनीयं होमं जुहोति
18.5.2.a.m: With "This true agreement of yours has come about...", he offers the oblation for unfastening the drums.

18.5.4.a.m: He gives a kṛṣṇala piece to each of the chariot-racers.

18.5.5.a.m: Taking them back, he gives them to the brahman.

18.5.5.b.m: And a honey-pot made of gold weighing a hundred mānas.

18.5.6.a.m: Now he introduces the chant of Mahendra.

18.5.7.a.s: aprastute kṣatrasyolbam asīti tārpyaṃ yajamānaḥ paridhatte
18.5.7.a.d: अप्रस्तुते क्षत्रस्योल्बम् असीति तार्प्यं यजमानः परिधत्ते
18.5.7.a.m: Before it is chanted, the sacrificer puts on a tārpya garment with "You are the inner membrane of the royal power."

18.5.8.a.m: The wife [puts on an apron] made of darbha grass with "You are the womb of the royal power."

18.5.9.a.m: The sacrificer calls out to his wife: "Wife, come!"

18.5.10.a.m: The other responds: "Let us two climb!"

18.5.12.a.s: ahaṃ nāv ubhayoḥ suvo rokṣyāmīti yajamāno 'ntataḥ
18.5.12.a.d: अहं नाव् उभयोः सुवो रोक्ष्यामीति यजमानो ऽन्ततः
18.5.12.a.m: Finally the sacrificer says: "I will climb to heaven for the two of us."

18.5.13.a.s: vājaś ca prasavaś ceti dvādaśa vājaprasavīyān homān hutvāyur yajñena kalpatām iti daśabhiḥ kalpaiḥ sarajase niśraṇyā yūpaṃ yajamāna ārohati
18.5.13.a.d: वाजश् च प्रसवश् चेति द्वादश वाजप्रसवीयान् होमान् हुत्वायुर् यज्ञेन कल्पताम् इति दशभिः कल्पैः सरजसे निश्रण्या यूपं यजमान आरोहति
18.5.13.a.m: Having offered the twelve vājaprasavīya oblations with "Strength and impulse...", the sacrificer ascends the sacrificial post by a ladder with "May life prosper by sacrifice..." through the ten kalpa formulas, accompanied by [a wheel] with pollen.

18.5.14.a.s: suvar devām̐ aganmety agraṃ prapya japati
18.5.14.a.d: सुवर् देवाम्̐ अगन्मेत्य् अग्रं प्रप्य जपति
18.5.14.a.m: Having reached the top, he mutters: "We have gone to heaven, to the gods!"

18.5.15.a.s: sam ahaṃ prajayā saṃ mayā prajeti gṛhān prekṣate
18.5.15.a.d: सम् अहं प्रजया सं मया प्रजेति गृहान् प्रेक्षते
18.5.15.a.m: He looks at his home with "May I be united with offspring, may offspring be united with me!"

18.5.16.a.s: tam āśvatthair āsapuṭair ūṣapuṭair ubhayair vā vaiśyāḥ pratidiśam arpayanti /
18.5.16.a.d: तम् आश्वत्थैर् आसपुटैर् ऊषपुटैर् उभयैर् वा वैश्याः प्रतिदिशम् अर्पयन्ति ।
18.5.16.a.m: The vaiśyas throw at him from each direction [packets of food] in packets of aśvattha leaves or packets of saline earth, or both.

18.5.16.b.m: Or the principal priests, having tied them onto long bamboos, [throw them]:

18.5.17.a.m: The adhvaryu from the east with "To food for you!";

18.5.17.b.m: The brahman from the south with "To the eating of food for you!";

18.5.17.c.m: The hotṛ from the west with "To strength for you!";

18.5.17.d.m: The udgātā from the north with "To winning strength for you!"

18.5.20.a.s: iyaṃ te rāṇ mitrāya yantrāya dhartrāya kṛṣyai kṣemāya rayyai poṣāyeti pratyavarohati
18.5.20.a.d: इयं ते राण् मित्राय यन्त्राय धर्त्राय कृष्यै क्षेमाय रय्यै पोषायेति प्रत्यवरोहति
18.5.20.a.m: He descends with "This is your rule: for friendship, for restraint, for support, for agriculture, for security, for wealth, for prosperity!"

18.5.21.a.m: In front of the sacrificial post, having spread out a he-goat skin with the neck to the east and the hair upward,

18.6.1.a.s: tasmiñ chatamānaṃ hiraṇyaṃ nidhāyāmṛtaṃ asīti hiraṇye dakṣiṇaṃ pādaṃ yajamānaḥ pratiṣṭhāpayate
18.6.1.a.d: तस्मिञ् छतमानं हिरण्यं निधायामृतं असीति हिरण्ये दक्षिणं पादं यजमानः प्रतिष्ठापयते
18.6.1.a.m: and placed gold weighing a hundred mānas upon it, the sacrificer sets his right foot upon the gold with "You are immortality."

18.6.2.a.s: puṣṭir asi prajananam asīti bastājine savyam
18.6.2.a.d: पुष्टिर् असि प्रजननम् असीति बस्ताजिने सव्यम्
18.6.2.a.m: His left [foot] upon the he-goat skin with "You are nourishment, you are procreation."

18.6.3.a.m: From there he ascends a chair.

18.6.4.a.s: divaṃ proṣṭhinīm āroha tām āruhya prapaśyaikarāṇ manuṣyāṇām ity ārohantam abhimantrayate
18.6.4.a.d: दिवं प्रोष्ठिनीम् आरोह ताम् आरुह्य प्रपश्यैकराण् मनुष्याणाम् इत्य् आरोहन्तम् अभिमन्त्रयते
18.6.4.a.m: He addresses him as he ascends with "Ascend heaven, the bench; having ascended it, look out as the sole ruler among men!"

18.6.5.a.m: With seven [formulas], he offers the seven preliminary food-oblations.

18.6.6.a.m: He is consecrated during the chant of Mahendra, just as at the piling of the fire altar.

18.6.7.a.s: mādhyaṃdinasya savanasya madhyama ukthyaparyāye brahmasāmny upākṛte 'tra sārasvataprabhṛtīn uttarān ālabhante
18.6.7.a.d: माध्यंदिनस्य सवनस्य मध्यम उक्थ्यपर्याये ब्रह्मसाम्न्य् उपाकृते ऽत्र सारस्वतप्रभृतीन् उत्तरान् आलभन्ते
18.6.7.a.m: At the midday pressing, in the middle ukthya round, when the Brahman's saman has been introduced, they seize the later [victims] beginning with the one for Sarasvatī.

18.6.8.a.m: He proceeds with their omenta without basting them.

18.6.9.a.s: sārasvatasya vapayā pracarya samavadāyetareṣāṃ vapābhiḥ pracarati
18.6.9.a.d: सारस्वतस्य वपया प्रचर्य समवदायेतरेषां वपाभिः प्रचरति
18.6.9.a.m: Having proceeded with the omentum of the victim for Sarasvatī, he cuts off [portions] together and proceeds with the omenta of the other [victims].

18.6.10.a.m: Having proceeded with the animal cake of the victim for Sarasvatī, he proceeds with the [cake] made of wild rice.

18.6.11.a.m: However, the sviṣṭakṛt and the iḍā are common.

18.6.12.a.m: The principal priests are the eaters of the remnants of the oblation.

18.6.13.a.m: They partake of the remnants of the oblation in the āgnīdhra [shed].

18.6.14.a.m: Now he proceeds with the portions for the deity of those ending with the one for Sarasvatī, up to the conversation of the iḍā,

18.6.15.a.s: ṣoḍaśinā pracarya hotṛcamasamukhyāṃś camasān unnīya bṛhataḥ stotram upākaroti
18.6.15.a.d: षोडशिना प्रचर्य होतृचमसमुख्यांश् चमसान् उन्नीय बृहतः स्तोत्रम् उपाकरोति
18.6.15.a.m: Having proceeded with the ṣoḍaśin [draught] and drawn the goblets, beginning with the hotṛ's goblet, he introduces the chant of the Bṛhat [sāman].

18.6.16.a.m: At the time of proceeding, the adhvaryu takes up the hotṛ's goblet,

18.6.16.c.m: the [other] priests the remaining soma draughts,

18.6.17.a.m: the pratiprasthātṛ takes up the chief of the surā draughts,

18.6.17.b.m: the chariot-racers the remaining surā draughts.

18.7.1.a.s: saṃpṛca stha saṃ mā bhadreṇa pṛṅkteti prāṅ adhvaryuḥ somagrahair uddravati /
18.7.1.a.d: संपृच स्थ सं मा भद्रेण पृङ्क्तेति प्राङ् अध्वर्युः सोमग्रहैर् उद्द्रवति ।
18.7.1.a.m: With "You are united; unite me with good fortune!", the adhvaryu runs forward toward the east with the soma draughts.

18.7.1.b.s: vipṛca stha vi mā pāpmanā pṛṅkteti pratyaṅ pratiprasthāṭ surāgrahaiḥ
18.7.1.b.d: विपृच स्थ वि मा पाप्मना पृङ्क्तेति प्रत्यङ् प्रतिप्रस्थाट् सुराग्रहैः
18.7.1.b.m: With "You are disunited; disunite me from evil!", the pratiprasthātṛ [runs] toward the west with the surā draughts.

18.7.2.a.m: They stand near the edge of the āhavanīya with the soma draughts,

18.7.2.b.m: near the edge of the mārjālīya with the surā draughts.

18.7.3.a.m: He proceeds with the soma draughts.

18.7.4.a.m: Following the vaṣaṭ-call and the secondary vaṣaṭ-call, they shake the surā draughts.

18.7.5.a.m: The partaking of the soma has been explained.

18.7.6.a.m: He modifies the formula for partaking: "...having the virāj as metre."

18.7.7.a.m: They bring the cut-off portions of the victim for the Maruts and the soma draughts to the priests,

18.7.7.b.m: the non-cut-off portions and the surā draughts to the chariot-racers.

18.7.8.a.m: Having torn them apart on the southern hip of the altar ground, they partake of them.

18.7.9.a.s: kakudo rājaputro dhruvagopo naivāragopo vā prāśnīyāt /
18.7.9.a.d: ककुदो राजपुत्रो ध्रुवगोपो नैवारगोपो वा प्राश्नीयात् ।
18.7.9.a.m: A foremost prince, a constant protector, or a protector of wild rice should eat [them].

18.7.9.b.m: Or [he offers] the whole peak [mess] after all the soma [oblations].

18.7.10.a.m: Here he proceeds with the deity-section of the animals beginning with that for Sarasvant.

18.7.11.a.m: "They proceed in the forest of the sacrifice," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

18.7.12.a.s: tad yatreṣṭā anūyājā bhavanty avyūḍhāḥ srucaḥ /
18.7.12.a.d: तद् यत्रेष्टा अनूयाजा भवन्त्य् अव्यूढाः स्रुचः ।
18.7.12.a.m: When the after-offerings are offered, [and] the ladles are not yet displaced,

18.7.12.d.s: hvalati vā etad yajño yad evaṃ kurvantīti
18.7.12.d.d: ह्वलति वा एतद् यज्ञो यद् एवं कुर्वन्तीति
18.7.12.d.m: "The sacrifice indeed stumbles when they do so," [so says the Brāhmaṇa].

18.7.13.a.s: tasmād yatraiva pūrveṣāṃ vapābhiś careyus tad itareṣām /
18.7.13.a.d: तस्माद् यत्रैव पूर्वेषां वपाभिश् चरेयुस् तद् इतरेषाम् ।
18.7.13.a.m: Therefore, wherever they proceed with the omenta of the earlier [victims], there [they should proceed with the omenta] of the others;

18.7.13.b.m: and wherever [they proceed] with the oblation-materials, there [they should proceed] with the oblation-materials.

18.7.15.a.m: Having sacrificed with it, he should sacrifice with the Sautrāmaṇī,

18.7.15.b.m: or with the curd-mixture for Mitra and Varuṇa.

18.7.16.a.m: As long as he lives, he should not descend before anyone;

18.7.17.a.m: or he should sacrifice with the Bṛhaspatisava that causes descending.

18.7.18.a.m: "He becomes one who possesses a white umbrella," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

18.8.1.a.m: A king desiring heaven should sacrifice with the Rājasūya.

18.8.3.a.m: The first day is an Agniṣṭoma terminating with five [stotras].

18.8.4.a.m: He gives five thousand at the Pavitra,

18.8.5.a.m: Or else, four [thousand] at the Abhiṣecanīya,

18.8.6.a.m: and one thousand for each of the other days.

18.8.7.a.s: ṣaṣṭitrīṇi śatāni sahasrāṇāṃ dadātīti bahvṛcabrāhmaṇaṃ bhavhati
18.8.7.a.d: षष्टित्रीणि शतानि सहस्राणां ददातीति बह्वृचब्राह्मणं भव्हति
18.8.7.a.m: "He gives three hundred and sixty thousands," so states the Brāhmaṇa of the Rigvedins.

18.8.8.a.m: He should distribute the sacrificial gifts in such a way that his days [of ritual] have their own proper times.

18.8.10.a.m: On the next day, he sacrifices day after day with the eight [offerings] beginning with the one to Anumati.

18.8.11.a.m: While grinding [the grains] for the offering to Anumati, he scatters [some] to the west and to the north.

18.8.12.a.m: Those that fall off towards the west of the yoke-pin form the cake on one potsherd for Nirṛti.

18.8.13.a.s: ya udañcastānudaṅ paretya valmīkavapāmuddhatyedamahamamuṣyāmuṣyāyaṇasya kṣetriyamavayaja iti śuktyā valmīkavapāyāṃ hutvedamahamamuṣyāmuṣyāyaṇasya kṣetriyamapidadhāmīti tayaiva śuktyā valmīkavapāmapidadhyāt
18.8.13.a.d: य उदञ्चस्तानुदङ् परेत्य वल्मीकवपामुद्धत्येदमहममुष्यामुष्यायणस्य क्षेत्रियमवयज इति शुक्त्या वल्मीकवपायां हुत्वेदमहममुष्यामुष्यायणस्य क्षेत्रियमपिदधामीति तयैव शुक्त्या वल्मीकवपामपिदध्यात्
18.8.13.a.m: Those that [fall off] towards the north, having gone north with them and taken up the moist earth of an anthill, [and] having made an offering into the moist earth of the anthill with a shell with the words: "Herewith I sacrifice away the hereditary disease of so-and-so, son of so-and-so," he should cover the moist earth of the anthill with that same shell, with the words: "Herewith I cover the hereditary disease of so-and-so, son of so-and-so."

18.8.14.a.m: "He offers with the moist earth of an anthill, [and] he covers with the moist earth of an anthill," say some.

18.8.15.a.m: Having placed the oblation for Anumati, he proceeds with the offering for Nirṛti.

18.8.16.a.s: vīhi svāheti gārhaptye hutvā dakṣiṇāgnerekolmukaṃ dhūpāyaddharati
18.8.16.a.d: वीहि स्वाहेति गार्हप्त्ये हुत्वा दक्षिणाग्नेरेकोल्मुकं धूपायद्धरति
18.8.16.a.m: Having offered into the gārhapatya with the words, "Svāhā to the bird!", he takes a smoking brand from the southern fire.

18.8.17.a.s: dakṣiṇamaparamavāntaradeśaṃ gatvā svakṛta iriṇe pradare vopasamādhāyaiṣa te nirṛte bhāga ityaṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ visraṃsikākāṇḍābhyāṃ vā nairṛtaṃ sarvahutaṃ juhoti
18.8.17.a.d: दक्षिणमपरमवान्तरदेशं गत्वा स्वकृत इरिणे प्रदरे वोपसमाधायैष ते निरृते भाग इत्यङ्गुष्ठाभ्यां विस्रंसिकाकाण्डाभ्यां वा नैरृतं सर्वहुतं जुहोति
18.8.17.a.m: Having gone to the south-western direction, [and] having established [the fire] in a natural cleft or chasm, he offers the oblation for Nirṛti as a whole-offering with the thumbs or with stems of visraṃsikā-reeds, with the words: "This is your share, O Nirṛti!"

18.8.18.a.m: A black garment with black fringe is the sacrificial gift.

18.8.19.a.m: "A black garment with torn border," say some.

18.8.20.a.m: "They return without looking back, for concealment from Nirṛti," so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

18.9.1.a.s: svāhā namo ya idaṃ cakāreti punaretya gārhapatye hutvānumatena pracarati
18.9.1.a.d: स्वाहा नमो य इदं चकारेति पुनरेत्य गार्हपत्ये हुत्वानुमतेन प्रचरति
18.9.1.a.m: Having returned, [and] having offered into the gārhapatya with the words, "Svāhā, homage to him who did this!", he proceeds with the offering to Anumati.

18.9.3.a.m: Having sacrificed day after day with these [offerings ending with] the mess of boiled rice for the Ādityas, he undertakes the Cāturmāsyas.

18.9.4.a.m: He sacrifices with them for a year.

18.9.5.a.m: He does not combine the Śunāsīrīya [with the other seasonal sacrifices].

18.9.6.a.m: Then he sacrifices with the Indraturīya having four oblations,

18.9.7.a.m: namely, [the cake] on eight potsherds for Agni, and so on.

18.9.9.a.m: With it he should cause one who has a rival, or one who is dear, to sacrifice.

18.9.10.a.m: In the night of that very night, he sacrifices with the Pañcedhmīya.

18.9.11.a.s: caturdhāhavanīyaṃ pratidiśaṃ vyuddhṛtya madhye pañcamaṃ kṛtvā pṛthagidhmānupasamādhāya juhvāṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā ye devāḥ puraḥsada ityetairyathāliṅgaṃ juhoti /
18.9.11.a.d: चतुर्धाहवनीयं प्रतिदिशं व्युद्धृत्य मध्ये पञ्चमं कृत्वा पृथगिध्मानुपसमाधाय जुह्वां पञ्चगृहीतं गृहीत्वा ये देवाः पुरःसद इत्येतैर्यथालिङ्गं जुहोति ।
18.9.11.a.m: Having taken up the āhavanīya in four parts toward each direction, having made a fifth in the middle, having placed separate piles of firewood [on them], [and] having taken five ladlings into the juhū ladle, he offers with the verses, "The gods who sit in the front...", according to their characteristics,

18.9.12.a.s: samūḍhaṃ rakṣa iti madhya idhmānupasamūhyaikadhopasamādhāyāparaṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvāgnaye rakṣoghne svāhetyuttarāḥ pañcāhutīrjuhoti
18.9.12.a.d: समूढं रक्ष इति मध्य इध्मानुपसमूह्यैकधोपसमाधायापरं पञ्चगृहीतं गृहीत्वाग्नये रक्षोघ्ने स्वाहेत्युत्तराः पञ्चाहुतीर्जुहोति
18.9.12.a.m: Having gathered the firewood together into the middle with the words, "Gathered together is the rakṣas!", having laid them together as one, [and] having taken another five ladlings, he offers the subsequent five oblations with the words, "Svāhā to Agni, the slayer of rakṣases!"

18.9.13.a.m: A chariot drawn by three horses is the sacrificial gift,

18.9.14.a.s: tena yajeta yo rakṣobhyo bibhīyātpiśācebhyo vā
18.9.14.a.d: तेन यजेत यो रक्षोभ्यो बिभीयात्पिशाचेभ्यो वा
18.9.14.a.m: He who fears rakṣases or piśācas should sacrifice with it.

18.9.15.a.m: At dawn, before the agnihotra, they proceed with the Apāmārga-homa.

18.9.16.a.m: Having fetched apāmārga plants from a pool of water, having turned them into groats, he takes a smoking brand from the southern fire.

18.9.17.a.s: uttaramaparamavāntaradeśaṃ gatvā svakṛta iriṇe pradare vopasamādhāya devasya tvetyanudrutya rakṣaso vadhaṃ juhomīti parṇamayena sruveṇa juhoti
