18.9.17.a.d: उत्तरमपरमवान्तरदेशं गत्वा स्वकृत इरिणे प्रदरे वोपसमाधाय देवस्य त्वेत्यनुद्रुत्य रक्षसो वधं जुहोमीति पर्णमयेन स्रुवेण जुहोति
18.9.17.a.m: Having gone to the north-western direction, having established [the fire] in a natural cleft or chasm, [and] having recited, "At the impulse of the god Savitṛ...", he offers with a spoon of parṇa wood with the words, "I offer the slaying of the rakṣas!"

18.9.18.a.s: hataṃ rakṣa iti sruvamanuprahṛtyāvadhiṣma rakṣa ityupatiṣṭhate
18.9.18.a.d: हतं रक्ष इति स्रुवमनुप्रहृत्यावधिष्म रक्ष इत्युपतिष्ठते
18.9.18.a.m: Having thrown in the spoon with the words, "Slain is the rakṣas!", he attends [the fire] with the words, "We have slain the rakṣas!"

18.9.20.a.m: They return without looking back, 'for the concealment of the demons', so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

18.10.1.a.m: Having offered the agnihotra, he pours out the offerings to the Devikās:

18.10.2.a.m: a twelve-pot-sherd cake for Dhātṛ—[these] five.

18.10.3.a.m: A pair of cattle is the dakṣiṇā.

18.10.4.a.m: An animal is also to be immolated here for Dhātṛ;

18.10.5.a.m: An eleven-pot-sherd [cake] for Agni-and-Viṣṇu—[these are] three offerings.

18.10.6.a.m: With the first of these, one desiring a village should sacrifice;

18.10.6.b.m: with the second, one desiring spiritual brilliance;

18.10.8.a.m: He pours out a twelve-pot-sherd cake for Vaiśvānara.

18.10.10.a.m: [He pours out] a pap of barley, solid, a span in measure in all directions;

18.10.11.a.m: a horse that carries [a draft] without being castrated is the dakṣiṇā.

18.10.12.a.m: A pap for Bṛhaspati—[these are] twelve offerings to the Jewel-holders day after day.

18.10.13.a.s: yasya gṛhe nirvapati tata iṣṭipariveṣaṇaṃ dakṣiṇā ca
18.10.13.a.d: यस्य गृहे निर्वपति तत इष्टिपरिवेषणं दक्षिणा च
18.10.13.a.m: In whosever house he pours out [the offering], from there come the distribution of food at the sacrifice and the dakṣiṇā.

18.10.14.a.m: The fourth [offering] is a pap for Bhaga in the house of the favorite wife.

18.10.15.a.m: A heifer whose embryo has miscarried is the dakṣiṇā.

18.10.16.a.m: Some say there is an offering to Nirṛti, a pap the measure of a thumb-joint in all directions.

18.10.17.a.m: A three-pot-sherd [cake] to Viṣṇu, the thirteenth, in the house of the carpenter and chariot-maker.

18.10.19.a.m: or [he offers] in [the house] of the carpenter or the chariot-maker, say some.

18.10.20.a.m: A gavidhukā-pap to Rudra in the house of the dice-keeper;

18.10.21.a.m: A halter made of horsehair is the dakṣiṇā;

18.10.21.b.m: or a sword wrapped in hair, or a spotted [bull];

18.10.22.a.m: 'a three-year-old', so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

18.10.23.a.s: asirvālāvṛto vārdhrīvālapratigrathitā govyacchinī barāsī dāmatūṣā śabalo vā vatsataraḥ
18.10.23.a.d: असिर्वालावृतो वार्ध्रीवालप्रतिग्रथिता गोव्यच्छिनी बरासी दामतूषा शबलो वा वत्सतरः
18.10.23.a.m: A sword wrapped with hair, a strap interwoven with hair, a cow-slayer, a coarse cloth with long fringes, or a spotted young bull.

18.10.25.a.m: 'To the road, svāhā!'—thus he offers in the house of the messenger.

18.10.27.a.m: Three leather [quivers] containing arrows are the dakṣiṇā;

18.10.27.b.m: or a bow wrapped with reed.

18.10.28.a.m: In the house of the sacrificer, he pours out in return an eleven-pot-sherd cake to Indra the Good Protector;

18.10.28.b.m: an eleven-pot-sherd [cake] to Indra the Deliverer from Distress.

18.11.1.a.s: ayaṃ no rājā vṛtrahā rājā bhūtvā vṛtraṃ vadhyāditi purastātsviṣṭakṛto 'dhvaryurjapati
18.11.1.a.d: अयं नो राजा वृत्रहा राजा भूत्वा वृत्रं वध्यादिति पुरस्तात्स्विष्टकृतो ऽध्वर्युर्जपति
18.11.1.a.m: 'May this our king, the slayer of Vṛtra, having become king, slay Vṛtra'—thus the adhvaryu mutters before the sviṣṭakṛt.

18.11.2.a.s: svayamavapannāyā aśvatthaśākhāyai maitraṃ pātraṃ catuḥsraktiṃ karoti
18.11.2.a.d: स्वयमवपन्नाया अश्वत्थशाखायै मैत्रं पात्रं चतुःस्रक्तिं करोति
18.11.2.a.m: From a branch of an aśvattha tree that has fallen by itself, he makes a four-cornered vessel for Mitra.

18.11.3.a.m: They milk a white cow having a white calf into a skin bag made of unprocessed hide.

18.11.4.a.m: They carry it about continuously until it thickens of itself.

18.11.5.a.m: Having churned of itself, they hang it in the sun.

18.11.6.a.m: Then, having melted of itself, it becomes clarified butter.

18.11.7.a.m: On the next day, he initiates the consecrations of the Abhiṣecanīya, which is an Ukthya.

18.11.8.a.m: The consecratory offering belongs to Mitra-and-Bṛhaspati.

18.11.10.b.m: they make half of the altar ground;

18.11.10.e.m: he binds up half that is self-cut;

18.11.10.f.m: he fells half of the firewood;

18.11.12.a.s: pātrasaṃsādanakāle bārhaspatyaṃ caruṃ maitraṃ ca pātraṃ kapālānāṃ sthāne prayunakti
18.11.12.a.d: पात्रसंसादनकाले बार्हस्पत्यं चरुं मैत्रं च पात्रं कपालानां स्थाने प्रयुनक्ति
18.11.12.a.m: At the time of setting down the vessels, he employs a vessel for the mess of boiled rice for Bṛhaspati and a vessel for Mitra in place of the potsherds.

18.11.13.a.m: With the dividing mantra, he separates the husked rice grains into those with ears and those without ears.

18.11.14.a.m: "The smallest and the largest," say some.

18.11.15.a.m: Those that are with ears [broken grains] become the Bārhaspatya [mess of boiled rice] cooked in milk.

18.11.16.a.m: When it is cooked, he covers it with the vessel for Mitra.

18.11.18.a.m: He scatters the earless [whole grains] into the ghee with the strainer.

18.11.19.a.m: He places the two [vessels] one above the other.

18.11.21.a.m: Having placed the Bārhaspatya [mess], he places the Maitra [mess].

18.11.23.a.m: A white-backed [ox] is the sacrificial gift for the Bārhaspatya [offering];

18.11.23.c.m: And that [cow] which is white and has a white calf.

18.12.1.a.s: tathābhiṣecanīyasyokthyasya dīkṣāḥ pravardhayati yathā saṃvatsarasya daśarātre śiṣṭe daśapeyo bhaviṣyatīti
18.12.1.a.d: तथाभिषेचनीयस्योक्थ्यस्य दीक्षाः प्रवर्धयति यथा संवत्सरस्य दशरात्रे शिष्टे दशपेयो भविष्यतीति
18.12.1.a.m: He extends the consecration days of the Abhiṣecanīya Ukthya sacrifice in such a way that the Daśapeya will take place when ten nights of the year remain.

18.12.2.a.m: He buys both somas together, for the Abhiṣecanīya and for the Daśapeya;

18.12.3.a.s: ardhaṃ rājñaḥ purohitasya gṛhe daśapeyārthaṃ nidadhāti
18.12.3.a.d: अर्धं राज्ञः पुरोहितस्य गृहे दशपेयार्थं निदधाति
18.12.3.a.m: He deposits half of the king [Soma] in the house of the domestic priest for the sake of the Daśapeya.

18.12.4.a.s: agnīṣomīyasya paśupuroḍāśam aṣṭau devasuvāṃ havīṃṣy anunirvapati
18.12.4.a.d: अग्नीषोमीयस्य पशुपुरोडाशम् अष्टौ देवसुवां हवींष्य् अनुनिर्वपति
18.12.4.a.m: After the animal cake for Agni-Soma, he pours out the eight offerings that impel the gods (devasū).

18.12.5.a.m: The Sviṣṭakṛt offering and the iḍā, however, are common.

18.12.6.a.s: purastāt sviṣṭakṛtaḥ savitā tvā prasavānāṃ suvatām iti brahmā yajamānasya hastaṃ gṛhṇāti
18.12.6.a.d: पुरस्तात् स्विष्टकृतः सविता त्वा प्रसवानां सुवताम् इति ब्रह्मा यजमानस्य हस्तं गृह्णाति
18.12.6.a.m: Before the Sviṣṭakṛt offering, the brahman priest takes the hand of the sacrificer with [the verse]: "May Savitṛ impel you of the impellers..."

18.12.7.a.s: athainaṃ ratnibhya āvedayatyeṣa vo bharatā rājeti /
18.12.7.a.d: अथैनं रत्निभ्य आवेदयत्येष वो भरता राजेति ।
18.12.7.a.m: Then he announces him to the royal dignitaries: "This, O Bharatas, is your king!"

18.12.7.b.m: "This, O Kurus, is your king!" to a descendant of Kuru;

18.12.7.c.m: "This, O Pañcālas, is your king!" to a descendant of Pañcāla;

18.12.7.d.s: eṣa vaḥ kurupañcālā rājeti vā kurupāñcālān /
18.12.7.d.d: एष वः कुरुपञ्चाला राजेति वा कुरुपाञ्चालान् ।
18.12.7.d.m: Or "This, O Kuru-Pañcālas, is your king!" to the Kuru-Pañcālas;

18.12.7.e.m: "This, O people, is your king!" to other kings.

18.12.8.a.d: सोमो ऽस्माकं ब्राह्मणानां राजेति ब्रह्मा जपति
18.12.8.a.m: "Soma is the king of us, the brāhmaṇas," mutters the brahman priest.

18.12.9.a.s: prati tyan nāma rājyam adhāyīti vāruṇībhyāṃ yajamāno mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe
18.12.9.a.d: प्रति त्यन् नाम राज्यम् अधायीति वारुणीभ्यां यजमानो मुखं विमृष्टे
18.12.9.a.m: The sacrificer wipes his face with the two [verses] addressed to Varuṇa: "This name, the kingship, has been assumed..."

18.12.10.a.s: viṣṇoḥ kramo 'sīti trīn viṣṇukramān prācaḥ krāmati
18.12.10.a.d: विष्णोः क्रमो ऽसीति त्रीन् विष्णुक्रमान् प्राचः क्रामति
18.12.10.a.m: With [the formula]: "You are the stride of Viṣṇu," he strides three Viṣṇu-strides toward the east.

18.12.11.a.s: prāṅ māhendrāt kṛtvā mādhyaṃdinīyān puroḍāśān nirupya mārutam ekaviṃśatikapālaṃ nirvapati /
18.12.11.a.d: प्राङ् माहेन्द्रात् कृत्वा माध्यंदिनीयान् पुरोडाशान् निरुप्य मारुतम् एकविंशतिकपालं निर्वपति ।
18.12.11.a.m: Having performed [the rites] up to the draught for Mahendra and having poured out the midday sacrificial cakes, he pours out [an oblation] on twenty-one potsherds for the Maruts,

18.12.12.a.m: He arranges its potsherds with the third sets of the Araṇye'nuvākya;

18.12.12.c.m: In the middle with an Araṇye'nuvākya [formula].

18.12.13.a.m: Having covered [the cake with ashes], he takes the draughts of water.

18.12.14.a.m: In the Āgnīdhra [shed] they are taken into Vāyu-vessels.

18.12.15.a.m: Sixteen or seventeen oblations are offered;

18.12.16.a.m: Just as many draughts are taken.

18.13.1.a.s: artheta stheti sārasvatiṣv apsu hutvaitenaiva mantreṇa gṛhṇāti
18.13.1.a.d: अर्थेत स्थेति सारस्वतिष्व् अप्सु हुत्वैतेनैव मन्त्रेण गृह्णाति
18.13.1.a.m: Having offered into the waters of the Sarasvatī with: "You are fit for the purpose...", he takes [water] with this very formula.

18.13.2.b.m: With whichever [formula] he makes the offering, with that he takes [the water].

18.13.3.a.s: apāṃ patir iti samudriyāḥ saindhavīrvā yo vānyaḥ puṃnadaḥ syāt
18.13.3.a.d: अपां पतिर् इति समुद्रियाः सैन्धवीर्वा यो वान्यः पुंनदः स्यात्
18.13.3.a.m: With "Lord of the waters..." [he takes water] from the ocean or from the Sindhu, or whichever other river has a masculine name.

18.13.4.a.m: When a man or an animal has stepped in, one wave fights against the current,

18.13.5.b.m: With "You are having a bull-host..." that which goes with the current.

18.13.6.a.m: With "You dwell in the pen..." [he takes] of well-waters.

18.13.7.a.m: With "You are the might of the Maruts..." of those which flow against the current;

18.13.8.a.s: prahāvarī stheti yā utsyanditvā tatraiva pratyavasicyante
18.13.8.a.d: प्रहावरी स्थेति या उत्स्यन्दित्वा तत्रैव प्रत्यवसिच्यन्ते
18.13.8.a.m: With "You are overflowing..." of those which, having welled up, are poured down right there.

18.13.9.a.m: With "You flow around..." of flowing rivers.

18.13.10.a.m: With "Sun-splendoured..." of rainwater when the sun shines.

18.13.11.a.m: With "Sun-skinned..." of those in which reflections are seen.

18.13.14.a.m: With "Mighty ones..." of the amniotic fluid of a cow.

18.13.17.a.m: With "Born of the brilliance of Agni..." of ghee.

18.13.18.a.m: With "The sap of waters and plants..." of honey.

18.13.19.a.s: apo devīr madhumatīr agṛhṇann iti sarvatra home grahaṇe cānuṣajati
18.13.19.a.d: अपो देवीर् मधुमतीर् अगृह्णन्न् इति सर्वत्र होमे ग्रहणे चानुषजति
18.13.19.a.m: With 'The divine waters took what contains sweetness', he appends [this formula] everywhere at an oblation and at a drawing.

18.13.20.a.s: rāṣṭradā stha rāṣṭraṃ datta svāheti homasaṃyukte /
18.13.20.a.d: राष्ट्रदा स्थ राष्ट्रं दत्त स्वाहेति होमसंयुक्ते ।
18.13.20.a.m: With 'You are kingdom-givers; give kingdom, svāhā!' [at that which is] accompanied by an oblation;

18.13.20.b.m: with 'You are kingdom-givers; give kingdom to so-and-so' [at that which is] accompanied by a drawing.

18.13.21.a.s: devīrāpa iti vaitase sate grahānsamavanīyānādhṛṣṭāḥ sidatetyantarā hoturdhiṣṇiyaṃ brāhmaṇācchaṃsinaśca sādayitvānibhṛṣṭamasīti tasmiñchatamānaṃ hiraṇyamavadhāya śukrā vaḥ śukreṇotpunāmīti tenotpūya sadhamādo dyumninīrūrja etā iti caturṣu pātreṣu vyānayati /
18.13.21.a.d: देवीराप इति वैतसे सते ग्रहान्समवनीयानाधृष्टाः सिदतेत्यन्तरा होतुर्धिष्णियं ब्राह्मणाच्छंसिनश्च सादयित्वानिभृष्टमसीति तस्मिञ्छतमानं हिरण्यमवधाय शुक्रा वः शुक्रेणोत्पुनामीति तेनोत्पूय सधमादो द्युम्निनीरूर्ज एता इति चतुर्षु पात्रेषु व्यानयति ।
18.13.21.a.m: Having poured together the draughts into a reed bowl with 'O divine waters', having placed [it] between the dhiṣṇiya of the hotṛ and [that] of the brāhmaṇācchaṃsin with 'Unassailable, sit down', having put a gold piece weighing a hundred mānas into it with 'You are unburned', having purified [the waters] with it with 'Bright ones, I purify you with the bright one', he distributes [the waters] into four vessels with 'These are the rapturous, brilliant invigorating draughts.'

18.13.21.b.m: [Into vessels] of palāśa wood, of udumbara wood, of aśvattha wood, and of nyagrodha wood.

18.13.22.a.s: yaḥ sate prarekas tam udaṅ paretya rudra yat te krayī paraṃ nāmety āgnīdhrīye juhoti
18.13.22.a.d: यः सते प्ररेकस् तम् उदङ् परेत्य रुद्र यत् ते क्रयी परं नामेत्य् आग्नीध्रीये जुहोति
18.13.22.a.m: Going north, he offers the remnant that is in the bowl on the āgnīdhra fire with 'O Rudra, your highest name is the purchaser.'

18.14.1.a.m: With 'You are the outer membrane of dominion', the sacrificer puts on a tārpya garment.

18.14.1.b.s: kṣatrasya yonir asīti pāṇḍaram uṣṇīṣaṃ dvitīyam
18.14.1.b.d: क्षत्रस्य योनिर् असीति पाण्डरम् उष्णीषं द्वितीयम्
18.14.1.b.m: With 'You are the womb of dominion', [he puts on] a white [undergarment, and] a turban as the second.

18.14.3.a.m: Some [prescribe] three: the pāṇḍara, the tārpya, and the turban.

18.14.5.a.m: Then he purifies him with one hundred and one blades of darbha grass.

18.14.8.a.d: अङ्क्ते ऽभ्यङ्क्ते ऽश्नाति वासः परिधत्त इत्येवमनुपूर्वाण्येके समामनन्ति
18.14.8.a.m: Some traditionally teach the order in this way: he anoints [his eyes], rubs [his body], eats, [and] puts on the garment.

18.14.9.a.m: These rites are performed at the āgnīdhra [hearth].

18.14.10.a.s: apa upasparśayitvāvinno agnir ity āvido yajamānaṃ vācayan bahir udānīyaiṣa vo bharatā rājety uktvendrasya vajro 'sīti dhanur yajamānāya prayacchati
18.14.10.a.d: अप उपस्पर्शयित्वाविन्नो अग्निर् इत्य् आविदो यजमानं वाचयन् बहिर् उदानीयैष वो भरता राजेत्य् उक्त्वेन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसीति धनुर् यजमानाय प्रयच्छति
18.14.10.a.m: Having made him touch water, causing the sacrificer to recite the proclamations beginning with 'Agni is found', having led him out towards the north, and having said 'This is your king, O Bharatas', he hands the bow to the sacrificer with 'You are Indra's thunderbolt.'

18.14.11.a.m: With 'You are expellers of enemies', [he gives him] three barbed arrows.

18.14.12.a.s: pāta mā pratyañcam iti pradīyamānān anumantrayate
18.14.12.a.d: पात मा प्रत्यञ्चम् इति प्रदीयमानान् अनुमन्त्रयते
18.14.12.a.m: With 'Protect me towards the west', [the sacrificer] recites over them as they are being handed over.

18.14.13.a.s: pāta prāñcaṃ pāta pratyañcaṃ pātodañcam iti prayacchann adhvaryur japati
18.14.13.a.d: पात प्राञ्चं पात प्रत्यञ्चं पातोदञ्चम् इति प्रयच्छन्न् अध्वर्युर् जपति
18.14.13.a.m: The adhvaryu whispers while handing [them] over: 'Protect [him] towards the east; protect [him] towards the west; protect [him] towards the north.'

18.14.14.a.d: मित्रो ऽसीति दक्षिणं बाहुं यजमान उद्यच्छते ।
18.14.14.a.m: The sacrificer raises his right arm with 'You are Mitra';

18.14.16.a.m: He addresses the raised [arms] with 'Golden-colored ones'.

18.14.17.a.m: Then he causes him to step out to the [five] directions with five [formulas],

18.15.2.a.m: Or at this point he should offer [the cake] for the Maruts.

18.15.3.a.s: taṃ barhiṣadaṃ kṛtvainā vyāghraṃ pariṣasvajānāḥ siṃhaṃ hinvanti mahate saubhagāya /
18.15.3.a.d: तं बर्हिषदं कृत्वैना व्याघ्रं परिषस्वजानाः सिंहं हिन्वन्ति महते सौभगाय ।
18.15.3.a.m: Having placed it on the barhis, [he mutters:] 'Embracing this tiger, they urge the lion toward great prosperity;

18.15.3.b.s: samudraṃ na suhavaṃ tasthivāṃsaṃ marmṛjyante dvīpinamapsvantariti sphyena puroḍāśamabhicarannihanti
18.15.3.b.d: समुद्रं न सुहवं तस्थिवांसं मर्मृज्यन्ते द्वीपिनमप्स्वन्तरिति स्फ्येन पुरोडाशमभिचरन्निहन्ति
18.15.3.b.m: they groom the panther seated within the waters as an easily invoked sea'—with this he strikes down upon the sacrificial cake with the wooden sword, performing sorcery.

18.15.4.a.s: yatsphya āśliṣyati yacca pratiśīryate tadviṣṇave śipiviṣṭāya juhoti
18.15.4.a.d: यत्स्फ्य आश्लिष्यति यच्च प्रतिशीर्यते तद्विष्णवे शिपिविष्टाय जुहोति
18.15.4.a.m: Whatever adheres to the wooden sword and whatever breaks off, he offers that to Viṣṇu Śipiviṣṭa.

18.15.5.a.s: agreṇa praśāsturdhiṣṇiyaṃ khādirīmaudumbarīṃ vāsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpya somasya tviṣirasīti tasyāṃ śārdūlacarma prācīnagrīvamuttaralomāstīryāmṛtamasīti tasmiñchatamānaṃ hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya didyonmā pāhīti sauvarṇena śatamānena śatakṣareṇa śatakṛṣṇalena vā yajamānasya śīrṣannadhi nidhatte
18.15.5.a.d: अग्रेण प्रशास्तुर्धिष्णियं खादिरीमौदुम्बरीं वासन्दीं प्रतिष्ठाप्य सोमस्य त्विषिरसीति तस्यां शार्दूलचर्म प्राचीनग्रीवमुत्तरलोमास्तीर्यामृतमसीति तस्मिञ्छतमानं हिरण्यं निधाय दिद्योन्मा पाहीति सौवर्णेन शतमानेन शतक्षरेण शतकृष्णलेन वा यजमानस्य शीर्षन्नधि निधत्ते
18.15.5.a.m: Having set up a chair of khadira or udumbara wood in front of the dhiṣṇiya of the praśāstṛ, having spread a tiger skin on it with the neck to the east and the hairy side up with 'You are the splendor of Soma', having placed a gold piece weighing a hundred mānas on it with 'You are immortality', he places [another gold piece] upon the sacrificer's head with 'Protect me from the missile', either a gold [piece] weighing a hundred mānas, or one of a hundred syllables, or one weighing a hundred kṛṣṇalas.

18.15.6.a.s: tamārohanyajamāno 'veṣṭā dandaśūkā iti dakṣiṇena padā sīsaṃ paṇḍakāya pratyasyati /
18.15.6.a.d: तमारोहन्यजमानो ऽवेष्टा दन्दशूका इति दक्षिणेन पदा सीसं पण्डकाय प्रत्यस्यति ।
18.15.6.a.m: Mounting it, the sacrificer kicks away a lead [piece] with his right foot to a eunuch with 'The biters are uncoiled';

18.15.6.b.s: nirastaṃ namuceḥśira iti savyena lohitāyasaṃ keśavāpāya
18.15.6.b.d: निरस्तं नमुचेःशिर इति सव्येन लोहितायसं केशवापाय
18.15.6.b.m: with the left [foot], a copper [piece] to a barber with 'Cast away is the head of Namuci.'

18.15.7.a.m: They two throw them outside the altar ground.

18.15.8.a.s: agnaye svāheti ṣaṭ pārthāni purastād abhiṣekasya juhoti
18.15.8.a.d: अग्नये स्वाहेति षट् पार्थानि पुरस्ताद् अभिषेकस्य जुहोति
18.15.8.a.m: Before the consecration he offers the six Pārtha oblations with 'To Agni, svāhā!'

18.15.9.a.m: With 'To the earth, svāhā!', [he offers] the six aveṣṭi oblations of the beings.

18.15.10.a.s: ūrdhvabāhuṃ tiṣṭhantaṃ māhendrasya stotraṃ praty abhiṣiñcati
18.15.10.a.d: ऊर्ध्वबाहुं तिष्ठन्तं माहेन्द्रस्य स्तोत्रं प्रत्य् अभिषिञ्चति
18.15.10.a.m: He sprinkles him while he is standing with raised arms, in response to the Māhendra chant,

18.15.11.a.s: <somo rājā> \ ity abhimantrya <somasya tvā dyumnenābhiṣiñcāmi> \ iti
18.15.11.a.d: <सोमो राजा> \ इत्य् अभिमन्त्र्य <सोमस्य त्वा द्युम्नेनाभिषिञ्चामि> \ इति
18.15.11.a.m: having addressed him with 'King Soma', [and then sprinkling] with 'I consecrate you with the brilliance of Soma.'

18.16.1.a.m: The adhvaryu [sprinkles him] from the front with the palāśa [vessel].

18.16.3.a.m: the brahman from the south with the udumbara [vessel],

18.16.4.a.m: the vaiśya from the west with the aśvattha [vessel];

18.16.5.a.m: a relative [or] friend from the north with the nyagrodha [vessel].

18.16.6.a.m: He addresses him while he is being consecrated with 'You are the lord of dominion among dominions.'

18.16.7.a.d: समाववृत्रन्न् इति ये ऽभिषिच्यमानस्य लेपा व्यवस्रवन्ति
18.16.7.a.m: With 'They have rolled together', [he addresses] the drippings that flow down the one being consecrated;

18.16.9.a.s: indrasya yonir asi janadhā iti kṛṣṇaviṣāṇayā vāsāṃsi vicacṛte /
18.16.9.a.d: इन्द्रस्य योनिर् असि जनधा इति कृष्णविषाणया वासांसि विचचृते ।
18.16.9.a.m: With 'You are Indra's womb, sustaining the people', he loosens the garments with a black antelope horn,

18.16.10.a.m: He casts them onto the rubbish heap with 'Protect [me] from the sky.'

18.16.11.a.s: indrāya svāheti ṣaṭ pārthāny upariṣṭād abhiṣekasya juhoti
18.16.11.a.d: इन्द्राय स्वाहेति षट् पार्थान्य् उपरिष्टाद् अभिषेकस्य जुहोति
18.16.11.a.m: After the consecration, he offers the six Pārtha oblations with 'To Indra, svāhā!'

18.16.12.a.m: With 'To the waters, svāhā!', [he offers] the six aveṣṭi oblations of the beings.

18.16.13.a.m: Or at this point he should offer the remnant.

18.16.14.a.s: yāṃ bhāryāṃ kāmayeta rāṣṭramasyai prajā syāditi tasyā aupāsane pratihitamārambhayitvā ye pātreṣu lepā vyavasṛtāstebhyo nāmavyatiṣañjanīyau homau juhuyātprajāpate na tvadetānīti
18.16.14.a.d: यां भार्यां कामयेत राष्ट्रमस्यै प्रजा स्यादिति तस्या औपासने प्रतिहितमारम्भयित्वा ये पात्रेषु लेपा व्यवसृतास्तेभ्यो नामव्यतिषञ्जनीयौ होमौ जुहुयात्प्रजापते न त्वदेतानीति
18.16.14.a.m: For whichever wife he desires, 'May her offspring possess the kingdom', having made her touch [the oblation] placed on the aupāsana fire, he should offer out of the drippings that have flowed down into the vessels the two name-intertwining oblations with 'O Prajāpati, none other than you [pervades all these things]'.

18.16.15.a.s: asāvamuṣya putro 'muṣyā asau putra iti nāmanī vyatiṣajati
18.16.15.a.d: असावमुष्य पुत्रो ऽमुष्या असौ पुत्र इति नामनी व्यतिषजति
18.16.15.a.m: He intertwines the two names: 'So-and-so is the son of such-and-such [a woman]; so-and-so is the son of such-and-such [a woman].'

18.17.1.a.s: indrasya vajro 'sīti ratham upāvahṛtya mitrāvaruṇayos tvā praśāstroḥ praśiṣā yunajmīti praṣṭivāhinaṃ rathaṃ yunakti
18.17.1.a.d: इन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसीति रथम् उपावहृत्य मित्रावरुणयोस् त्वा प्रशास्त्रोः प्रशिषा युनज्मीति प्रष्टिवाहिनं रथं युनक्ति
18.17.1.a.m: Having brought down the chariot with, 'You are Indra's thunderbolt,' he yokes the chariot drawn by three horses with, 'By the command of Mitra and Varuṇa, the two rulers, I yoke you.'

18.17.2.a.d: विष्णोः क्रमो ऽसीति रथं यजमानो ऽभ्येति
18.17.2.a.m: With "You are the stride of Viṣṇu," the sacrificer approaches the chariot.

18.17.3.a.m: The kṣatriya who has been assigned takes hold of him from behind.

18.17.4.a.m: The brahman follows on the right with the very [verse]: "Thou hast prevailed, O thou invoked by many."

18.17.5.a.m: He sets out with: "May I conquer under the impulse of the Maruts!"

18.17.6.a.m: A noble with a bow stands in front or to the north.

18.17.7.a.s: tasmā etān iṣūn asyaty āptaṃ mana iti
18.17.7.a.d: तस्मा एतान् इषून् अस्यत्य् आप्तं मन इति
18.17.7.a.m: He discharges these arrows at him with: "The mind is obtained."

18.17.8.a.s: ekaikamutsṛjya taṃ jitvā samahamindriyeṇa vīryeṇeti pradakṣiṇamāvartate
18.17.8.a.d: एकैकमुत्सृज्य तं जित्वा समहमिन्द्रियेण वीर्येणेति प्रदक्षिणमावर्तते
18.17.8.a.m: Having shot them one by one [and] having defeated him, he turns around sunwise with: "Together with sensory power, with virility."

18.17.9.a.m: He comes to a halt where he sets out from.

18.17.10.a.m: With: "Thou art the thunderbolt of Indra," he nudges the wife and the horses with the end of the bow.

18.17.11.a.s: eṣa vajro vājasāstena nau putro vājaṃ sediti dhanuḥ patnyai prayacchati
18.17.11.a.d: एष वज्रो वाजसास्तेन नौ पुत्रो वाजं सेदिति धनुः पत्न्यै प्रयच्छति
18.17.11.a.m: With: "This thunderbolt wins booty; through it may a son conquer booty for the two of us," he hands the bow over to his wife.

18.17.12.a.s: paśūnāṃ manyurasīti vārāhī upānahāvupamucya namo mātra ityavarokṣyanpṛthivīmabhimantryāvaruhya maṇīnpratimuñcate /
18.17.12.a.d: पशूनां मन्युरसीति वाराही उपानहावुपमुच्य नमो मात्र इत्यवरोक्ष्यन्पृथिवीमभिमन्त्र्यावरुह्य मणीन्प्रतिमुञ्चते ।
18.17.12.a.m: Having put on boar-skin sandals with: "Thou art the fury of cattle," having addressed the earth with: "Homage to the mother!" as he is about to descend, having descended, he attaches amulets [to himself]:

18.17.13.a.m: Some teach [putting] the golden one in the middle.

18.17.14.a.s: agnaye gṛhapataye svāheti rathavimocanīyānhomānhutvā haṃsaḥ śuciṣaditi saha saṃgrahītrā rathavāhane rathamatyādadhāti
18.17.14.a.d: अग्नये गृहपतये स्वाहेति रथविमोचनीयान्होमान्हुत्वा हंसः शुचिषदिति सह संग्रहीत्रा रथवाहने रथमत्यादधाति
18.17.14.a.m: Having offered the chariot-releasing oblations with: "To Agni, lord of the house, svāhā," he places the chariot onto the chariot-stand together with the charioteer with: "The goose sitting in the pure."

18.17.15.a.m: When it is placed, the charioteer steps down.

18.18.1.a.d: मित्रो ऽसीति दक्षिणं बाहुं यजमान उपावहरते ।
18.18.1.a.m: The sacrificer lowers his right arm with: "Thou art Mitra";

18.18.3.a.m: He lowers his two hands into the curd-mixture for the Viśvedevas with: "Together with all the gods."

18.18.4.a.s: sadasi sanme bhūyā iti vā maitrāvaruṇīmāmikṣāmeke samāmananti
18.18.4.a.d: सदसि सन्मे भूया इति वा मैत्रावरुणीमामिक्षामेके समामनन्ति
18.18.4.a.m: Some teach [lowering them into] the curd-mixture for Mitra and Varuṇa with: "May I have a being in the assembly!"

18.18.5.a.s: agreṇāgnīdhraṃ caturapasrāvaṃ vimitaṃ viminvanti purastādunnataṃ paścānninatam
18.18.5.a.d: अग्रेणाग्नीध्रं चतुरपस्रावं विमितं विमिन्वन्ति पुरस्तादुन्नतं पश्चान्निनतम्
18.18.5.a.m: In front of the Āgnīdhra they erect a four-eaved shed, raised in the east [and] sloping downward in the west.

18.18.6.a.s: syonāsi suṣadeti tasminkhādirīmāsandīṃ pratiṣṭhāpya kṣatrasya nābhirasīti tasyāṃ kṛttyadhīvāsamāstīryāvanahani viśi mā dṛṃhetyavanahyati
18.18.6.a.d: स्योनासि सुषदेति तस्मिन्खादिरीमासन्दीं प्रतिष्ठाप्य क्षत्रस्य नाभिरसीति तस्यां कृत्त्यधीवासमास्तीर्यावनहनि विशि मा दृंहेत्यवनह्यति
18.18.6.a.m: Having set up a throne of khadira wood in it with: "Soft art thou, good to sit upon," having spread an upper-cloth of skin upon it with: "Thou art the navel of the nobility," he ties it down with: "At the binding, strengthen me among the people."

18.18.7.a.s: syonāmā sīda suṣadāmā sīdeti tāmāsādya yajamāno mā tvāhiṃsīnmā mā hiṃsīdityupaviśati
18.18.7.a.d: स्योनामा सीद सुषदामा सीदेति तामासाद्य यजमानो मा त्वाहिंसीन्मा मा हिंसीदित्युपविशति
18.18.7.a.m: Having approached it with: "Sit on the soft one, sit on the one good to sit upon," the sacrificer sits down with: "May it not harm thee; may it not harm me."

18.18.8.a.m: He addresses him as he is seated with: "He has sat down, he whose ordinance is firm."

18.18.9.a.m: The priests and the courtiers sit around him on all sides:

18.18.10.a.m: When they are seated, the king addresses the adhvaryu: "O brahma3n!"

18.18.11.a.m: The other replies: "Thou, O king, art Brahman."

18.18.12.a.m: In the same way [he addresses] the brahman, the hotṛ, and the udgātṛ.

18.18.13.a.m: The others reply with each subsequent formula.

18.18.14.a.s: indrasya vajro 'sīti sphyaṃ brahmā rājñe prayacchati /
18.18.14.a.d: इन्द्रस्य वज्रो ऽसीति स्फ्यं ब्रह्मा राज्ञे प्रयच्छति ।
18.18.14.a.m: With: "Thou art the thunderbolt of Indra," the brahman gives the wooden sword to the king;

18.18.14.b.m: The king to the deputy; the deputy to the royal chaplain;

18.18.15.a.m: They pass it on to each successive lower person,

18.18.16.a.m: With it the dice-thrower, having dug up the gaming ground [and] sprinkled it with water, should pour out the dice,

18.19.1.a.m: More than a hundred or more than a thousand made of gold.

18.19.2.a.m: Four [persons], a brāhmaṇa, a kṣatriya, a vaiśya, and a śūdra, being its team, playing for a four-year-old cow, state the rice-mess [as the stake].

18.19.3.a.m: Then the sacrificial gift for this rite is the two front draught-oxen.

18.19.5.a.s: audbhidyaṃ rājña iti tebhyaścatuḥśatānsauvarṇānakṣānudupya vijitya diśo 'bhyayaṃ rājābhūditi pañcākṣānrājñe prayacchati
18.19.5.a.d: औद्भिद्यं राज्ञ इति तेभ्यश्चतुःशतान्सौवर्णानक्षानुदुप्य विजित्य दिशो ऽभ्ययं राजाभूदिति पञ्चाक्षान्राज्ञे प्रयच्छति
18.19.5.a.m: Having scooped out four hundred golden dice from them with: "The king's victory!", [and] having won with: "This king has overcome the directions!", he hands five dice to the king.

18.19.6.a.m: The king calls those with auspicious names:

18.19.7.a.m: Having summoned them, he gives a four-cornered field to the brahman.

18.19.9.a.m: Or here he should offer the two oblations connecting the names.

18.19.10.a.m: He causes the story of Śunaḥśepa to be narrated,

18.19.10.b.m: More than a hundred or more than a thousand verses mixed with narrative stanzas.

18.19.11.a.m: Sitting on a golden cushion, the hotṛ recites.

18.19.12.a.m: Standing on two golden bundles of grass, the adhvaryu responds.

18.19.14.a.m: When the Śunaḥśepa [story] is concluded, he gives the golden cushion to the hotṛ,

18.19.14.b.m: The two golden bundles of grass to the adhvaryu,

18.19.14.c.m: And the two gold plates used at the consecration.

18.19.15.a.m: At this point, he proceeds with the [offering] for the Maruts and the one for the Viśve Devas.

18.19.16.a.m: However, the sviṣṭakṛt-offering and the iḍā are common.

18.19.17.a.m: When the iḍā has been invoked, he unties the beads and gives them to the Brahman.

18.20.1.a.m: He undertakes the rites beginning with the proceeding for the Mahendra [draught].

18.20.3.a.m: Having proceeded with the purificatory bath, he offers into the waters with: “To the child of the waters, svāhā!”

18.20.4.a.s: ūrjo naptre svāhetyantarā darbhastambe sthāṇau valmīkavapāyāṃ vā hutvāgnaye gṛhapataye svāheti pratyetya gārhapatye hutvaindrīṃ sūtavaśāmanūbandhyāmālabhate
18.20.4.a.d: ऊर्जो नप्त्रे स्वाहेत्यन्तरा दर्भस्तम्बे स्थाणौ वल्मीकवपायां वा हुत्वाग्नये गृहपतये स्वाहेति प्रत्येत्य गार्हपत्ये हुत्वैन्द्रीं सूतवशामनूबन्ध्यामालभते
18.20.4.a.m: Having offered in between into a clump of darbha, on a stump, or into a molehill with: “To the child of vigor, svāhā!”, and having returned and offered into the gārhapatya with: “To Agni, lord of the house, svāhā!”, he immolates an anūbandhyā cow, a barren cow that has calved, dedicated to Indra.

18.20.5.a.s: tasyāḥ paśupuroḍāśaṃ naivāraṃ catuṣpadyāḥ sūnāyā nirvapati
18.20.5.a.d: तस्याः पशुपुरोडाशं नैवारं चतुष्पद्याः सूनाया निर्वपति
18.20.5.a.m: For its animal-cake, he pours out [wild rice] of nīvāra grain from a four-legged plaited basket.

18.20.6.a.m: “It serves as a substitute for the cart,” so it is taught.

18.20.7.a.s: śvobhūte 'pareṇa saumikaṃ devayajanaṃ daśabhiḥ saptabhirvā saṃsṛpāṃ havirbhiryajeta /
18.20.7.a.d: श्वोभूते ऽपरेण सौमिकं देवयजनं दशभिः सप्तभिर्वा संसृपां हविर्भिर्यजेत ।
18.20.7.a.m: On the next day, behind the soma-sacrificial place, he should sacrifice with the ten or seven oblations of the Saṃsṛps:

18.20.7.b.m: “[A cake] on eight potsherds for Agni…”

18.20.8.a.m: He shifts progressively forward to each succeeding sacrificial place.

18.20.9.a.m: Where the āhavanīya of the preceding [offering] was, there is the gārhapatya of the subsequent one.

18.20.10.a.m: For the last one, the āhavanīya is in the prāgvaṃśa hall;

18.20.11.a.m: Having sacrificed with that, in the afternoon he initiates the framework of the Daśapeya.

18.20.14.a.s: apo dīkṣāyāḥ sthāne dvādaśapuṇḍarīkāṃ srajaṃ pratimuñcate
18.20.14.a.d: अपो दीक्षायाः स्थाने द्वादशपुण्डरीकां स्रजं प्रतिमुञ्चते
18.20.14.a.m: In place of the waters of consecration, he puts on a garland of twelve lotus flowers.

18.20.15.a.m: He purchases the soma with ten uncastrated yearling calves.

18.20.16.a.m: He does not bargain; he does not carry [it] around.

18.20.18.a.m: There is one consecration day and three Upasads.

18.20.19.a.m: Before the Upasads, he sets out a caru for Soma;

18.20.19.b.m: between [them], [a cake] on eight potsherds for Tvaṣṭṛ;

18.20.19.c.m: after [them], [a cake] on three potsherds for Viṣṇu.

18.20.20.a.m: For these, the grass bunch and enclosing sticks are the very same as those of the Upasads.

18.20.24.a.m: He draws water from the Sarasvatī.

18.21.1.a.m: On the next day, at the time of arranging the vessels, he sets out ten additional goblets.

18.21.2.a.m: He fills them at the time of drawing up [the soma].

18.21.3.a.s: bhakṣaṇakāle daśadaśaikaikasmiṃścamase brāhmaṇāḥ somapāḥ somaṃ bhakṣayantyā daśamātpuruṣādavicchinnasomapīthāḥ
18.21.3.a.d: भक्षणकाले दशदशैकैकस्मिंश्चमसे ब्राह्मणाः सोमपाः सोमं भक्षयन्त्या दशमात्पुरुषादविच्छिन्नसोमपीथाः
18.21.3.a.m:
At the time of partaking, ten soma-drinking Brahmins partake of the soma from each individual goblet, their lineage of soma-drinking unbroken down to the tenth generation.

He who can recount [his ancestors] down to the tenth generation is eligible to partake.

18.21.4.a.s: ā daśamātpuruṣādanvākhyāyaṃ sa bhakṣasya kartā bhavati
18.21.4.a.d: आ दशमात्पुरुषादन्वाख्यायं स भक्षस्य कर्ता भवति

18.21.5.a.m: A hundred soma-drinking Brahmins glide into the sadas.

18.21.6.a.m: At the time of the sacrificial gifts, he gives two gold mirrors to the adhvaryu,

18.21.6.b.m: a golden garland to the udgātṛ,

18.21.6.c.m: a gold plate to the hotṛ, as handed down in the sacred text.

18.21.7.b.m: He gives [a cow] that appears to be miscarrying to the unnetṛ,

18.21.7.g.m: [and] a one-horse cart loaded with barley to the acchāvāka.

18.21.8.a.m: Having offered the daśāmaveṣṭi, he concludes [the rite].

18.21.9.a.m: There are five [oblations]: “[A cake] on eight potsherds for Agni…”

18.21.10.a.s: tayā brāhmaṇo rājanyo vaiśyo vā tejaskāmo yajeta
18.21.10.a.d: तया ब्राह्मणो राजन्यो वैश्यो वा तेजस्कामो यजेत
18.21.10.a.m: With it, a Brahmin, a nobleman, or a Vaiśya desiring spiritual luster should sacrifice.

18.21.11.a.s: yadi brāhmaṇo yajeta bārhaspatyaṃ madhye kṛtvāhutimāhutiṃ hutvā tamabhighārayet /
18.21.11.a.d: यदि ब्राह्मणो यजेत बार्हस्पत्यं मध्ये कृत्वाहुतिमाहुतिं हुत्वा तमभिघारयेत् ।
18.21.11.a.m: If a Brahmin sacrifices, he should place [the oblation] for Bṛhaspati in the middle, and after making each oblation, he should baste it [with clarified butter];

18.21.11.c.m: if a Vaiśya, [the oblation] for the Viśve Devas.

18.21.12.a.m: In the afternoon, he should sacrifice with an animal sacrifice of two victims.

18.21.13.a.m: He immolates a pregnant cow with dewlaps on the neck dedicated to Aditi,

18.21.13.b.m: [and] a dappled four-year-old heifer dedicated to the Maruts.

18.21.14.a.m: For the one dedicated to Aditi, he calls for the prompt aloud;

18.21.14.b.m: he proceeds silently for the one dedicated to the Maruts.

18.21.15.a.m: The call and the response are [performed] silently.

18.21.16.a.m: On the next day, he sets out the three-oblation offering of the Satyadhūtas:

18.21.16.b.m: “A cake on twelve potsherds for the Aśvins and Pūṣan…”

18.21.17.a.m: A bow with three arrows and a dry waterskin are the sacrificial gift.

18.22.1.a.m: A staff and boar-skin sandals, say some.

18.22.2.a.s: daṇḍo vā śuṣko vā dṛtirjaradupānahau vā
18.22.2.a.d: दण्डो वा शुष्को वा दृतिर्जरदुपानहौ वा
18.22.2.a.m: Or a staff, or a dry waterskin, or old sandals.

18.22.3.a.m: Having made them bathe, he sends [messengers] to the neighboring kings.

18.22.4.a.m: He announces: “I have been consecrated; I have become king.”

18.22.5.a.m: In the afternoon, he sacrifices with the six Prayuj offerings,

18.22.6.a.m: The right-hand ox of the chariot-carrier is the sacrificial gift.

18.22.7.a.m: The next day, [he sacrifices] with the latter six.

18.22.8.a.m: The left-hand ox of the chariot-carrier is the sacrificial gift.

18.22.9.a.m: Having offered the agnihotra for a year, he sacrifices with the Keśavapanīya Atirātra.

18.22.10.a.s: ye keśinaḥ prathamāḥ sattramāsateti vapanapravādā mantrāḥ
18.22.10.a.d: ये केशिनः प्रथमाः सत्त्रमासतेति वपनप्रवादा मन्त्राः
18.22.10.a.m: “Those hairy ones who first sat at the sattra”—these are the mantras mentioning hair-shaving.

18.22.11.a.m: With those mentioning the beginning, he has [the hair] shaved from the beginning;

18.22.11.b.m: with those mentioning the end, at the end.

18.22.12.a.m: Immediately afterward, he sacrifices with the Vyuṣṭi two-day rite.

18.22.13.a.m: The Agniṣṭoma is the first day;

18.22.14.a.m: The first day is on the full-moon day;

18.22.15.a.m: Or the first day is on the new-moon day,

18.22.16.a.s: āpūryamāṇapakṣasya vā ye puṇye ahanī syātām
18.22.16.a.d: आपूर्यमाणपक्षस्य वा ये पुण्ये अहनी स्याताम्
18.22.16.a.m: Or on whichever two days of the waxing half of the month are auspicious.

18.22.17.a.m: They seize five of the eleven animals on the first day,

18.22.18.a.m: The Kṣatradhṛti is an Agniṣṭoma with the Triṣṭoma chant, having five terminations.

18.22.21.a.m: Having sacrificed with it, he should sacrifice with the Sautrāmaṇī,

18.22.21.b.m: or with the curd mixture for Mitra and Varuṇa.

18.22.22.a.m: The days have separate concluding baths, except for the very first [day] of a two-day rite.

19.1.1.a.s: tryahe purastātsīsena klībācchaṣpāṇi krītvā kṣaume vāsasyupanahya nidhāya sautrāmaṇyāstantraṃ prakramayati
19.1.1.a.d: त्र्यहे पुरस्तात्सीसेन क्लीबाच्छष्पाणि क्रीत्वा क्षौमे वासस्युपनह्य निधाय सौत्रामण्यास्तन्त्रं प्रक्रमयति
19.1.1.a.m: Three days beforehand, having bought young barley sprout with lead from a eunuch, tied it in a linen garment, and set it down, he begins the procedure of the Sautrāmaṇī.

19.1.2.a.m: Its ritual is like that of the independent animal sacrifice.

19.1.3.a.s: agnīnanvādhāya vedaṃ kṛtvāgnīnparistīrya pāṇiprakṣālanādi karma pratipadyate
19.1.3.a.d: अग्नीनन्वाधाय वेदं कृत्वाग्नीन्परिस्तीर्य पाणिप्रक्षालनादि कर्म प्रतिपद्यते
19.1.3.a.m: Having added fuel to the fires, made the grass broom, and strewn grass around the fires, he proceeds with the work beginning with washing the hands.

19.1.4.a.m: He sets out the vessels as needed,

19.1.4.b.m: and a pot in place of the pot-sherds.

19.1.5.a.d: निर्वपणकाले ऽश्विभ्यां सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे प्रभूतान्व्रीहीन्निर्वपति
19.1.5.a.m: At the time of pouring out the offerings, he pours out abundant paddy for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector.

19.1.6.a.m: The procedure for the caru has been explained.

19.1.7.a.s: śrapayitvāgreṇa gārhapatyamavaṭaṃ khātvā tasminsurāyāḥ kalpena surāṃ saṃdadhāti
19.1.7.a.d: श्रपयित्वाग्रेण गार्हपत्यमवटं खात्वा तस्मिन्सुरायाः कल्पेन सुरां संदधाति
19.1.7.a.m: Having cooked [it] and dug a pit in front of the gārhapatya, he brews liquor therein according to the ritual of liquor.

19.1.9.a.s: svādvīṃ tvā svāduneti śaṣpaiḥ surāṃ saṃsṛjati
19.1.9.a.d: स्वाद्वीं त्वा स्वादुनेति शष्पैः सुरां संसृजति
19.1.9.a.m: With [the mantra]: “Thee, the sweet one, with the sweet,” he mixes the liquor with young barley sprouts.

19.1.10.a.m: Mixed, it sits for three nights.

19.1.13.a.m: he accomplishes the requirements with the one made beforehand.

19.1.14.a.m: “He sacrifices in one third of the altar ground of a Soma sacrifice,” so it is known [from the Brāhmaṇa].

19.1.15.a.s: uttaravedyāṃ kriyamāṇāyāṃ pratiprasthātā cātvālātpurīṣamāhṛtya dakṣiṇenottaravediṃ kharaṃ kṛtvāgreṇānvāhāryapacanaṃ surāgrahārthaṃ dvitīyaṃ kharaṃ karoti
19.1.15.a.d: उत्तरवेद्यां क्रियमाणायां प्रतिप्रस्थाता चात्वालात्पुरीषमाहृत्य दक्षिणेनोत्तरवेदिं खरं कृत्वाग्रेणान्वाहार्यपचनं सुराग्रहार्थं द्वितीयं खरं करोति
19.1.15.a.m: While the high altar is being prepared, the pratiprasthātṛ brings loose earth from the cātvāla pit, makes a mound south of the high altar, and makes a second mound in front of the anvāhāryapacana for the draughts of liquor.

19.1.16.a.s: agnau praṇīyamāne pratiprasthātā dakṣiṇāgneragnimāhṛtya dakṣiṇenottaravediṃ khare nyupyopasamādadhāti
19.1.16.a.d: अग्नौ प्रणीयमाने प्रतिप्रस्थाता दक्षिणाग्नेरग्निमाहृत्य दक्षिणेनोत्तरवेदिं खरे न्युप्योपसमादधाति
19.1.16.a.m: While the fire is being brought forward, the pratiprasthātṛ, having taken fire from the southern fire, pours it out on the mound south of the high altar and adds fuel to it.

19.1.17.a.s: pātrasaṃsādanakāle 'śvibhyāṃ sarasvatyā indrāya sutrāmṇe trīni pātrāṇi prayunakti /
19.1.17.a.d: पात्रसंसादनकाले ऽश्विभ्यां सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे त्रीनि पात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति ।
19.1.17.a.m: At the time of arranging the vessels, he sets out three vessels for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector,

19.1.17.b.m: a basin, a hair strainer, a falcon-leaf [strainer], and cooking vessels.

19.1.18.a.s: prāk paśūpākaraṇātkṛtvodbhidya surāṃ brāhmaṇasya mūrdhankhare vā sādayitvā punātu te parisrutamiti vālamayena pavitreṇa surāṃ pāvayati
19.1.18.a.d: प्राक् पशूपाकरणात्कृत्वोद्भिद्य सुरां ब्राह्मणस्य मूर्धन्खरे वा सादयित्वा पुनातु ते परिस्रुतमिति वालमयेन पवित्रेण सुरां पावयति
19.1.18.a.m: Prior to bringing up the victim, having uncovered the liquor and placed it on the head of a Brahmin or on the mound, he purifies the liquor with a strainer of hair, with [the mantra]: “May it purify thy fermenting liquor.”

19.1.19.a.m: “Forward hath soma run beyond,” in the case of one who has vomited soma;

19.1.19.b.m: “Backward hath soma run beyond,” in the case of one purged by soma.

19.1.20.a.m: Having placed the purified [liquor] in its proper place, he brings up the animal victims at the single sacrificial post:

19.2.1.a.s: āśvinaḥ dhūmramajaṃ sārasvataṃ meṣamaindramṛṣabhaṃ vṛṣṇiṃ vā bārhaspatyam
19.2.1.a.d: आश्विनः धूम्रमजं सारस्वतं मेषमैन्द्रमृषभं वृष्णिं वा बार्हस्पत्यम्
19.2.1.a.m: a dusky he-goat for the Aśvins, a ram for Sarasvatī, and a bull for Indra, or a ram for Bṛhaspati,

19.2.2.a.m: as the fourth for one who has vomited soma or one purged by soma.

19.2.3.a.s: hutāsu vapāsu niṣkamṛṣabhaṃ sātvarīṃ ca vaḍabāṃ dadāti
19.2.3.a.d: हुतासु वपासु निष्कमृषभं सात्वरीं च वडबां ददाति
19.2.3.a.m: When the omenta have been offered, he gives a gold ornament, a bull, and a fast mare.

19.2.4.a.m: They explain [sātvarī as] one that has strayed and returned.

19.2.5.a.m: A mare with a foal is the sacrificial gift;

19.2.6.a.m: and gold and silver plates weighing a hundred mānas, say some.

19.2.7.a.m: Having cleansed themselves at the cātvāla pit, they draw the draughts of liquor on the western mound.

19.2.8.a.s: kuvidaṅgeti sarveṣāmekā purorugekā puro'nuvākyaikaḥ praiṣa ekā yājyā
19.2.8.a.d: कुविदङ्गेति सर्वेषामेका पुरोरुगेका पुरोऽनुवाक्यैकः प्रैष एका याज्या
19.2.8.a.m: With [the verse beginning] 'kuvid aṅga', there is one introductory verse, one invitatory verse, one ritual call, and one consecratory verse for all [the draughts].

19.2.9.a.m: With: 'You are taken with a base; I take you, who are uninjured, through an uninjured [strainer], dear to the Aśvins', the adhvaryu takes the draught for the Aśvins.

19.2.9.b.s: etenaiva sarasvatyā iti sārasvataṃ pratiprasthātāgnīdhro vā /
19.2.9.b.d: एतेनैव सरस्वत्या इति सारस्वतं प्रतिप्रस्थाताग्नीध्रो वा ।
19.2.9.b.m: With the very same [formula, but saying] 'for Sarasvatī', the pratiprasthātṛ or the agnīdh [takes] the draught for Sarasvatī.

19.2.9.c.m: With: '...for Indra', the brahman or the sacrificer [takes] the draught for Indra.

19.2.10.a.m: He mixes the draught for the Aśvins with groats of kvala-jujube and with lion's hairs.

19.2.10.b.m: The draught for Sarasvatī with groats of badara-jujube and tiger's hairs.

19.2.10.c.m: The draught for Indra with groats of karkandhu-jujube and wolf's hairs.

19.2.11.a.m: In the absence of these, the adhvaryu should meditate mentally on two lions;

19.2.12.a.s: sarvāñchyenapattreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yoniriti yathādevataṃ yathāyatanaṃ sādayati
19.2.12.a.d: सर्वाञ्छ्येनपत्त्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिरिति यथादेवतं यथायतनं सादयति
19.2.12.a.m: Having wiped all around them with an eagle's feather, he sets them down with: 'This is your seat...', according to each deity and according to each place.

19.2.14.a.m: Having taken the clarified butter portions for the animal sacrifice, they should take the draughts.

19.2.15.a.m: Then he apportions the sacrificial cakes:

19.2.15.b.m: having apportioned the animal-cake of the victim for Bṛhaspati, [he apportions] the eleven-pot-sherd cake for Indra, and so on.

19.2.16.a.m: Taking those three [draughts], they proceed with the draughts.

19.2.17.a.m: To those who take them, the adhvaryu issues the ritual call:

19.2.18.a.s: aśvibhyāṃ sarasvatyā indrāya sutrāmṇe somānāṃ surāmṇāmanubrūhi /
19.2.18.a.d: अश्विभ्यां सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे सोमानां सुराम्णामनुब्रूहि ।
19.2.18.a.m: 'Recite for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector, for the somas and the surās!'

19.2.18.b.s: aśvibhyāṃ sarasvatyā indrāya sutrāmṇe somānāṃ surāmṇāṃ preṣyeti saṃpraiṣau /
19.2.18.b.d: अश्विभ्यां सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे सोमानां सुराम्णां प्रेष्येति संप्रैषौ ।
19.2.18.b.m: 'Urge for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector, for the somas and the surās!'—these are the two ritual calls;

19.2.18.c.m: or: 'Urge for the somas and the surās that have been set forward!'

19.2.19.a.m: 'You two, O Aśvins, [drank] surā together with the Asura Namuci;

19.2.19.b.m: drinking intensely, O lords of brilliance, you aided Indra in his deeds.'

19.2.19.c.m: 'Like parents aiding a son, both Aśvins aided Indra by deed and wonders,

19.2.19.d.s: yatsurāmaṃ vyapibaḥ śacībhiḥ sarasvatī tvā maghavannabhīṣṇāditi sarvadevatye yājyānuvākye bhavataḥ
19.2.19.d.d: यत्सुरामं व्यपिबः शचीभिः सरस्वती त्वा मघवन्नभीष्णादिति सर्वदेवत्ये याज्यानुवाक्ये भवतः
19.2.19.d.m: when you, O bounteous one, drank surā by your powers and Sarasvatī healed you'—these are the invitatory and consecratory verses addressed to all deities.

19.3.1.a.m: He offers the secondary offering with: 'O Agni, enjoy the soma!'

19.3.2.a.s: ahāvyagne havirāsye te srucīva ghṛtaṃ camū iva somaḥ /
19.3.2.a.d: अहाव्यग्ने हविरास्ये ते स्रुचीव घृतं चमू इव सोमः ।
19.3.2.a.m: 'The oblation, O Agni, has been poured into your mouth, as ghee into the ladle, as soma into the vats;

19.3.2.b.s: vājasaniṃ rayimasme suvīraṃ praśataṃ dhehi yaśasaṃ bṛhantam //
19.3.2.b.d: वाजसनिं रयिमस्मे सुवीरं प्रशतं धेहि यशसं बृहन्तम् ॥
19.3.2.b.m: confer upon us prize-winning wealth, rich in good heroes, renowned, great, and celebrated!'

19.3.2.c.s: aysminnaśvāsa ṛṣabhāsa ukṣaṇo vaśā meṣā avasṛṣṭāsa āhutāḥ /
19.3.2.c.d: अय्स्मिन्नश्वास ऋषभास उक्षणो वशा मेषा अवसृष्टास आहुताः ।
19.3.2.c.m: 'In whom horses, bulls, oxen, barren cows, and sheep are released and offered;

19.3.2.d.s: kīlālape somapṛṣṭhāya vedhase hṛdā matiṃ janaye cārumagnaya iti hutāṃ hūyamānāṃ vā yajamāno 'numantrayate
19.3.2.d.d: कीलालपे सोमपृष्ठाय वेधसे हृदा मतिं जनये चारुमग्नय इति हुतां हूयमानां वा यजमानो ऽनुमन्त्रयते
19.3.2.d.m: for Agni, who drinks sweet drink, whose back is soma, the dispenser, I produce a pleasing thought from the heart'—with these [verses] the sacrificer follows [the oblation] with a mantra, either when offered or while being offered.

19.3.3.a.m: He should hire a Brahmin who will be the drinker of the residue.

19.3.4.a.s: nānā hi vāṃ devahitaṃ sado mitaṃ mā saṃsṛkṣāthāṃ parame vyoman /
19.3.4.a.d: नाना हि वां देवहितं सदो मितं मा संसृक्षाथां परमे व्योमन् ।
19.3.4.a.m: 'For separately have your seats, arranged for the gods, been measured out; do not mingle in the highest heaven!

19.3.4.b.s: surā tvamasi śuṣmiṇī soma eṣa mā mā hiṃsīḥ svāṃ yonimāviśan //
19.3.4.b.d: सुरा त्वमसि शुष्मिणी सोम एष मा मा हिंसीः स्वां योनिमाविशन् ॥
19.3.4.b.m: You are spirited surā; this here is soma. Do not injure me as you enter your own seat!'

19.3.4.c.s: yadatra śiṣṭaṃ rasinaḥ sutasya yadindro apibacchacībhiḥ /
19.3.4.c.d: यदत्र शिष्टं रसिनः सुतस्य यदिन्द्रो अपिबच्छचीभिः ।
19.3.4.c.m: 'What is left here of the savoury pressed juice, which Indra drank through his powers,

19.3.4.d.s: ahaṃ tadasya manasā śivena somaṃ rājānamiha bhakṣayāmīti vā svayaṃ pibet
19.3.4.d.d: अहं तदस्य मनसा शिवेन सोमं राजानमिह भक्षयामीति वा स्वयं पिबेत्
19.3.4.d.m: that King Soma belonging to him do I consume here with a benevolent mind'—with this [formula] he may himself drink it;

19.3.5.a.s: dve srutī aśṛṇavaṃ pitṝṇāmahaṃ devānāmuta martyānām /
19.3.5.a.d: द्वे स्रुती अशृणवं पितॄणामहं देवानामुत मर्त्यानाम् ।
19.3.5.a.m: or with: 'Two paths have I heard of for the ancestors, for gods, and for mortals;

19.3.5.b.s: tābhyāmidaṃ viśvaṃ bhuvanaṃ sametyantarā pūrvamaparaṃ ca ketumiti vā valmīkavapāyāmavanayet
19.3.5.b.d: ताभ्यामिदं विश्वं भुवनं समेत्यन्तरा पूर्वमपरं च केतुमिति वा वल्मीकवपायामवनयेत्
19.3.5.b.m: by these all this world meets together, between the eastern and the western beacon'—with this he may pour it down into the mound of an anthill.

19.3.6.a.d: दक्षिणे ऽग्नौ शतातृणां स्थालीं प्रबद्धां धारयति
19.3.6.a.m: He holds a perforated pot suspended over the southern fire.

19.3.7.a.s: tasyā bila udīcīnadaśaṃ pavitraṃ vitatya yanme manaḥ parāgatamiti tasmiñchatamānaṃ hiraṇyaṃ nidhāya somapratīkāḥ pitarastṛpṇuteti tasminsurāśeṣamānayati /
19.3.7.a.d: तस्या बिल उदीचीनदशं पवित्रं वितत्य यन्मे मनः परागतमिति तस्मिञ्छतमानं हिरण्यं निधाय सोमप्रतीकाः पितरस्तृप्णुतेति तस्मिन्सुराशेषमानयति ।
19.3.7.a.m:
Having spread over its opening a strainer with fringe turned northward, and placing on it a gold piece weighing one hundred measures with: 'That mind of mine which has departed...', he pours into it the residue of the surā with: 'O ancestors who present the appearance of soma, be satisfied!';

or with: 'O ancestors who present the appearance of soma, rejoice! May we attain the full life-span established by the gods!'

19.3.7.b.s: somapratīkāḥ pitaro madantāṃ vyaśema devahitaṃ yadāyuḥ /
19.3.7.b.d: सोमप्रतीकाः पितरो मदन्तां व्यशेम देवहितं यदायुः ।

19.3.7.c.s: indrapīto vicakṣaṇo vyaśema devahitaṃ yadāyuriti vā
19.3.7.c.d: इन्द्रपीतो विचक्षणो व्यशेम देवहितं यदायुरिति वा
19.3.7.c.m: or: 'Drunk by Indra, far-seeing, may we attain the full life-span established by the gods!'

19.3.8.a.m: As it flows down, they stand by it, each following in order, reciting three verses to Soma associated with the Fathers;

19.3.9.a.s: tvaṃ soma pracikita ityetā āmnātā bhavanti
19.3.9.a.d: त्वं सोम प्रचिकित इत्येता आम्नाता भवन्ति
19.3.9.a.m: these are handed down [in the canon] as: 'You, O Soma, knowledgeable...'

19.3.11.a.s: yadagne kavyavāhaneti kāvyavāhanībhirdakṣiṇe 'gnau śatātṛṇāṃ pratiṣṭhāpayati yadi brāhmaṇo yajate
19.3.11.a.d: यदग्ने कव्यवाहनेति काव्यवाहनीभिर्दक्षिणे ऽग्नौ शतातृणां प्रतिष्ठापयति यदि ब्राह्मणो यजते
19.3.11.a.m: With the verses addressed to Agni Kavyavāhana, beginning 'yad agne kavyavāhana', he sets the perforated pot firmly down over the southern fire, if a Brahmin is sacrificing.

19.4.1.a.s: atha yadi rājanyo vaiśyo vā nādriyeta dakṣiṇamagniṃ praṇayitum
19.4.1.a.d: अथ यदि राजन्यो वैश्यो वा नाद्रियेत दक्षिणमग्निं प्रणयितुम्
19.4.1.a.m: Now, if he is a nobleman or a Vaiśya, he should not pay heed to bringing forward the southern fire;

19.4.2.a.m: he should sit consuming this residue of surā himself as his ritual food.

19.4.3.a.s: bārhaspatyasya paśupuroḍāśena pracarya paśubhiḥ pracarya puroḍāśaiḥ pracarati
19.4.3.a.d: बार्हस्पत्यस्य पशुपुरोडाशेन प्रचर्य पशुभिः प्रचर्य पुरोडाशैः प्रचरति
19.4.3.a.m: Having proceeded with the animal-cake of the victim for Bṛhaspati and with the animal victims, he proceeds with the sacrificial cakes.

19.4.4.a.m: The Sviṣṭakṛt offering and the iḍā, however, are common.

19.4.5.a.m: He begins the animal ritual procedure starting with: 'Agnīdh, bring the coals for the secondary offerings!'

19.4.6.a.m: They go down to the purificatory bath with the heart-spits, the fermentation dregs, and the vessels.

19.4.7.a.m: He disposes of the fermentation dregs in the manner of the pressed soma husks.

19.4.8.a.m: They refer to sediment as fermentation dregs.

19.4.9.a.s: yaste deva varuṇa gāyatracchandāḥ pāśas taṃ ta etenāvayaje svāhety āśvinapātram avabhṛthe pravidhyati /
19.4.9.a.d: यस्ते देव वरुण गायत्रच्छन्दाः पाशस् तं त एतेनावयजे स्वाहेत्य् आश्विनपात्रम् अवभृथे प्रविध्यति ।
19.4.9.a.m: With: 'Whatever noose of yours, O god Varuṇa, has the gāyatrī metre, that [noose] of yours I cast off with this, svāhā!', he throws the vessel of the Aśvins into the purificatory bath;

19.4.9.b.m: with the very same [formula, but saying] '...has the triṣṭubh metre', [he throws the vessel] of Sarasvatī;

19.4.9.c.m: saying '...has the jagatī metre', [the vessel] of Indra;

19.4.9.d.s: anuṣṭupchandā iti sataṃ vālasrāvaṃ śyenapattraṃ ca /
19.4.9.d.d: अनुष्टुप्छन्दा इति सतं वालस्रावं श्येनपत्त्रं च ।
19.4.9.d.m: saying '...has the anuṣṭubh metre', the broad vessel, the hair-strainer, and the eagle's feather;

19.4.9.e.m: saying '...has the paṅkti metre', the spits.

19.4.11.a.m: With it he should cause one who vomits soma, one through whom soma purges, an exiled king, one being exiled, one being consecrated, or one who has consecrated himself, to sacrifice.

19.4.12.b.m: Or one practicing sorcery, one desiring food, one desiring offspring, or one desiring cattle [should sacrifice].

19.4.13.a.m: It is taught in all consecrations.

19.4.14.a.s: tayā brāhmaṇo rājanyo vaiśyo vā tejaskāmo yajeta
19.4.14.a.d: तया ब्राह्मणो राजन्यो वैश्यो वा तेजस्कामो यजेत
19.4.14.a.m: With it a brāhmaṇa, a rājanya, or a vaiśya desiring splendour should sacrifice.

19.5.1.a.m: Now then we shall explain the Kaukikī [Sautrāmaṇī].

19.5.3.a.m: At the time of measuring out [the offerings], he seizes an animal for Indra.

19.5.7.a.s: purastādeva kālāyasena kālānuśātanena kālena tasareṇa pakṣmaṇā vrīhiyavaśyāmākānkrītvā kṣaume vāsasyupanaddhānvrīhīṃstokmāni kurvanti /
19.5.7.a.d: पुरस्तादेव कालायसेन कालानुशातनेन कालेन तसरेण पक्ष्मणा व्रीहियवश्यामाकान्क्रीत्वा क्षौमे वासस्युपनद्धान्व्रीहींस्तोक्मानि कुर्वन्ति ।
19.5.7.a.m: Well beforehand, having bought rice, barley, and millet with dark iron, with a dark cutting implement, with a black shuttle, and with a lash, and having tied the rice in a linen cloth, they make sprouts.

19.5.8.a.s: cūrṇāni tāni dadhnodaśvitā vā saṃsṛjya darbhaiḥ paritaṃsya nidadhāti
19.5.8.a.d: चूर्णानि तानि दध्नोदश्विता वा संसृज्य दर्भैः परितंस्य निदधाति
19.5.8.a.m: Having mixed their meal with curd or buttermilk, and having wrapped it around with darbha grass, he places it.

19.5.10.a.m: Coarse meal of the very same [grains], sprinkled with scum—that is nagnahu.

19.5.11.a.s: śyāmākānsaktūnkṛtvā surāyāḥ saṃdhānakāle tokmairmāsareṇa nagnahunā ca surāṃ saṃsṛjya saktūnāṃ tṛtīyena parikīrya parīto ṣiñcatā sutamityekasyā gordugdhena pariṣicyāpareṇa tṛtīyena parikīryaitayaiva dvayordugdhenāpareṇa tṛtīyena parikīryaitayaiva tisṛṇāṃ dugdhena tisro rātrīḥ saṃsṛṣṭā vasati
19.5.11.a.d: श्यामाकान्सक्तून्कृत्वा सुरायाः संधानकाले तोक्मैर्मासरेण नग्नहुना च सुरां संसृज्य सक्तूनां तृतीयेन परिकीर्य परीतो षिञ्चता सुतमित्येकस्या गोर्दुग्धेन परिषिच्यापरेण तृतीयेन परिकीर्यैतयैव द्वयोर्दुग्धेनापरेण तृतीयेन परिकीर्यैतयैव तिसृणां दुग्धेन तिस्रो रात्रीः संसृष्टा वसति
19.5.11.a.m: Having made groats of the millet, at the time of fermenting the surā, having mixed the surā with the sprouts, with the māsara, and with the nagnahu, having scattered around a third of the groats, having poured [around] with the milk of one cow with "Poured around, pour the pressed [soma]...", having scattered around another third and [poured] with this very [formula] with the milk of two [cows], having scattered around another third and [poured] with this very [formula] with the milk of three [cows], mixed together, it rests for three nights.

19.6.1.a.m: Some teach a kārotara in place of a pit.

19.6.2.a.m: It is made of split cane, bound with leather.

19.6.3.a.m: Into it he sets a spout-mouthed vessel of split cane.

19.6.4.a.m: Its opening is covered with leather.

19.6.5.a.m: What flows out into it, that becomes parisrut.

19.6.6.a.s: pātrasaṃsādanakāle 'śvibhyāṃ sarasvatyā indrāya sutrāmṇe trīṇi pātrāṇi prayunakti
19.6.6.a.d: पात्रसंसादनकाले ऽश्विभ्यां सरस्वत्या इन्द्राय सुत्राम्णे त्रीणि पात्राणि प्रयुनक्ति
19.6.6.a.m: At the time of placing the vessels, he sets out three vessels: for the Aśvins, for Sarasvatī, and for Indra the Good Protector.

19.6.7.a.m: Three [kinds of] groats—of barley, wheat, and upavāka—in a falcon-leaf, in a hair strainer, or in a wooden trough.

19.6.8.a.m: The filter of the adhvaryu is made of goat and sheep hair.

19.6.8.b.m: [The filter] of the pratiprasthātṛ is made of cow and horse [hair].

19.6.9.a.m: Having poured out ghee, the adhvaryu pours out abundant milk into a wooden trough.

19.6.11.a.m: Having purified the ghee, he purifies the milk with the hair strainer.

19.6.12.a.m: With "Eastward the soma has run beyond..." for one who vomits soma.

19.6.12.b.m: With "Westward the soma has run beyond..." for one through whom soma purges.

19.6.13.a.s: brahma kṣatraṃ pavata iti surāṃ pratiprasthātā
19.6.13.a.d: ब्रह्म क्षत्रं पवत इति सुरां प्रतिप्रस्थाता
19.6.13.a.m: The pratiprasthātṛ [purifies] the surā with "The sacred lore and the ruling power are purified..."

19.6.14.a.m: Having taken the clarified butter for the animals, the adhvaryu draws the milk draughts.

19.6.15.a.s: kuvidaṅgeti sarveṣāmekā purorugekā puro'nuvākyaikaḥ praiṣa ekā yājyā
19.6.15.a.d: कुविदङ्गेति सर्वेषामेका पुरोरुगेका पुरोऽनुवाक्यैकः प्रैष एका याज्या
19.6.15.a.m: With "Truly indeed..." there is for all [three] one preliminary verse, one invitatory verse, one ritual call, and one consecratory verse.

19.7.1.a.s: upayāmagṛhīto 'syaśvibhyāṃ tvā juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvā yavasaktubhiḥ śrītvā pavitreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yonistejase tveti sādayitvopayāmagṛhīto 'si sarasvatyai tvā juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvā godhūmasaktubhiḥ śrītvā pavitreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yonirvīryāya tveti sādayitvopayāmagṛhīto 'sīndrāya tvā sutrāmṇe juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvopavākāsaktubhiḥ śrītvā pavitreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yonirbalāya tveti sādayitvottarairyathāliṅgamupatiṣṭhate
19.7.1.a.d: उपयामगृहीतो ऽस्यश्विभ्यां त्वा जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वा यवसक्तुभिः श्रीत्वा पवित्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिस्तेजसे त्वेति सादयित्वोपयामगृहीतो ऽसि सरस्वत्यै त्वा जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वा गोधूमसक्तुभिः श्रीत्वा पवित्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिर्वीर्याय त्वेति सादयित्वोपयामगृहीतो ऽसीन्द्राय त्वा सुत्राम्णे जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वोपवाकासक्तुभिः श्रीत्वा पवित्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिर्बलाय त्वेति सादयित्वोत्तरैर्यथालिङ्गमुपतिष्ठते
19.7.1.a.m: Having drawn with "You are taken with a receptacle; I take you pleasing to the Aśvins," having mixed it with barley groats, having wiped it around with the filter, and having set it down with "This is your cradle; for splendour you!", having drawn with "You are taken with a receptacle; I take you pleasing to Sarasvatī," having mixed it with wheat groats, having wiped it around with the filter, and having set it down with "This is your cradle; for virility you!", having drawn with "You are taken with a receptacle; I take you pleasing to Indra the Good Protector," having mixed it with upavāka groats, having wiped it around with the filter, and having set it down with "This is your cradle; for strength you!", he attends [them] with the subsequent [verses] according to their characteristic marks.

19.7.2.a.s: surāyāṃ vāla ānīyamānāyāṃ dhārāyāḥ pratiprasthātā surāgrahāngṛhṇāti
19.7.2.a.d: सुरायां वाल आनीयमानायां धारायाः प्रतिप्रस्थाता सुराग्रहान्गृह्णाति
19.7.2.a.m: While the surā is being brought through the hair strainer in a stream, the pratiprasthātṛ draws the surā draughts.

19.7.3.a.s: nānā hi vāṃ devahitaṃ sadaḥ kṛtamiti sarveṣāmekā purorugekā puro'nuvākyaikaḥ praiṣa ekā yājyā
19.7.3.a.d: नाना हि वां देवहितं सदः कृतमिति सर्वेषामेका पुरोरुगेका पुरोऽनुवाक्यैकः प्रैष एका याज्या
19.7.3.a.m: With "Distinct indeed for the two of you has the seat pleasing to the gods been made..." there is for all [three] one preliminary verse, one invitatory verse, one ritual call, and one consecratory verse.

19.7.4.a.s: upayāmagṛhīto 'syāśvinaṃ tejo 'śvibhyāṃ tvā juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvā pavitreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yonirmodāya tveti sādayati
19.7.4.a.d: उपयामगृहीतो ऽस्याश्विनं तेजो ऽश्विभ्यां त्वा जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वा पवित्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिर्मोदाय त्वेति सादयति
19.7.4.a.m: Having drawn with "You are taken with a receptacle; splendour of the Aśvins, I take you pleasing to the Aśvins," and having wiped it around with the filter, he sets it down with "This is your cradle; for joy you!"

19.7.5.a.s: upapayāmagṛhīto 'si sārasvataṃ vīryaṃ sarasvatyai tvā juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvā pavitreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yonirānandāya tveti sādayati
19.7.5.a.d: उपपयामगृहीतो ऽसि सारस्वतं वीर्यं सरस्वत्यै त्वा जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वा पवित्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिरानन्दाय त्वेति सादयति
19.7.5.a.m: Having drawn with "You are taken with a receptacle; virility of Sarasvatī, I take you pleasing to Sarasvatī," and having wiped it around with the filter, he sets it down with "This is your cradle; for delight you!"

19.7.6.a.s: upayāmagṛhīto 'syaindraṃ balamindrāya tvā sutrāmṇe juṣṭaṃ gṛhṇāmīti gṛhītvā pavitreṇa parimṛjyaiṣa te yonirmahase tveti sādayati
19.7.6.a.d: उपयामगृहीतो ऽस्यैन्द्रं बलमिन्द्राय त्वा सुत्राम्णे जुष्टं गृह्णामीति गृहीत्वा पवित्रेण परिमृज्यैष ते योनिर्महसे त्वेति सादयति
19.7.6.a.m: Having drawn with "You are taken with a receptacle; strength of Indra, I take you pleasing to Indra the Good Protector," and having wiped it around with the filter, he sets it down with "This is your cradle; for greatness you!"

19.7.8.a.m: With the remainder of the section, the adhvaryu and the sacrificer attend upon the [draughts] that have been set down.

19.8.1.a.m: He assigns the animal victims as before.

19.8.2.a.m: Excepting that for Bṛhaspati, it is identical up to the carrying of fire around [the victims].

19.8.3.a.m: In the middle round of the carrying of fire around, having poured out a portion of the firebrand on the mound, he adds fuel.

19.8.4.a.m: Having carried fire around with the remainder, he brings this very [firebrand] forward for the cooking of the animal victims.

19.8.5.a.m: When the omenta have been offered, he gives forty cows as the sacrificial gift.

19.8.6.a.m: Or they may draw the draughts here.

19.8.8.a.m: "All should be offered in the āhavanīya," says Āśmarathya.

19.8.8.b.m: "The surā draughts [should be offered] in the southern fire," says Ālekhana.

19.8.9.a.m: He offers the milk draughts with "Possessing surā..."

19.8.9.b.m: The surā draughts with "Whatever sap of yours has been collected..."

19.8.10.a.m: Having offered when the secondary vaṣaṭ-call has been made silently, the adhvaryu partakes of the draught for the Aśvins with "Whom the two Aśvins from Namuci..."

19.8.11.a.m: With "What here is defiled..." the pratiprasthātṛ and the agnīdh [partake of] that for Sarasvatī.

19.8.12.a.m: With "This oblation..." the brahman and the sacrificer [partake of] that for Indra.

19.8.13.a.m: The disposal of the surā has been explained.

19.8.14.a.s: dakṣiṇenāhavanīyaṃ payaḥśeṣaṃ pitṛpitāmahaprapitāmahebhyo dadāti pitṛbhyaḥ svadhāvibhyaḥ svadhā nama iti
19.8.14.a.d: दक्षिणेनाहवनीयं पयःशेषं पितृपितामहप्रपितामहेभ्यो ददाति पितृभ्यः स्वधाविभ्यः स्वधा नम इति
19.8.14.a.m: To the south of the āhavanīya, he gives the remainder of the milk to the father, grandfather, and great-grandfather with: 'To the fathers who possess the svadhā, svadhā, homage!'

19.8.15.a.m: He pays reverence with: 'May the soma-loving fathers purify me!'

19.9.1.b.m: The adhvaryu with: 'Those who are equal...';

19.9.1.c.m: The pratiprasthātṛ with: 'Those who are of the same kin...'

19.9.2.a.s: manotākāle pṛthak pātreṣu paśūnāṃ yūṣāṇi nidadhāti
19.9.2.a.d: मनोताकाले पृथक् पात्रेषु पशूनां यूषाणि निदधाति
19.9.2.a.m: At the time of the Manotā hymn, he places the broths of the victims in separate vessels.

19.9.3.a.m: Before the sviṣṭakṛt, he offers the subsidiary oblations with the horns and hooves.

19.9.4.a.m: For each [victim] there are eight dewclaws and hooves.

19.9.5.a.s: āśvinasya yūṣeṇa kuṣṭhikāṃ śaphaṃ ca pūrayitvā sīsena tantramityaṣṭarcena pratimantraṃ dvābhyāṃdvābhyāṃ kuṣṭhikāśaphābhyāṃ juhoti
19.9.5.a.d: आश्विनस्य यूषेण कुष्ठिकां शफं च पूरयित्वा सीसेन तन्त्रमित्यष्टर्चेन प्रतिमन्त्रं द्वाभ्यांद्वाभ्यां कुष्ठिकाशफाभ्यां जुहोति
19.9.5.a.m: Having filled a dewclaw and a hoof with the broth of the [victim] belonging to the Aśvins, he offers with an eight-verse hymn, 'With lead the web...', verse by verse, with two dewclaws and hooves each time.

19.9.6.a.m: At the last [verse], he fastens the two horns.

19.9.7.a.m: Each time after offering, having poured down the residues into the respective anointing vessels, he casts the dewclaws and hooves into the āhavanīya.

19.9.8.a.m: In the same manner, [he offers] of the Sarasvatī victim with the subsequent eight verses.

19.9.9.a.m: With the whole anuvāka, [he offers] of the Indra victim.

19.9.10.a.m: There is a chair of udumbara wood, its headpiece and crossbars measuring a cubit, its legs reaching up to the navel, woven with muñja grass.

19.9.11.a.d: मित्रो ऽसि वरुणो ऽसीति तां यजमानायातने प्रतिष्ठापयति
19.9.11.a.m: He sets it down in the place of the sacrificer with: 'You are Mitra, you are Varuṇa.'

19.9.12.a.m: The setting down, sitting upon, and addressing [of the chair] are as in the Rājasūya.

19.9.13.a.s: tasyāṃ prāṅmukhamāsīnaṃ pratyaṅmukhastiṣṭhannāśvinasaṃpātairabhiṣiñcati devasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinorbāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāmaśvinorbhaiṣajyena tejase brahmavarcasāyābhiṣiñcāmīti
19.9.13.a.d: तस्यां प्राङ्मुखमासीनं प्रत्यङ्मुखस्तिष्ठन्नाश्विनसंपातैरभिषिञ्चति देवस्य त्वा सवितुः प्रसवे ऽश्विनोर्बाहुभ्यां पूष्णो हस्ताभ्यामश्विनोर्भैषज्येन तेजसे ब्रह्मवर्चसायाभिषिञ्चामीति
19.9.13.a.m: Standing facing west, he anoints him seated on it facing east with the residues of the Aśvin offering, saying: 'At the impulse of the divine Savitṛ, with the arms of the Aśvins, with the hands of Pūṣan, with the healing medicine of the Aśvins, I anoint you for brilliance, for spiritual luster.'

19.9.14.a.m: In the same manner, [he anoints him with the residue] of the Sarasvatī offering with the next formula.

19.10.1.a.d: को ऽसि कतमो ऽसीति पाणी संमृश्याध्वर्युर्व्याहृतीर्जुहोति
19.10.1.a.m: Having touched both hands with: 'Who are you? Which one are you?', the adhvaryu offers the vyāhṛtis.

19.10.2.a.s: atra rājasūyavanmaṅgalyanāmna āhūya śiro me śrīriti yathāliṅgamaṅgāni saṃmṛśya jaṅghābhyāṃ padbhyāmiti pratyavaruhya prati kṣatre pratitiṣṭhāmi rāṣṭra iti japitvā trayā devā ityāhutīrhutvā lomāni prayatirmameti yathāliṅgamaṅgāni saṃmṛśate
19.10.2.a.d: अत्र राजसूयवन्मङ्गल्यनाम्न आहूय शिरो मे श्रीरिति यथालिङ्गमङ्गानि संमृश्य जङ्घाभ्यां पद्भ्यामिति प्रत्यवरुह्य प्रति क्षत्रे प्रतितिष्ठामि राष्ट्र इति जपित्वा त्रया देवा इत्याहुतीर्हुत्वा लोमानि प्रयतिर्ममेति यथालिङ्गमङ्गानि संमृशते
19.10.2.a.m: Here, having called out auspicious names as in the Rājasūya, having touched the limbs in accordance with the markers with: 'My head is prosperity...', having descended with: 'With two shanks, with two feet...', having whispered: 'I establish myself in royal power, in dominion', having offered the oblations with: 'Three gods...', he touches the limbs in accordance with the markers with: 'My body hairs are exertion...'

19.10.3.a.m: From the sviṣṭakṛt onward, it is identical [with the animal sacrifice] up to the purificatory bath.

19.10.4.a.m: Āśmarathya says: 'He offers five oblations at the purificatory bath with: "Whatever offense against the gods, O gods..."'

19.10.4.b.m: Ālekhana says: 'They should be offered in the āhavanīya.'

19.10.5.a.s: avabhṛtha nicaṅkaṇetyavabhṛthaṃ yajamāno 'bhimantrya sumitrā na āpo drupadādivenmumucāna ityāplutyodvayaṃ tamasasparītyādityamupasthāya pratiyuto varuṇasya pāśa ityudakāntaṃ pratyasyati
19.10.5.a.d: अवभृथ निचङ्कणेत्यवभृथं यजमानो ऽभिमन्त्र्य सुमित्रा न आपो द्रुपदादिवेन्मुमुचान इत्याप्लुत्योद्वयं तमसस्परीत्यादित्यमुपस्थाय प्रतियुतो वरुणस्य पाश इत्युदकान्तं प्रत्यस्यति
19.10.5.a.m: Having addressed the purificatory bath with: 'O purificatory bath, gliding down...', having bathed with: 'May the waters be friendly to us...', 'As if released from a wooden post...', and having reverenced the sun with: 'Arising from the darkness...', the sacrificer throws [a stick] towards the edge of the water with: 'Repelled is Varuṇa's noose.'

19.10.6.a.m: [Putting on] firewood and reverencing are as in the animal sacrifice.

19.10.7.a.m: Having paid reverence with: 'The returner...', having offered an oblation with: 'Bhūḥ svāhā', the sacrifice to the ancestors is performed as before.

19.10.8.a.m: He seizes an animal victim for Indra Vayodhas.

19.10.12.b.m: 'He gives the calf at the former [sacrifice];

19.10.14.a.m: One who desires heaven should sacrifice with it.

19.11.1.a.m: One who desires heaven should pile the Sāvitra [altar].

19.11.3.a.s: ceṣyamāṇa upakalpayate pañcāśītiśataṃ hiraṇyeṣṭakā yāvaduttamamaṅguliparu tāvatīḥ śarkarā vābhyaktāścatasraḥ svayamātṛṇā aparimitā lokaṃpṛṇāḥ
19.11.3.a.d: चेष्यमाण उपकल्पयते पञ्चाशीतिशतं हिरण्येष्टका यावदुत्तममङ्गुलिपरु तावतीः शर्करा वाभ्यक्ताश्चतस्रः स्वयमातृणा अपरिमिता लोकंपृणाः
19.11.3.a.m: One about to pile procures one hundred and eighty-five golden bricks, or as many pebbles anointing them as measure up to the last finger-joint, four naturally perforated bricks, and an unlimited number of space-filling bricks.

19.11.4.a.m: He commences the ritual of the animal sacrifice beginning with the six Hotṛs formula.

19.11.5.a.m: It is declared: 'He sacrifices on a third of the altar ground.'

19.11.6.a.s: prāguttarātparigrāhātkṛtvottaravedideśasya madhye śaṅkuṃ nihatya sarvataḥ parimaṇḍalaṃ rathacakramātraṃ sāvitraṃ parilikhyā samūlaṃ haritaṃ darbhastambamāhṛtya madhye 'gnernikhāya juhvāṃ pañcagṛhītaṃ gṛhītvā sajūrabdo 'yāvabhiriti darbhastambe pañcāhutīrhutvoddhatyāvokṣya vyāghāraṇāntāmuttaravediṃ kṛtvā likhāyā abhyantaraṃ nava parimaṇḍalā lekhā likhitvā sikatābhiravakīrya darbhaiḥ pracchādya dadhnā madhumiśreṇa śarkarābhiriti bāhyāṃ lekhāṃ saṃpūrya vasati
19.11.6.a.d: प्रागुत्तरात्परिग्राहात्कृत्वोत्तरवेदिदेशस्य मध्ये शङ्कुं निहत्य सर्वतः परिमण्डलं रथचक्रमात्रं सावित्रं परिलिख्या समूलं हरितं दर्भस्तम्बमाहृत्य मध्ये ऽग्नेर्निखाय जुह्वां पञ्चगृहीतं गृहीत्वा सजूरब्दो ऽयावभिरिति दर्भस्तम्बे पञ्चाहुतीर्हुत्वोद्धत्यावोक्ष्य व्याघारणान्तामुत्तरवेदिं कृत्वा लिखाया अभ्यन्तरं नव परिमण्डला लेखा लिखित्वा सिकताभिरवकीर्य दर्भैः प्रच्छाद्य दध्ना मधुमिश्रेण शर्कराभिरिति बाह्यां लेखां संपूर्य वसति
19.11.6.a.m: Before the upper enclosing boundary, having driven in a peg in the middle of the high altar's area, having marked all around the Sāvitra [ground] circular, the size of a chariot-wheel, having fetched a green clump of darbha grass with its roots, having planted it in the middle of the fire[-site], having drawn five ladlings into the offering ladle, having offered five oblations onto the darbha clump with: 'In union, the year with its months...', having excavated [the site], having sprinkled it with water, having completed the high altar up to the pourings of clarified butter, having drawn nine circular furrows inside the marked area, having scattered them with sand, having covered them with darbha grass, having filled the outer furrow with curd mixed with honey and pebbles, he remains overnight.

19.11.7.a.s: hute prātaragnihotre prajāpatistvā sādayatu tayā devatayāṅgirasvaddhruvā sīdetyuttaravedimabhimṛśya mayi gṛhṇāmyagre agniṃ yo no agniḥ pitara iti dvābhyāmātmannagniṃ gṛhītvā yāste agne samidha iti svayaṃdityābhimṛśyāgnerbhasmāsīti sikatā nivapati /
19.11.7.a.d: हुते प्रातरग्निहोत्रे प्रजापतिस्त्वा सादयतु तया देवतयाङ्गिरस्वद्ध्रुवा सीदेत्युत्तरवेदिमभिमृश्य मयि गृह्णाम्यग्रे अग्निं यो नो अग्निः पितर इति द्वाभ्यामात्मन्नग्निं गृहीत्वा यास्ते अग्ने समिध इति स्वयंदित्याभिमृश्याग्नेर्भस्मासीति सिकता निवपति ।
19.11.7.a.m: When the morning agnihotra has been offered, having touched the high altar with: 'May Prajāpati seat you; with that deity, in the manner of the Aṅgirases, sit firm', having taken the fire into himself with the two verses: 'I take Agni into myself at first...', 'The fire of ours which, O fathers...', having touched the self-perforated [brick] with: 'Agni, the firewood that is yours...', he scatters the sand with: 'You are Agni's ashes.'

19.11.8.a.m: While scattering them, he mentally meditates: 'Whatever black spot is there in the moon, may that be here.'

19.11.9.a.s: saṃ yā vaḥ priyāstanuva ityūṣānsikatāśca saṃsṛjya cita stha paricita ityaparimitābhiḥ śarkarābhiḥ pariśrityā pyāyasva sametu ta iti sikatā vyūhati
19.11.9.a.d: सं या वः प्रियास्तनुव इत्यूषान्सिकताश्च संसृज्य चित स्थ परिचित इत्यपरिमिताभिः शर्कराभिः परिश्रित्या प्यायस्व समेतु त इति सिकता व्यूहति
19.11.9.a.m: Having mixed the saline earth and the sand with: 'Those dear bodies of yours that unite...', having enclosed [the altar] with an unlimited number of pebbles with: 'You are piled, you are enclosed', he spreads out the sand with: 'Swell up, may it gather together for you...'

19.11.10.a.m: They do not obscure the furrows.

19.11.11.a.s: abhyantaraṃ jaghanārdha udapātramupadadhāti vāktvā samudra upadadhe suprajāvaniṃ rāyaspoṣavaniṃ mahyaṃ vājināyeti
19.11.11.a.d: अभ्यन्तरं जघनार्ध उदपात्रमुपदधाति वाक्त्वा समुद्र उपदधे सुप्रजावनिं रायस्पोषवनिं मह्यं वाजिनायेति
19.11.11.a.m: Inside, in the western half, he places a water pot with: 'I place speech, you the ocean, bestowing good offspring, bestowing increase of wealth, for me, the energetic.'

19.12.1.a.s: navamyāṃ bāhyāyāṃ lekhāyāṃ pañcadaśa pūrvapakṣasyāhānyupadadhāti saṃjñānaṃ vijñānamiti
19.12.1.a.d: नवम्यां बाह्यायां लेखायां पञ्चदश पूर्वपक्षस्याहान्युपदधाति संज्ञानं विज्ञानमिति
19.12.1.a.m: In the ninth, outer furrow, he places the fifteen days of the waxing fortnight with: 'Agreement, understanding...'

19.12.2.a.m: In the intervals between those days, he places fifteen [hours] with: 'Bright, banner...'

19.12.3.a.s: athāntarasyāṃ pañcadaśa pūrvapakṣasya rātrīrupadadhāti darśā dṛṣṭeti
19.12.3.a.d: अथान्तरस्यां पञ्चदश पूर्वपक्षस्य रात्रीरुपदधाति दर्शा दृष्टेति
19.12.3.a.m: Then in the inner [furrow], he places the fifteen nights of the waxing fortnight with: 'The new moon, the visible...'

19.12.4.a.s: tāsāmantarāleṣvetāsāṃ rātrīṇāṃ pañcadaśa muhūrtānupadadhāti dātā pradāteti
19.12.4.a.d: तासामन्तरालेष्वेतासां रात्रीणां पञ्चदश मुहूर्तानुपदधाति दाता प्रदातेति
19.12.4.a.m: In the intervals between those nights, he places the fifteen muhūrtas with: 'Giver, bestower...'

19.12.5.a.m: Then in the inner [furrow], he places the fifteen days of the waning fortnight with: 'Puffed, chanted...'

19.12.6.a.m: In the intervals between those days, he places the fifteen muhūrtas with: 'Savitṛ, the impeller...'

19.12.7.a.m: Then in the inner [furrow], he places the fifteen nights of the waning fortnight with: 'Pressed, pressing...'

19.12.8.a.m: In the intervals between those nights, he places the fifteen muhūrtas with: 'Accuser, approver...'

19.12.9.a.m: Then in the inner [furrow], he places the twelve waxing fortnights with: 'The strainer, about to purify...'

19.12.10.a.m: Then in the inner [ring] he lays down the twelve dark fortnights with: 'Sahasvān sahīyān…' [TB 3.10.1.2].

19.12.11.a.m: Then in the inner [ring] he lays down the thirteen month-names with: 'Aruṇo 'ruṇarajas…' [TB 3.10.1.3].

19.12.12.a.m: Then he lays down sand with: 'Ejatkā jovatkā…' [TB 3.10.1.4].

19.12.13.a.m: Then in the inner [ring] he lays down the fifteen muhūrtas with: 'Idānīṃ tadānīm…' [TB 3.10.1.4].

19.12.14.a.m: Then in the inner [ring] he lays down the six sacrificial rites [and] three four-names with: 'Agniṣṭoma ukthyo agnirṛtuḥ…' [TB 3.10.1.4].

19.12.15.a.s: atha nābhyāṃ catvāri saṃvatsaranāmānyupadadhāti prajāpatiḥ saṃvatsaro mahānka iti
19.12.15.a.d: अथ नाभ्यां चत्वारि संवत्सरनामान्युपदधाति प्रजापतिः संवत्सरो महान्क इति
19.12.15.a.m: Then on the navel he lays down the four year-names with: 'Prajāpatiḥ saṃvatsaro mahānkaḥ…' [TB 3.10.1.4].

19.12.16.a.s: catasraḥ svayamātṛṇā dikṣūpadadhāti bhūragniṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca māṃ ceti
19.12.16.a.d: चतस्रः स्वयमातृणा दिक्षूपदधाति भूरग्निं च पृथिवीं च मां चेति
19.12.16.a.m: He lays down four naturally perforated [bricks] in the quarters with: 'Bhūr agniṃ ca pṛthivīṃ ca māṃ ca…' [TB 3.10.2.1].

19.12.17.a.m: He lays down the space-filling [bricks] with: 'Fill the space…' [TB 3.10.2.1].

19.12.18.a.m: Having brought loose earth from the pit, he spreads it out over the piling with the verse addressed to Vaiśvānara: 'Pṛṣṭo divi…' [TB 3.10.2.2].

19.12.21.a.s: upasthānenopatiṣṭhate tvameva tvāṃ vettha yo 'si so 'sīti
19.12.21.a.d: उपस्थानेनोपतिष्ठते त्वमेव त्वां वेत्थ यो ऽसि सो ऽसीति
19.12.21.a.m: He reveres [the fire] with the attendance verse: 'Thou alone knowest thyself, who thou art, that art thou' [TB 3.10.2.3].

19.12.23.a.s: dhenūḥ kṛtvā yajamānaḥ saṃhāravihārābhyāmupatiṣṭhate saṃvatsaro 'si parivatsaro 'sīti
19.12.23.a.d: धेनूः कृत्वा यजमानः संहारविहाराभ्यामुपतिष्ठते संवत्सरो ऽसि परिवत्सरो ऽसीति
19.12.23.a.m: Having made cows, the sacrificer attends [the fire] with contraction and expansion, [reciting]: 'Thou art the Saṃvatsara, thou art the Parivatsara…' [TB 3.10.4.1].

19.12.24.a.m: To the north, on the highest brick, he offers goat's milk with an arka-leaf.

19.12.25.a.s: tvamagne rudra iti śatarudrīyasya rūpamasaṃcare paśūnāmarkaparṇa udasyati valmīkavapāyāṃ vāvadadhāti
19.12.25.a.d: त्वमग्ने रुद्र इति शतरुद्रीयस्य रूपमसंचरे पशूनामर्कपर्ण उदस्यति वल्मीकवपायां वावदधाति
19.12.25.a.m: With 'Thou, O Agni, art Rudra…' [TB 3.10.5.1], which has the form of the Śatarudrīya; he throws away the arka-leaf where cattle do not roam, or places it in the mound of an anthill.

19.12.26.a.s: jaghanenāgniṃ prāṅmukha upaviśya saṃcitokthyena hotānuśaṃsati bhūrbhuvaḥ svarityanuvākena
19.12.26.a.d: जघनेनाग्निं प्राङ्मुख उपविश्य संचितोक्थ्येन होतानुशंसति भूर्भुवः स्वरित्यनुवाकेन
19.12.26.a.m: Seated facing east behind the fire, the hotṛ recites the accompaniment with the Saṃcitokthya, [namely] with the anuvāka: 'Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ…' [TB 3.10.5.1].

19.13.1.a.m: He undertakes the animal sacrifice rites beginning with the leading forward of the fire, identical [with the archetype] up to the Atimukti offerings.

19.13.2.a.m: Having offered the Atimukti libations, he offers a fourfold-drawn portion [of clarified butter]:

19.13.3.a.m: 'Thou, O Agni, art Rudra…' [TB 3.10.6.1], which is the form of the Śatarudrīya.

19.13.6.a.s: sapta te agne samidhaḥ sapta jihvā iti viśvaprīḥ
19.13.6.a.d: सप्त ते अग्ने समिधः सप्त जिह्वा इति विश्वप्रीः
19.13.6.a.m: 'Seven are thy kindling-sticks, O Agni, seven thy tongues…' [TB 3.10.6.1] is the Viśvaprī offering.

19.13.7.a.s: aparaṃ caturgṛhītaṃ vasūnāṃ tvādhītena rudrāṇāmūrmyādityānāṃ tejasā viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ dratunā marutāmemnā juhomi svāheti
19.13.7.a.d: अपरं चतुर्गृहीतं वसूनां त्वाधीतेन रुद्राणामूर्म्यादित्यानां तेजसा विश्वेषां देवानां द्रतुना मरुतामेम्ना जुहोमि स्वाहेति
19.13.7.a.m: Another fourfold-drawn portion [he offers] with: 'With the design of the Vasus, with the surge of the Rudras, with the brilliance of the Ādityas, with the resolve of the Viśvedevas, with the host of the Maruts, I offer, svāhā!' [TB 3.10.6.1].

19.13.8.a.s: tāsāṃ saṃsrāveṇa yajamāno mukhaṃ vimṛṣṭe rājñī virājñītyanuvākena
19.13.8.a.d: तासां संस्रावेण यजमानो मुखं विमृष्टे राज्ञी विराज्ञीत्यनुवाकेन
19.13.8.a.m: With the residue of those [libations] the sacrificer wipes his face, with the anuvāka: 'Rājñī virājñī…' [TB 3.10.7.1].

19.13.9.a.m: Then he offers twenty-one oblations with the anuvāka: 'To Asu svāhā, to Vasu svāhā…' [TB 3.10.8.1], mantra by mantra.

19.13.10.a.s: barhiṣaḥ saṃbharaṇādi pāśukaṃ karma pratipadyate samānamā vapāyā homāt
19.13.10.a.d: बर्हिषः संभरणादि पाशुकं कर्म प्रतिपद्यते समानमा वपाया होमात्
19.13.10.a.m: He undertakes the animal sacrifice rites beginning with the gathering of the sacrificial grass, identical [with the archetype] up to the offering of the omentum.

19.13.11.a.m: When the omentum has been offered, he gives four-year-old heifers as sacrificial gifts corresponding to the bricks.

19.13.12.a.m: If he cannot afford so many sacrificial gifts, he should give that many brāhmaṇas groats-drinks to drink,

19.13.13.a.s: teno haivāsya sa kāma upāpto bhavati
19.13.13.a.d: तेनो हैवास्य स काम उपाप्तो भवति
19.13.13.a.m: By that indeed that wish of his becomes attained.

19.13.14.a.m: He should, however, give one pregnant four-year-old heifer, gold, and a garment.

19.13.15.a.s: yatprāṅ manotāyāstatkṛtvaudumbarapātreṇa yuṣṇo mṛtyave grahaṃ gṛhṇāti
19.13.15.a.d: यत्प्राङ् मनोतायास्तत्कृत्वौदुम्बरपात्रेण युष्णो मृत्यवे ग्रहं गृह्णाति
19.13.15.a.m: Having performed what comes before the Manotā hymn, he draws a draught of broth for Mṛtyu with an udumbara cup.

19.13.16.a.m: With 'To the wise, to the purifying…' [TB 3.10.8.2] are the drawing and depositing [mantras].
