19.13.17.a.m: According to another view, the draught to Mṛtyu should belong only to the Nāciketa [fire].

19.13.18.a.m: Its offering is after the Sviṣṭakṛt.

19.13.19.a.m: About to offer, he touches water with: 'Thou art lightning; sever my sin!' [TB 3.10.8.3].

19.13.20.a.m: Then he offers with: 'Away death, away hunger…' [TB 3.10.8.4].

19.13.21.a.m: Then having offered, he touches [water] with: 'Thou art rain; cut away my sin!' [TB 3.10.8.5].

19.13.23.a.m: He partakes with: 'Thou art the portion, the immortal portion…' [TB 3.10.8.6].

19.13.24.a.m: Having partaken, he establishes the breath-calls in himself with the remainder of the anuvāka: 'Mandrābhibhūtiḥ…' [TB 3.10.8.7].

19.13.25.a.m: From here onwards the animal sacrifice rites are identical [with the archetype].

19.14.1.a.m: By this the Nāciketa is explained.

19.14.3.a.s: ekaviṃśatirhiraṇyeṣṭakāḥ śarkarā vābhyaktā upadhānakāle nābhyāmevopadhīyante caturaśraṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ vā loko 'si svargo 'sītyanuvākena pratimantram
19.14.3.a.d: एकविंशतिर्हिरण्येष्टकाः शर्करा वाभ्यक्ता उपधानकाले नाभ्यामेवोपधीयन्ते चतुरश्रं परिमण्डलं वा लोको ऽसि स्वर्गो ऽसीत्यनुवाकेन प्रतिमन्त्रम्
19.14.3.a.m: Twenty-one gold bricks or greased pebbles are laid down only on the navel at the time of laying down, square or circular, with the anuvāka: 'Thou art the world, thou art heaven…' [TB 3.11.1.1], mantra by mantra.

19.14.4.a.s: taṃ haitameke paśubandha evottaravedyāṃ cinvata iti brāhmaṇavyākhyātā vikārāḥ
19.14.4.a.d: तं हैतमेके पशुबन्ध एवोत्तरवेद्यां चिन्वत इति ब्राह्मणव्याख्याता विकाराः
19.14.4.a.m: Some pile this very [Nāciketa fire] on the uttaravedī only in an animal sacrifice; thus are the modifications explained in the Brāhmaṇa.

19.14.6.a.s: paśubandhe some sattre sahasre sarvavedase vā yatra vā bhūyiṣṭhā āhutayo hūyeraṃstatra cetavyaḥ
19.14.6.a.d: पशुबन्धे सोमे सत्त्रे सहस्रे सर्ववेदसे वा यत्र वा भूयिष्ठा आहुतयो हूयेरंस्तत्र चेतव्यः
19.14.6.a.m: In an animal sacrifice, in a Soma sacrifice, in a sacrificial session, in a thousand-cow sacrifice, or in an all-property sacrifice, or wherever the most oblations are offered, there it should be piled.

19.14.7.a.m: Desiring a firm foundation in a sacrificial session, desiring glory, offspring, cattle, heaven, [or] prosperity, according to opportunity [and] according to the traditional text.

19.14.8.a.m: Everywhere the beginning is in the east, the completion is in the north in a clockwise direction.

19.14.9.a.m: One who desires cattle should pile [the bricks] only in a fivefold manner:

19.14.9.b.m: five in each direction, one in the middle.

19.14.10.a.m: One desiring pre-eminence, glory, or offspring [should pile them] in a threefold manner:

19.14.10.b.s: sapta purastāttisro dakṣiṇataḥ sapta paścāttisra uttarata ekāṃ madhye
19.14.10.b.d: सप्त पुरस्तात्तिस्रो दक्षिणतः सप्त पश्चात्तिस्र उत्तरत एकां मध्ये
19.14.10.b.m: seven in the east, three in the south, seven in the west, three in the north, one in the middle.

19.14.11.a.m: One who desires pre-eminence should proceed starting from the middle along an upward row.

19.14.12.a.m: One who desires heaven should proceed starting from the west along an eastward row.

19.14.13.a.s: sa yadīcchettejasvī yaśasvī brahmavarcasī syāmiti prāgdakṣiṇebhyaḥ prāṅā hoturdhiṣṇyādutsarpedyeyaṃ prāgādyaśasvatī sā mā prorṇotu tejasā yaśasā brahmavarcaseneti
19.14.13.a.d: स यदीच्छेत्तेजस्वी यशस्वी ब्रह्मवर्चसी स्यामिति प्राग्दक्षिणेभ्यः प्राङा होतुर्धिष्ण्यादुत्सर्पेद्येयं प्रागाद्यशस्वती सा मा प्रोर्णोतु तेजसा यशसा ब्रह्मवर्चसेनेति
19.14.13.a.m: If he should desire: 'May I be brilliant, renowned, endowed with spiritual luster', he should glide forward to the east from the southern ones, up to the dhiṣṇya hearth of the hotṛ, with: 'May this renowned one that has gone east cover me with brilliance, with renown, with spiritual luster.'

19.14.14.a.s: atha yadīcchedbhūyiṣṭhaṃ me śraddadhīranbhūyiṣṭhā dakṣiṇā nayeyuriti dakṣiṇāsu nīyamānāsu prācyehi prācyehīti
19.14.14.a.d: अथ यदीच्छेद्भूयिष्ठं मे श्रद्दधीरन्भूयिष्ठा दक्षिणा नयेयुरिति दक्षिणासु नीयमानासु प्राच्येहि प्राच्येहीति
19.14.14.a.m: Now, if he should wish: “May they place the utmost faith in me; may they lead away the most abundant sacrificial gifts,” while the sacrificial gifts are being led away, with the words: “Come facing east, come facing east;”

19.14.15.a.s: prācī juṣāṇā vetvājyasya svāheti sruveṇopahatyāhavanīye juhuyāt
19.14.15.a.d: प्राची जुषाणा वेत्वाज्यस्य स्वाहेति स्रुवेणोपहत्याहवनीये जुहुयात्
19.14.15.a.m: having scooped [ghee] with the sruva, he should offer into the āhavanīya with the formula: “Facing east, enjoying, let her partake of the ghee, svāhā!”

19.14.16.a.m: The subsequent [procedure], beginning with the self-perforated [brick], is the same.

19.14.18.a.m: By this, the Cāturhotra [fire-altar] is explained.

19.14.19.a.m: As many gold bricks or smeared pebbles as there are pādas [are used].

19.14.20.a.m: At the time of piling, he piles [the bricks of] the Daśahotṛ northwards in front of the tuft of darbha grass, mantra by mantra.

19.14.20.b.s: hṛdayaṃ grahaṃ catvāri padāni saṃbhārāṇāṃ dve patnīnām
19.14.20.b.d: हृदयं ग्रहं चत्वारि पदानि संभाराणां द्वे पत्नीनाम्
19.14.20.b.m: The heart, the cup, four pādas of the materials, [and] two of the wives.

19.14.21.a.m: Similarly, [he piles the bricks of] the Caturhotṛ eastwards to the south.

19.14.22.a.m: [He piles the bricks of] the Pañcahotṛ northwards to the west.

19.14.23.a.m: [He piles the bricks of] the Ṣaḍḍhotṛ eastwards to the north.

19.14.24.a.m: [He piles the bricks of] the Saptahotṛ eastwards above.

19.14.25.a.m: Here [there are] five pādas of the materials and the remaining ones of the wives.

19.14.26.a.m: The subsequent [procedure], beginning with the self-perforated [brick], is the same.

19.15.1.a.m: By this, the Vaiśvasṛja [fire-altar] is explained.

19.15.2.a.m: As many gold bricks or smeared pebbles as there are mantras [are used].

19.15.3.a.m: At the time of piling, he piles the fire in a clockwise direction in front of the northern navel with these three anuvākas: “What is immortal and what is mortal...”

19.15.4.a.m: Or [there are] three layers by means of the three anuvākas.

19.15.5.a.m: The subsequent [procedure], beginning with the self-perforated [brick], is the same, except for the subsequent recitation.

19.15.6.a.m: He recites subsequently with this anuvāka: “The eastern great quarter of the verses is declared...”

19.15.7.a.s: rātrisattreṣu śatarātrānteṣu samahāvrateṣu triṣu ca sārasvateṣu sattreṣu kāṭhakacāturmāsyeṣu sādhyānāṃ ṣaḍahavarjiteṣu viśvasṛjāmayane prajāpateḥ sahasrasaṃvatsarayośca vaiśvasṛjo 'gnirniyataḥ
19.15.7.a.d: रात्रिसत्त्रेषु शतरात्रान्तेषु समहाव्रतेषु त्रिषु च सारस्वतेषु सत्त्रेषु काठकचातुर्मास्येषु साध्यानां षडहवर्जितेषु विश्वसृजामयने प्रजापतेः सहस्रसंवत्सरयोश्च वैश्वसृजो ऽग्निर्नियतः
19.15.7.a.m: The Vaiśvasṛja fire is prescribed in night sessions, in those ending in a hundred nights, in those accompanied by the Mahāvrata, in the three Sārasvata sessions, in the Cāturmāsyas of the Kaṭhas, in [sessions] of the Sādhyas excluding the six-day period, in the course of the Viśvasṛjs, and in the two thousand-year [sessions] of Prajāpati.

19.15.8.a.m: If they should pile it upon marching forward, he should touch the site of the high altar with these mantras.

19.15.9.a.s: yo 'sya supriyaḥ suvicita iva syāttasmai vaiśvasṛjam /
19.15.9.a.d: यो ऽस्य सुप्रियः सुविचित इव स्यात्तस्मै वैश्वसृजम् ।
19.15.9.a.m: For one who is very dear to him and thoroughly examined, as it were, he should pile the Vaiśvasṛja [fire-altar].

19.15.10.a.m: Combining the Sāvitra, Nāciketa, Cāturhotra, Vaiśvasṛja, and Āruṇaketuka [altars], one may pile [the fire-altar] even in a Soma sacrifice.

19.15.11.a.m: The Sāvitra is the first layer;

19.15.12.a.m: He draws a draught for Death from the broth of the animal victim belonging to the pressing day.

19.15.13.a.s: ya etānagnīnpṛthak samāsena vā cinvāna ubhayīrdakṣiṇā dadāti kratudakṣiṇā yathāsamāmnātamagnidakṣināśceti
19.15.13.a.d: य एतानग्नीन्पृथक् समासेन वा चिन्वान उभयीर्दक्षिणा ददाति क्रतुदक्षिणा यथासमाम्नातमग्निदक्षिनाश्चेति
19.15.13.a.m: One who piles these fires separately or combined gives both kinds of sacrificial gifts: the sacrificial gifts for the sacrifice as handed down by tradition, and the sacrificial gifts for the fire-altar.

19.15.14.a.m: Here, without having employed them separately, they are not combined.

19.15.15.a.m: Having piled the fire-altar, one should sacrifice with the Sautrāmaṇī;

19.15.15.b.m: or with the curd mess dedicated to Mitrā-Varuṇā.

19.15.16.a.m: The Āruṇaketuka is explained by the Brāhmaṇa.

19.15.17.a.m: Desiring heaven, one should sacrifice day after day with the Divaḥśyenī [bricks];

19.15.18.a.m: They are explained by the Brāhmaṇa.

19.16.1.a.m: One should sacrifice with the optional animal sacrifices on the new-moon day or on the full-moon day.

19.16.2.a.m: The ritual procedure for them is like that of the independent animal sacrifice.

19.16.3.a.m: They are explained by the Brāhmaṇa beginning: “A white [animal] dedicated to Vāyu...”

19.16.4.a.m: In their variable places, he inserts six verses according to the deity:

19.16.4.b.m: two each for the omentum, the sacrificial cake, [and] the oblation [of meat].

19.16.5.a.s: pīvo 'nnāṃ rayivṛdhaḥ sumedhā ityetāni yathāpūrvaṃ yathāliṅgamāmnātāni bhavanti
19.16.5.a.d: पीवो ऽन्नां रयिवृधः सुमेधा इत्येतानि यथापूर्वं यथालिङ्गमाम्नातानि भवन्ति
19.16.5.a.m: These verses: “Pīvo'nnām...”, “Rayivṛdhaḥ...”, “Sumedhāḥ...” are handed down according to previous order and according to characteristic marks.

19.16.6.a.s: sarveṣvābhicaraṇikeṣu lohitoṣṇīṣā lohitavasanā nivītā ṛtvijaḥ pracaranti malhā iti
19.16.6.a.d: सर्वेष्वाभिचरणिकेषु लोहितोष्णीषा लोहितवसना निवीता ऋत्विजः प्रचरन्ति मल्हा इति
19.16.6.a.m: In all sorcery rites, the priests perform their duties wearing red turbans, red garments, with sacred threads suspended [around the neck], and malhāḥ.

19.16.8.a.s: viṣama ālabheteti viṣamaṃ devayajanaṃ syātpaśuṃ vā viṣama ālabheta
19.16.8.a.d: विषम आलभेतेति विषमं देवयजनं स्यात्पशुं वा विषम आलभेत
19.16.8.a.m: As for “he should immolate on an uneven [ground]”: the sacrificial site should be uneven, or he should immolate the animal on uneven [ground].

19.16.9.a.m: There is a discussion regarding the deity of the ten-bull [sacrifice]:

19.16.10.a.s: ādityā syātprājāpatyā vaikādaśinadevatā vā yaddevatā vā garbhiṇayaḥ
19.16.10.a.d: आदित्या स्यात्प्राजापत्या वैकादशिनदेवता वा यद्देवता वा गर्भिणयः
19.16.10.a.m: She should be dedicated to Aditi, or dedicated to Prajāpati, or having the deities of the Ekādaśinī, or belonging to the deity to whom pregnant [victims] belong.

19.16.11.a.m: “Paryāriṇī” means she is one that gives birth successively.

19.16.12.a.s: sphyo yūpa iti sphyākṛtiyūpa agnyāgāriko vā
19.16.12.a.d: स्फ्यो यूप इति स्फ्याकृतियूप अग्न्यागारिको वा
19.16.12.a.m: As for “the sacrificial post is a sphya”: it is a sacrificial post shaped like a wooden sword, or one belonging to the fire house.

19.16.13.a.m: As for “a mare dedicated to Tvaṣṭṛ”: one which mounts [another] while being male.

19.16.14.a.s: apāṃ cauṣahīnāṃ ca saṃdhāviti prāvṛṣi śaratpratipattau vā /
19.16.14.a.d: अपां चौषहीनां च संधाविति प्रावृषि शरत्प्रतिपत्तौ वा ।
19.16.14.a.m: As for “at the junction of waters and plants”: in the rainy season or at the onset of autumn;

19.16.14.b.m: or at the junction of waters and plants.

19.16.15.a.m: As for “a forked sacrificial post”: that which is above the girdle is forked;

19.16.15.b.m: or both branches above the peg should be eight-cornered and equipped with top-rings.

19.16.16.a.s: prāśṛṅgo 'vāśṛṅga ukṣā vaśā vehaddhenurvatsa ṛṣabho 'naḍvānpunarutsṛṣṭo gomṛga iti gavyāḥ
19.16.16.a.d: प्राशृङ्गो ऽवाशृङ्ग उक्षा वशा वेहद्धेनुर्वत्स ऋषभो ऽनड्वान्पुनरुत्सृष्टो गोमृग इति गव्याः
19.16.16.a.m: One with forward-pointing horns, one with downward-pointing horns, an ox, a barren cow, a miscarrying cow, a milk cow, a calf, a bull, a draft-ox, a bull set free again, and a gomṛga: these are bovine [victims].

19.16.17.a.m: He seizes a miscarrying cow for Food.

19.16.18.a.m: The subsidiary offerings are [performed with the verses] 'The cows have come…'.

19.16.20.a.m: There he should offer along with it [the verse beginning with] 'Bhartāram…'.

19.16.21.a.m: For Sun and Moon, twins, one white and one black, at a single sacrificial post.

19.16.23.a.m: There he should offer along with it [the verse beginning with] 'Salilam…'.

19.16.25.a.m: For those animals which come after the animal for the Aśvins, the procedure is according to the order of the hymn.

19.17.1.a.m: When the bull among the cattle has grown old, he should whisper into the ear of a young [bull with these two verses]: 'Of reddish-brown form…' and 'That fourth of ours…'.

19.17.2.a.m: Then he sends him forth among the cows with [the verse]: 'This young one…'.

19.17.3.a.m: Then he seizes the old one for Prajāpati, for Indra, or for Tvaṣṭṛ.

19.17.4.a.m: At the dedication he follows up with [the verse]: 'Homage to greatness…'.

19.17.5.c.m: With the fifth, the [oblation] to Sviṣṭakṛt.

19.17.6.a.m: Having apportioned a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, he seizes a barren she-goat.

19.17.7.a.m: 'One desiring prosperity should seize [a barren she-goat] sacred to Vāyu'—thus the deities have been stated.

19.17.8.a.m: He dedicates [her] with the verse to Vāyu: 'Come, O Vāyu, adorn [our sacrifice], drinker of the pure…'.

19.17.9.a.s: ākūtyai tvā kāmāya tveti paryagnau kriyamāṇe juhoti
19.17.9.a.d: आकूत्यै त्वा कामाय त्वेति पर्यग्नौ क्रियमाणे जुहोति
19.17.9.a.m: While carrying fire around [her], he offers with: 'To intention thee, to desire thee…'.

19.17.10.a.m: He addresses [the victim] being led northwards with: 'Thou art the fourth, the ruling barren cow…'.

19.17.11.a.m: As she is being struck down, with: 'Thou art a she-goat, abiding in wealth…'.

19.17.12.a.m: With 'Extending the web…' he offers the omentum.

19.17.13.a.m: With 'Weave an uninterrupted web…' [he offers] the oblation.

19.17.14.a.m: With 'Thou art the oblation of the mind…' they eat the remnants of the oblation.

19.17.15.a.m: 'Indeed, that one [secures the wish] of only three'—thus it is declared [in the Brāhmaṇa].

19.17.16.a.s: tasyai vā etasyā ekamevādevayajanaṃ yadālabdhāyāmabhro bhavati
19.17.16.a.d: तस्यै वा एतस्या एकमेवादेवयजनं यदालब्धायामभ्रो भवति
19.17.16.a.m:
Indeed, for this one there is only one unfitness for sacrifice: namely, when a cloud appears after she has been seized.

If a cloud should appear after she has been seized, he should either make [her] enter into the waters, or the sacrificer alone should eat the entire [victim] day after day.

19.17.17.a.s: yadālabdhāyāmabhraḥ syādapsu vā praveśayetsarvāṃ vā yajamāna evānvahaṃ prāśnīyāt
19.17.17.a.d: यदालब्धायामभ्रः स्यादप्सु वा प्रवेशयेत्सर्वां वा यजमान एवान्वहं प्राश्नीयात्

19.17.18.a.m: The Jayas, the Abhyātānas, and the Rāṣṭrabhṛts have been explained in the Brāhmaṇa.

19.17.19.a.m: In the Abhyātānas, he adds [the words] 'In this holy power…'.

19.17.20.a.s: yena karmaṇertsettatra hotavyā ṛdhnotyeva tena karmaṇeti vijñāyate
19.17.20.a.d: येन कर्मणेर्त्सेत्तत्र होतव्या ऋध्नोत्येव तेन कर्मणेति विज्ञायते
19.17.20.a.m: 'For whichever rite he desires success, therein they should be offered; he indeed prospers through that rite'—so it is known.

19.18.1.a.m: One should sacrifice with the optional sacrifices on the new moon day or on the full moon day.

19.18.2.a.m: They have been explained in the Brāhmaṇa.

19.18.3.a.s: samidhyamānavatīṃ samiddhavatīṃ cāntareṇa pṛthupājavatyau dhāyye dadhāti /
19.18.3.a.d: समिध्यमानवतीं समिद्धवतीं चान्तरेण पृथुपाजवत्यौ धाय्ये दधाति ।
19.18.3.a.m: Between the verse containing [the word] 'being kindled' and the one containing 'kindled', he inserts two supplementary kindling verses containing [the word] 'pṛthupājas'.

19.18.3.b.m: Or the two portions of clarified butter are matching as prescribed.

19.18.4.a.m: They should contain mention of whatever the desire of the sacrifice is, because they are for that purpose, [and] because they bear its characteristic mark;

19.18.5.a.m: Where there is no specific instruction, the standard form is to be understood.

19.18.7.b.m: 'Thee, O Agni, mortals with oblations praise as god;

19.18.7.c.s: manye tvā jātavedasaṃ sa havyā vakṣyānuṣagityete āmnāte bhavataḥ
19.18.7.c.d: मन्ये त्वा जातवेदसं स हव्या वक्ष्यानुषगित्येते आम्नाते भवतः
19.18.7.c.m: I think of thee as Jātavedas; do thou carry the oblations in succession'—these two are handed down.

19.18.8.a.s: ubhā vāmindrāgnī āhuvadhyā ityetāsāṃ yathāpūrvamāmnātā yājyānuvākyā liṅgairniyamyante
19.18.8.a.d: उभा वामिन्द्राग्नी आहुवध्या इत्येतासां यथापूर्वमाम्नाता याज्यानुवाक्या लिङ्गैर्नियम्यन्ते
19.18.8.a.m: [For the optional sacrifices beginning with] 'Both of you, Indra and Agni, we call upon…', the invitatory and consecratory verses handed down in their order are determined by their characteristic marks:

19.18.9.a.m: That which has the deity mentioned in the first half-verse, having its mark in front, is the invitatory verse;

19.18.9.b.m: that which has its mark later is the consecratory verse.

19.18.11.a.m: The remaining ones are for the purpose of option.

19.18.12.a.m: Or the subsidiary offerings there are doubtful.

19.18.14.a.s: agnaye rakṣoghne puroḍāśamaṣṭākapālamamāvāsyāyāṃ niśāyāṃ nirvapettasyāḥ sādguṇyasāmarthyāt
19.18.14.a.d: अग्नये रक्षोघ्ने पुरोडाशमष्टाकपालममावास्यायां निशायां निर्वपेत्तस्याः साद्गुण्यसामर्थ्यात्
19.18.14.a.m: He should apportion a cake on eight potsherds for Agni, slayer of demons, at night on the new moon day, because of its suitability for that excellence.

19.18.15.a.m: There should be a removal of the time of the new moon.

19.18.16.a.s: kṛṇuṣva pāja iti rakṣoghnīḥ parācīḥ sāmidhenīranvāha
19.18.16.a.d: कृणुष्व पाज इति रक्षोघ्नीः पराचीः सामिधेनीरन्वाह
19.18.16.a.m: With 'Put forth thy strength…' he recites straight through the kindling verses which slay demons.

19.18.17.a.m: The invitatory and consecratory verses are [the two verses beginning with] 'With light…'.

19.19.1.a.m: One about to set out for battle should apportion boiled rice for the Ādityas.

19.19.2.a.m: Having gone to the battlefield, he should apportion a cake on twelve potsherds for Agni Vaiśvānara.

19.19.3.a.s: yayā rajjvottamāṃ gāmājettayā bhrātṛvyagavīmabhidadhyādgoṣṭhe vāsya nyasyet
19.19.3.a.d: यया रज्ज्वोत्तमां गामाजेत्तया भ्रातृव्यगवीमभिदध्याद्गोष्ठे वास्य न्यस्येत्
19.19.3.a.m: With the rope with which he drives the last cow, he should bind the rival's cow, or cast it into his cow-pen.

19.19.4.a.m: He should bind balbaja-grass into the firewood.

19.19.5.a.m: He should sprinkle it together with the firewood.

19.19.6.a.m: With the formula 'O Sarasvatī, having ghee as your share,' the oblation consists of ghee.

19.19.7.a.m: 'Ghee is the sprinkling; with ghee they wipe'—thus all sprinklings and cleansings are done with ghee.

19.19.8.a.m: He should make two verses belonging to Manu the insertion verses.

19.19.8.b.m: Two from among these beginning with 'Quickly for one possessing gods…'

19.19.9.a.m: He should offer this very [sacrifice] having reached the proper ground.

19.19.10.a.m: Having gone to the field of the rival, he should perform this offering.

19.19.11.a.s: tatra dakṣiṇamardhaṃ vedyā uddhatya tadevārdhena barhiṣa stṛṇīyāt /
19.19.11.a.d: तत्र दक्षिणमर्धं वेद्या उद्धत्य तदेवार्धेन बर्हिष स्तृणीयात् ।
19.19.11.a.m: Having raised up the southern half of the altar ground there, he should strew only that with half of the sacrificial grass.

19.19.11.b.m: He should place half of the firewood on [the fire].

19.19.12.a.m: One desirous of a village should offer an eleven-pot-sherd [cake] to Indra and a seven-pot-sherd [cake] to the Maruts.

19.19.13.a.m: He places the one for Indra over the āhavanīya fire.

19.19.14.a.m: At the proper time, he sets down the one for Indra.

19.19.14.b.m: While the kindling verses are being recited, [he sets down] the one for the Maruts.

19.19.15.a.m: Now, where 'Recite for Indra' is the invitatory verse relating to Indra,

19.19.15.b.m: 'Worship the Maruts' is the consecratory verse relating to the Maruts.

19.19.15.c.m: 'Recite for the Maruts' is the invitatory verse relating to the Maruts.

19.19.15.d.m: 'Worship Indra' is the consecratory verse relating to Indra.

19.19.16.a.m: One desirous of a village should offer an eleven-pot-sherd [cake] to Indra and a twelve-pot-sherd [cake] to the All-Gods.

19.19.17.a.m: Having cut the first portion of that for Indra there, he should cut both portions of that for the All-Gods.

19.19.17.b.m: Then, the remaining portion of that for Indra is taken on top.

19.19.18.a.d: इन्द्राय विश्वेभ्यो देवेभ्यो ऽनुब्रूहीन्द्रं विश्वान्देवान्यजेति संप्रेष्यति
19.19.18.a.m: He gives the ritual call: 'Recite for Indra [and] for the All-Gods; worship Indra [and] the All-Gods.'

19.19.19.a.m: [The two verses] beginning with 'Indra in the battles…' serve as the invitatory and consecratory verses.

19.20.1.a.m: A garment with an ornamented upper border is the sacrificial gift.

19.20.3.a.s: saṃjñānīṃ pṛthaṅnirupya sarvataḥ samavadāya sarvā devatā anudrutya saṃpreṣyati
19.20.3.a.d: संज्ञानीं पृथङ्निरुप्य सर्वतः समवदाय सर्वा देवता अनुद्रुत्य संप्रेष्यति
19.20.3.a.m: Having poured out the concord offering separately, having cut portions from all sides, and having recited the names of all the deities in succession, he issues the ritual call.

19.20.4.a.s: agniḥ prathamo vasubhiriti sarvadevatye yājyānumākye bhavataḥ
19.20.4.a.d: अग्निः प्रथमो वसुभिरिति सर्वदेवत्ये याज्यानुमाक्ये भवतः
19.20.4.a.m: [The two verses] beginning with 'Agni first with the Vasus…' serve as the invitatory and consecratory verses addressed to all the deities.

19.20.5.a.s: aparuddho 'prarudhyamāno vā dhārayadvatīyaṃ nirupyāsīta yāvadenaṃ nāparundhyuḥ
19.20.5.a.d: अपरुद्धो ऽप्ररुध्यमानो वा धारयद्वतीयं निरुप्यासीत यावदेनं नापरुन्ध्युः
19.20.5.a.m: One who has been expelled or is being expelled should, having poured out the [oblation] accompanied by the dhārayadvat verses, remain seated as long as they do not banish him.

19.20.6.a.m: Then, while being expelled, he should take the footprint of the expeller with the formula 'O Aditi, agree!' and depart.

19.20.7.a.m: He should bring rice grains from the house of whoever might be a speaker on behalf of the village beyond.

19.20.8.a.m: He should separate the white and the black [grains].

19.20.9.a.m: Those that are white, he should offer as that boiled rice oblation for the Ādityas.

19.20.10.a.s: ye kṛṣṇāstānkṛṣṇājina upanahya nidhāya haviṣkṛtā vācaṃ visṛjyopa preta marutaḥ sudānava iti yajamānamabhyaiti
19.20.10.a.d: ये कृष्णास्तान्कृष्णाजिन उपनह्य निधाय हविष्कृता वाचं विसृज्योप प्रेत मरुतः सुदानव इति यजमानमभ्यैति
19.20.10.a.m: Those that are black, having tied them up in a black antelope skin and set them down, releasing speech with the call to the preparer of the oblation, he approaches the sacrificer with the formula: 'Come forward, O Maruts of generous gifts!'

19.20.11.a.m: With the formula 'True is the blessing…', he scatters a portion of the [dust of the] footprint into the upper garment of the sacrificer.

19.20.12.a.m: With the formula 'Here is the mind…', he pours down the remainder on his chest.

19.20.13.a.m: The offering is completed according to the established rule.

19.20.14.a.s: yadi nāvagacchedimamahamādityebhyo bhāgaṃ nirvapāmyāmuṣmādamuṣyai viśo 'vagantorityaparoddhurnāma gṛhṇīyāttasyai ca viśaḥ
19.20.14.a.d: यदि नावगच्छेदिममहमादित्येभ्यो भागं निर्वपाम्यामुष्मादमुष्यै विशो ऽवगन्तोरित्यपरोद्धुर्नाम गृह्णीयात्तस्यै च विशः
19.20.14.a.m: If he does not return, he should utter the name of the expeller and of that settlement, saying: 'This share I offer to the Ādityas, so that so-and-so may return from such-and-such a settlement.'

19.20.15.a.m: If he does not return, he should drive seven pegs of Aśvattha wood into the middle pole of the chariot, saying: 'Here I bind the Ādityas, so that so-and-so may return from such-and-such a settlement'—

19.20.15.b.m: three pointing eastward and four pointing northward.
